description: Infinity Kingdom Guide: The Complete Golden Path Guide (Updated for Patch 2.8.5)By Myrahk – July 2025
html:
Infinity Kingdom Guide: The Complete Golden Path Guide (Updated for Patch 2.8.5)
By Myrahk – July 2025

Introduction – The Golden Path: Still the Best Deal in Infinity Kingdom

For many Infinity Kingdom players, the Golden Path (often shortened to GP) is the single most important recurring event in the game. It’s not just a battle pass — it’s a core progression system for immortals, artifacts, resources, and even server migration tools.

With the 2.8.5 update, the Golden Path has been reworked. The number of immortal fragments you can purchase each season has been reduced, but in exchange, we’ve gained access to Unique Artifacts for top-tier immortals. This is a huge buff for players aiming to build meta-relevant teams.

In this guide, we’ll break down everything you need to know about the Golden Path:

  • What it is
  • How it works
  • What’s changed in 2.8.5
  • What you should prioritize as a player (whether F2P or spender)
  • Why it’s still the best value in Infinity Kingdom

What Is the Golden Path?

The Golden Path is Infinity Kingdom’s seasonal battle pass, available starting in Season 1 after you progress far enough in your Chronicle. It runs for a set duration (typically around 30 days) and allows players to earn Golden Path Coins by completing quests and leveling up the pass.

These coins can be spent in the Golden Path Shop, which features:

  • Meta immortals & their fragments
  • Unique artifacts (NEW)
  • Castle skins
  • Migration portals
  • Random immortal fragments (for purple crystal farming)
  • Action Point flasks
  • Miscellaneous cosmetics

On top of this, the pass includes tons of direct rewards like gems, speeds, philosopher stones, and random immortal fragments just for leveling up.

The Spender Unlock: Why It’s Worth It

The Golden Path has two tiers:

  • Free tier – Gives some coins, fragments, and basic rewards.
  • Premium tier ($19.99) – Unlocks an extra 20 levels instantly (worth 600 coins or 9,000 gems) and 230 more coins as you progress, plus significant extra rewards.

Total value of the spender tier:

  • ~800 Golden Path Coins (20 levels + tier progression)
  • Immortal fragments
  • Speeds, gold, stones
  • Philosopher stones
  • Random frags for purple crystals

Note: that while the image and tooltip show 200 coins, you in fact earn 200 plus 600 from the 20 additional levels you are getting ahead, since you are going to complete the level 50 multiple times earning coins each time.

Myrahk´s Take: If you spend on anything in Infinity Kingdom, this is where to spend it. For $20, you get one of the highest coin-to-dollar ratios in the game, plus powerful progression items.

Golden Path Shop – What to Buy and Why

The real magic of Golden Path is in the shop, which offers some of the best value purchases in the game. Let’s go through them:

1. Meta Immortals (5×60 Fragments per Season)

Immortals include: Yi Sun-Shin, Louis, Margaret, Seondeok, Artemisia, Pakal, Tokugawa, Matilda, Trajan.

Price: 200 coins per 60 fragments
Limit: 5x purchases per immortal per season (was 10 before patch 2.8.5)

Why it matters:
These are top-tier immortals for key meta teams. Especially:

  • Yi Sun-Shin (YSS) – A core for Earth and Himiko meta builds.
  • Matilda – Crucial for many burst-based setups. E.g. core support for S2 fire builds.
  • Artemisia & Trajan – S-tier supports for multiple water and fire respectively.
  • Tokugawa – Amazing for Lightning sustain.

Player Strategy: Always prioritize immortals you are actively building. Maxing their fragments early means faster access to their talents, which are meta-defining in Conquest.

2. Unique Artifacts (NEW in Patch 2.8.5)

Elemental Selection Unique Artifacts

Cost: 480 coins each.
Limit: 2 per immortal per season

Use them to upgrade your core damage dealer in your main setup max. This is a huge deal, make sure you max out your main damage dealers artifact asap. Keep crafting until you get the right top main stat and bonus. Basically, you should unlock one UA for all immortals you use in combat builds, then forget everyone besides your most important damage dealer, max his or hers artifact.

Pay-wall Immortals Unique Artifacts

Cost: 600 coins each
Limit: 1 per immortal per season

Artifacts for:

Yi Sun-Shin (YSS)
Matilda
Artemisia
Trajan
Tokugawa

Why it matters:
Until now, Unique Artifacts for these immortals were very hard to get. Now, Golden Path provides guaranteed seasonal access.

This is a major buff for players chasing late-game builds. Artifacts like Yi Sun-Shin’s Dragonbane Bow or Trajan’s Imperial Seal can completely change how your team performs.

Player Strategy: If you’re already using one of these immortals on your main team, prioritize their artifact. It’s one of the best long-term investments you can make.

3. Random Immortal Fragments (For Purple Crystals)

Price: 60 coins per 60 fragments
Limit: 5x per element (Fire, Water, Earth, Lightning, Wind)

That’s 1,500 total fragments per season. When melted, they give 150,000 purple crystals — essential for upgrading your Tower of Knowledge skills.

Why it matters:
This is the cheapest and fastest way to farm purple crystals. Even with the stock reduction (10 → 5), this remains the #1 way to fuel ToK growth.

Player Strategy: Always buy these first if your Tower of Knowledge is underdeveloped. Purple crystals are one of the biggest long-term bottlenecks in IK.

4. Portals (Migration Tokens)

Price: 50 coins each
Limit: 10 per season

If you ever plan to migrate servers, buy these every season. They’re cheaper here than anywhere else, and stockpiling them saves a ton of money in the long run.

5. Action Point Flasks

Price: 10 coins each for 1,000 AP
Limit: 10 per season

Always buy them. AP is king for farming gnomes, gathering event points, and prepping for KvK.

6. Castle Skins & Cosmetics

The same as previous Golden Paths — if you’re a collector, this is your spot. Cosmetics don’t impact gameplay, but the castle skins do provide important buffs (check the guides here for full skin breakdowns).

7. Skip These:

  • Stardust – Terrible value.
  • Crimson Crystals – Even worse.

Player Strategy – How to Use Your Coins

For F2P players:

  1. Buy Random Fragments first (for purple crystals).
  2. Buy Action Points.
  3. Save for immortal fragments of a meta immortal you need.

For Light Spenders:

  1. Unlock premium tier for the massive coin boost.
  2. Prioritize immortal fragments and artifacts for your main team.
  3. Stockpile portals in case you need to migrate.

For Whales:

  1. Max out artifacts + immortals every season.
  2. Buy castle skins and cosmetics.
  3. Stockpile portals for server movement flexibility.

TL;DR – The Golden Path in 30 Seconds

  • Cost: $20 for premium tier — best value purchase in the game.
  • New in 2.8.5: Unique Artifacts for meta immortals.
  • Immortal Fragments: Limit reduced to 5x per season, but still top-tier value.
  • Purple Crystals: Buy random fragments (150K per season).
  • Portals & AP: Always stock up.
  • Skip: Stardust and Crimsons — awful value.

Conclusion – Still the Best Deal in Infinity Kingdom

Even with the nerfs to fragment availability, Golden Path remains the best value-for-money feature in Infinity Kingdom.

The addition of Unique Artifacts has transformed it from a “nice-to-have” into an essential seasonal investment for any player serious about long-term progression. Whether you’re building a Conquest-ready main march or just farming purple crystals to expand your Tower of Knowledge, this is where you get the biggest bang for your buck.

If you spend on anything in Infinity Kingdom, make it the Golden Path.

Once you hit castle level 40 and you are in season 2, you unlock the Legendary Battle Pass. This article will give you the details you need to understand and plan how to best take advantage of this pass relative to your goals and objectives.

Legendary Battle Pass is the steady, predictable way to build out Holy and Shadow rosters without relying on lucky pulls. There are two tracks per pass — Silver Medallion (free) and Golden Medallion (paid, $29.99) — and you level them by doing normal daily stuff like hunting gnomes and collecting resources. There will also be special daily quests that relate to current calendar events, like honor for KE days or Rebels killed for Rebel Event days.
A full cycle runs on your server timeline; if you migrate while it’s active, don’t stress — your progress stays. When a pass ends, the next one syncs to the server’s schedule.

How the Two Medallions Work

Silver Medallion (free):

  • Rewards across level 1–100:
    • 60 × Random Immortal Fragments
    • 30 × Random Holy/Shadow Immortal Fragments
    • 10 × 30-min Universal Speedups
    • 5 × 30-min Training Speedups
    • 5 × 30-min Healing Speedups
    • 250,000 of each basic resource (no gold)
  • Good baseline for F2P or alts. The random Holy/Shadow frags are nice trickle progress.

Golden Medallion ($29.99):

  • Additional rewards on top of Silver:
    • 60 × Shadow and Light Selection Chest II
    • 60 × Random Holy/Shadow Immortal Fragments
    • 1,900 Gems
    • 930 Inferno Insignias (the currency you spend in the BP shop)
  • If you’re actively building Holy/Shadow, Golden basically turns steady grind into targeted progress via the shop + selection chests.

Level cap: Silver medallions go up to level 50 and Gold continues rewarding Insignias until 100. You cannot repeat level 100 for additional insignias in the same way as you can repeat the last level of the Golden Pass.

Leveling the Pass (EXP Math You Can Actually Use)

Daily there are 6–7 tasks, each worth 150 pass EXP.

  • Min-case (6 tasks): 900 EXP/day
  • Often (7 tasks): 1,050 EXP/day

Cost per pass level: 250 EXP
Total EXP to max to level 100: 24,750 EXP (that’s 99 level-ups × 250)

28-day season floor math:

  • Min-case missions: 6 × 28 = 168
  • EXP from those: 168 × 150 = 25,200
  • That’s more than enough to hit level 100 without grinding anything extra. You can even miss a few tasks and still cap. Bare in mind, that some days hold 7 daily quests, allowing you to catch up slightly if you missed some tasks during the season.

Skip option: If you fall behind, you can buy levels at 600 Gems per level.

Migration note: Moving servers during the season does not reset your progress.

The Legendary Battle Pass Shop (Holy/Shadow)

This is where the pass really pays out.

  • Inventory: All Holy and Shadow Immortals and their artifacts.
  • Currency: Inferno Insignias (same currency used later in Peak BP; more on that below).
  • Prices & limits:
    • 60 Immortal Fragments = 450 insignias (limit 4 purchases per cycle)
    • Artifact = 600 insignias (limit 2 purchases per cycle)

Quick value gut-check: The Golden track gives 930 insignias, which is worth just over two 60-frag packs (930 ÷ 450 ≈ 2.06 → ~124 frags), or 1 artifact + leftover. Combine this with the selection chests and you can make a noticeable dent in a Holy/Shadow project every season.

Tip: If you are close to castle level 50. You need to know that the currency Insignias are used in both the Legendary and the Peak Battle Pass where you can redeem for Chaos immortals and artifacts. Read below.

Peak Battle Pass (Heads-Up for Castle 50+)

Once you hit Castle level 50, there’s also the Peak Battle Pass (separate guide here), focused on Chaos immortals and artifacts.
The important thing here: both passes use the same insignia currency. That means you can bank insignias across seasons and spend them in either shop.

So what should you do?

  • Below C50 and far from it: It’s totally fine to spend on Holy/Shadow now — you’ll feel the power spike earlier. Not all players have the spending level required to ever complete Chaos Immortals with artifacts and talents requireing a lot of investment. If that is you, going for key shadow or holy immortals and artifacts is perfectly valid!
  • Close to C50 or planning Chaos soon: Consider banking insignias so that, when Peak BP unlocks, you can grab Chaos fragments/artifacts. It’s a long grind if you’re going pure Battle Pass, but banking makes the first Peak cycle hit way harder. If you do go for Chaos Immortals remember you need 4750 immortal fragments to upgrade talents after completing the star ranks. More on that here.
  • If you plan to spend real money specifically for Chaos, banking before C50 is usually the smarter play.

Conclusion Summary

  • Two tracks: Silver (free) and Golden ($29.99).
  • Leveling is easy: 6–7 × 150 EXP dailies; you need 24,750 EXP total; 28 days at minimum tasks is 25,200 EXP, so you can cap without sweat.
  • Rewards worth noting: Golden adds 1,900 Gems, 930 insignias, 60 Selection Chest II, and 60 random Holy/Shadow frags.
  • Shop: 450 insignias = 60 frags (limit 4), 600 insignias = 1 artifact (limit 2). Plan purchases ahead.
  • Think ahead: Same insignia currency is used in Peak BP (C50+ Chaos). If Chaos is your endgame, bank now and cash out later.

Bottom line: If you’re actively building Holy or Shadow or Chaos later, Golden Medallion is a good value. If Chaos is your target and C50 is close, bank the insignias and go big when Peak unlocks.

html:
The Peak Battle Pass is the late‑game, Chaos‑focused pass in Infinity Kingdom. It unlocks at Castle level 50 (this is your Season 2 pass) and rotates roughly once a month for 28 days. The whole idea is simple: if you’re planning to build Chaos immortals and their Exclusive Artifacts, this is where the best recurring value lives.

There’s also a Legendary Battle Pass running alongside it; both feeds the same currency, so you can plan out long‑term Chaos purchases without wasting tokens. Read more about the Legendary Battle Pass here.

How It Works

  • Availability: Unlocks at C50 (Season 2).
  • Duration: Each run lasts 28 days.
  • Tiers: Two tracks per run.
    • Silver Medallion: Free.
    • Golden Medallion: Paid ($49.99).
  • Currency: Both Peak and Legendary passes award Inferno Insignias. You can spend them in either shop, which is huge for planning.

Daily Tasks & Leveling

  • You’ll see 6 or 7 daily tasks (depends on the day), each worth 150 Pass EXP.
  • Each Battle Pass level needs 250 EXP.
  • To hit Level 100, you need 24,750 EXP in total.
  • Over 28 days you get at least 168 tasks (6 × 28), which equals 25,200 EXP. That’s more than enough to cap the pass without buying levels.
  • You can also skip and buy levels at 750 Gems per level if you’re short.

Rewards Overview

Silver Medallion (Free Track)

  • 120 Random Immortal Fragments
  • 30 Random Holy/Shadow Immortal Fragments
  • 10 × 60‑min universal speedups
  • 5 × 60‑min training speedups
  • 5 × 60‑min healing speedups
  • 500,000 of each resource (except gold)

Golden Medallion (Paid, $49.99)

  • 80 Fate of Chaos Selection Chest II (contains fragments for all current Chaos immortals except Ares and Apollo)
  • 6,000 Gems
  • 1,674 Inferno Insignias

Note: The exact behavior of Fate of Chaos Selection Chest II follows the “select from pool” logic and does not include Ares and Apollo.

Peak Battle Pass Shop

  • The shop includes all current Chaos Immortals except Ares and Apollo, plus their Exclusive Artifacts.
  • Costs & Limits:
    • Chaos Immortal Fragments: 80‑fragment bundle costs 800 Inferno Insignias (limit 4 per immortal per run).
    • Chaos Exclusive Artifact: costs 1,200 Inferno Insignias (limit 2 per run).

Important Season 2 Note: In the current version, the shop also lacks Fu Fei. This is not intended and will be fixed in the next rotation. If Fu Fei is your planned first Chaos immortal, bank your insignias now and buy her next season when she appears.

Legendary Battle Pass (Context)

If you have Peak unlocked, you’ll also see a Legendary Battle Pass. It also contributes Inferno Insignias and focuses on Chaos immortals/artifacts. Because both passes award the same currency, you can push both to funnel insignias into one shop plan.

  • Cost Together: Doing both (Legendary + Peak) runs you about $80 total.
  • Insignia Total: If you cap both passes to Level 100, you’ll get 2,604 Inferno Insignias in total.

Planning tip: If you’re under C50 and not close, you can stack insignias across seasons via the Legendary pass and spend later in the Peak shop once you hit C50.

Value Check (Why this matters)

  • With 2,604 insignias (both passes maxed), you can target Chaos fragments or Artifacts directly in the Peak Shop.
  • Example plan people like: Put insignias into Chaos Immortal Fragments. At 800 insignias for 80 fragments, pure math says 240 fragments should cost 2,400 insignias (3 × 800). That’s a clean pickup and leaves a small buffer for next run.
  • For comparison, 500 Eye of Chaos typically gets ~200–250 fragments and costs more than $80, so the passes are generally better value if your goal is specific Chaos progress.

Strategy: What I’d Actually Do

If you’re aiming at Chaos, here’s the practical flow I recommend after testing this across a couple rotations:

  1. Bank Insignias if your target isn’t in shop. With the Fu Fei situation (Season 2 missing in UI), don’t panic spend. Wait a rotation and buy exactly what you want.
  2. Secure your first chaos. Getting your first main Chaos immortal to usable stars is the biggest spike. Usually that’s Apollo long‑term, but he is not in this shop, so plan a different main chaos like e.g., Fu Fei (when available) and build around it.
  3. If you’re below C50, use Legendary pass to stockpile insignias. Don’t force Shadow/Holy unless they’re part of your end‑game plan. It’s totally fine to sit on currency and power‑spike at C50.
  4. Don’t overbuy in one run. There are purchase limits (4 × 80‑frag bundles per immortal, 2 artifacts). If you can’t finish a purchase this season, carry insignias over – they do not disapear.

Quick Summary

  • Unlocks at C50/Season 2, runs 28 days.
  • Silver (free) gives mixed frags, speedups, and resources.
  • Gold ($49.99) gives 80 Fate of Chaos II chests (excludes Ares/Apollo), 6,000 Gems, 1,674 insignias.
  • Shop: 800 insignias → 80 Chaos frags (limit 4 per immortal); 1,200 insignias → Artifact (limit 2).
  • Maxing both Legendary + Peak ≈ $80 total → 2,604 insignias.
  • Best baseline buy: Fragments. Once stars are done get one Artifact to unlock unique effect then continue to build talents with immortal fragments.
  • If your target is missing (e.g., Fu Fei this Season 2), bank insignias and buy next rotation.

Bottom line: If Chaos is your endgame, the Peak + Legendary passes are the most controlled and cost‑efficient way to progress—just be patient and buy the right things at the right time. But you should expect to supplement the battle passes with Chaos Eyes and the Roulette event, since you need 1640 immortal fragments to star and unlock artifact slot plus 4750 in total to fully complete the talents. It is perfectly fine to not have chaos within your budget and thus spend the Insignias in the Legenday Pass to complete holy or shadow immortals. Only you can make that decision, just think long term and be realistic about your budget for Infinity Kingdom.

html:
Table of content:
– Training Grounds

– Upgrade Costs of Training Grounds & Walls

Training Grounds

The Training Grounds is where you can check your army status like total number of available troops, troops that are already deployed, the number of wounded troops, etc. The higher the level of your Training Grounds, the more troops you can have. You cannot build a real army without upgrading your Training Grounds.

Walls

The Walls is what protects your Castle city from harm. When you are attacked by enemies you can place armies at your walls to garrison your city. You can also assist fellow alliance teamplayers by sending garrisons to their walls at a time of need. The high the level of your Walls the more durability they have. If an attacker defeats all garrisoned armies on the walls, they also need to defeat the walls themselves. I.e. killing the durability of your wall whilst they take damage from all of your fortifications. You can train fortifications at the walls.

The last line of defense

Upgrading your castle level requires specific buildings to have been constructed first. You can find my comprehensive list of all requirements for each castle level here.

Every Castle level requires you to have upgraded your walls and for walls your training grounds. Hence these two always go hand in hand and you need to upgrade both continually to unlock new Castle levels. See Upgrade Costs of Castle levels here.

title: New Technology in patch 2.6
description: New Technology Additions in Update 2.6 – A Comprehensive Guide
html:
New Technology Additions in Update 2.6 – A Comprehensive Guide

Update 2.6 in Infinity Kingdom brings exciting new technology additions, including Troop tech and Immortal tech. While the Troop technology upgrades may have fallen short of expectations, the Immortal tech introduces compelling enhancements. This guide explores the new technologies, highlighting their effects and potential impact on gameplay.

Troop Technology: The Troop technology additions primarily focus on reducing troop losses in battles. Although these upgrades may appear lackluster, they play a significant role in preserving troops during combat. The reductions in “troop deaths” directly translate to fewer losses on the battlefield.

The Troop technology were kind of a let down. These are reductions of “troop deaths” which essentially just reduces the amount of troops you loose in battle. A boring upgrade for something we have been waiting so long for if you ask me. However, we are getting new and interesting technology for Immortals. These are getting first “Defense Stance” which gives a massive total of 10% reduction to critical hit damage taken. Very very very good. Furthermore, the last nodes in the new Immortal technology tree are all very very good too.

Immortal Technology

The Immortal technology upgrades, on the other hand, bring more exciting and impactful enhancements. Let’s delve into the specific upgrades and their effects:

Defense Stance (All Immortals): The Defense Stance upgrade provides a substantial 10% reduction in critical hit damage taken by Immortals. This defensive boost significantly improves their survivability, making Immortals more resilient on the battlefield. This upgrade is highly valuable and contributes to the overall effectiveness of Immortal-based armies.

Bowmen: Bowmen’s normal attacks now have a chance to reduce a proportion of the target’s Magical Defense for 3 seconds. This upgrade empowers Bowmen by weakening the magical defenses of their targets, making them more vulnerable to magical damage. This enhancement promotes the rise of endgame magic setups, potentially challenging the dominance of physical setups in the new max level meta.

Shieldmen: Shieldmen Immortals receive a significant buff, as they now have a chance to protect the front row from normal attacks. This enhancement provides a powerful defense against normal attacks, making Shieldmen an effective choice for countering hybrid marches. While it indirectly nerfs hybrid setups, it greatly strengthens Shieldmen’s role in specific battle scenarios.

Cavalry: Cavalry’s normal attacks gain a chance to reduce a proportion of the target’s Physical Defense for 3 seconds. This upgrade marks a massive buff for Cavalry, particularly in the physical damage meta. With this enhancement, Cavalry becomes more formidable, allowing for greater impact and effectiveness on the battlefield. It has the potential to reshape the strategic landscape of max level gameplay.

Spearmen: Spearmen Immortals now have a chance to recover some HP when dealing normal attacks. While the Spearmen upgrade offers a minor benefit of HP recovery, its impact may be limited in practical use. The healing effect from normal attacks may not significantly impact battle outcomes unless utilized in a specific spear setup that benefits greatly from leeching.

Conclusion: The new technology additions in Update 2.6 bring both underwhelming and exciting upgrades. The Immortal technology introduces game-changing enhancements. Notably, the Defense Stance, along with the upgrades for Bowmen, Shieldmen, and Cavalry, offers powerful advantages in combat. These upgrades have the potential to reshape the meta and diversify strategic options in the game.

Prepare to adapt your army compositions and battle strategies as you explore the new technologies and harness their potential in Infinity Kingdom. May these upgrades lead you to triumph in the ever-evolving world of warfare!

title: Technology Research in Infinity Kingdom
description: Technology in Infinity Kingdom – An Overview
html:
Technology in Infinity Kingdom – An Overview

Technology is the backbone of long-term growth in Infinity Kingdom. While your marches, dragons, and immortals often steal the spotlight, your real ceiling of power is determined by how far your technology research has gone. Every upgrade in the Academy directly influences your efficiency, your strength in battle, and how quickly you can progress through each season.

In this article we are going to be going through each of the four different technology trees, meaning the four different types of technology research you will find inside your Academy. It is important to note, that the way you should progress this technology depends on your activity level, how much you spend and have access to speedups and on your access to resources. I will include small tips and tricks as to how to best prioritize as you grow, but in general this will be an overview and introduction to the way technology works in Infinity Kingdom for newer players. If you are looking only for information on the best progression paths, see my other guide under castle > technology.

How Technology Progression Works

Technology research happens in the Academy. To unlock deeper and stronger nodes in the tech trees, you first need to:

  • Upgrade prerequisite nodes: Most new nodes require prior technologies to reach a certain level before they unlock.
  • Upgrade your Academy level: Each time your Academy levels up, new parts of the technology trees become available. Once unlocked you can progress the tree but remember you will need the prerequisite nodes also.
  • Prioritize Technology as you grow: The Tech Trees are quite long and it will take you FAR longer to finish upgrading your technology than your buildings and dragons. Therefore, technology is where the smart player invests resources and speedups to get ahead. You will have downtime on e.g. builders as you wait for a new seasonal limit increase on buildings, but your technology is not going to be complete until you are far into conquest.

Research consumes resources and speedups to rapid finish, so pacing your Academy levels with your resource generation is key. Even whales can get stuck if they over-invest without balancing speedups and resources.

The Four Technology Trees

There are four distinct technology trees in Infinity Kingdom. Each serves a different purpose, and knowing their role helps you decide what to prioritize at different stages of the game.

1. Production

The Production tree is all about growth and economy. It boosts resource generation, building speed, carry load, and other efficiency-related stats.

  • What it’s good for: Rushing early building upgrades (Speedy Construction), sustaining your gold economy (Gold Piles), and cheaper research (Rapid Progress).
  • When to focus: Early game quickly pick up construction, get some gold boost (important) and a bit of tech research boost (5-7/10 ish depending on spending level. The more you spend and earn speedups the more you will be bottlenecked on resources and not speeds. If you are F2P you may want to push development further, but ultimately that depends on your ability to quickly and consistently farm resources).
  • Later this tree is not as impactful as combat trees, but essential for faster overall progression and thus very good to get early on. Note that you will be bottlenecked for gold shortly but in season 2 it becomes much more readily available as you can push Infernals with your alliance.

2. Troops

The Troop tree powers up your actual soldiers: cavalry, shieldmen, bowmen, and spearmen.

  • What it’s good for: Straight combat strength. Attack, defense and the powerful “major node” upgrades like Great Vigor and Sturdy Build in the first major row and Double Shot and Shield Block. These are very powerful and ones you want to push for as milestones.
  • When to focus: Season 1 especially, since these upgrades give your marches a huge immediate impact in PvP and PvE. In season 1 Troop Technology is the most value for your armies. You are going to want to dip into the Immortal tree but then you want to go max the Troop tree before the end of season 1 if possible (see below for details). The efficiency dips in Season 2 simply because the new nodes unlocked on the trees are better in Immortal than the new ones added to Troop tech.

3. Immortals

The Immortal tree enhances your Immortals directly. This is perhaps a bit wierd to understand, since we are fighting with Troops and Immortals automatically. But the way it works is, that modifiers can apply to troops or immortals, both have their own attribute modifiers. Immortal ultimate skills and ToK skill output scales off of troop stats/attributes and Immortal stats/attributes.

  • What it’s good for: Quickly (in season 1 before you finish Troop) dive in for Gold efficiency (Boost Consumption), faster ultimate skill charging (Outstanding Talent), and, after finishing Troop tech and in later seasons, collect the massive troop count increases.
  • When to focus: Modest upgrades in Season 1, then a top priority in Season 2 once troop count nodes unlock. These nodes are some of the most powerful in the entire game.

4. Defense

The Defense tree strengthens your city walls and fortifications.

  • What it’s good for: Defensive bonuses like Iron Body (pretty much the only worth while tech node and hidden way too deep) and stronger fortifications.
  • When to focus: Honestly, this is the lowest-priority tree for most players. It only really matters if you’re a heavy city defender or a completionist. For raw power and march strength, the other three trees outclass it by far.

Closing Thoughts

Technology is less flashy than pulling a new immortal or leveling a dragon, but it’s the steady engine behind everything you do. Without it, your marches plateau early, and your economy struggles to keep up. The key is pacing: match your Academy level ups with your seasonal goals, and don’t spread too thin across all trees at once.

In conclusion, technology research is crucial in Infinity Kingdom, and players who neglect it will find it challenging to succeed in the game. The four types of technology research available in the game are development, troops, immortals, and defense. Each type of technology research is essential and plays a unique role in a player’s success in the game. Technology research is one of the most important aspects of the game and is vital to growth and player power.

Bottom line: Do not underestimate technology, this should be your main priority as you grow and progress in Infinity Kingdom.

description: Welcome to this comprehensive guide on the reworked harbour system in your game! html:
Welcome to this comprehensive guide on the reworked harbour system in your game! Over the past month and a half, with help from the community (huge thanks to Magic Mage for his contributions), we’ve gathered and organized key information to help you maximize your harbour’s potential. Let’s dive in!

Harbour 101: Understanding the Basics

Continuous Sailing

  • Continuous Exploration: Unlike the previous long voyages, ships now sail continuously, collecting rewards and EXP along the way.
  • EXP and Leveling: As your ship earns experience points, its level increases, improving both the quality and quantity of rewards.

Dispatching Immortals

  • Crew Assignment: Immortals assigned to the ship’s crew are unavailable for marches but can still participate in Arena and Throne activities.
  • Rotating Immortal Compositions: Periodically, specific immortals offer bonus rewards when dispatched. Rotate your crew to include these bonus immortals and maximize your rewards.

Weather Conditions

  • Impact on Rewards: Weather changes can influence reward probabilities:
    • Sunny: +5% bonus to other rewards.
    • Overcast: No effect.
    • Downpour: -2% penalty.
    • Windy: -3% penalty.

Strategies for Optimizing Rewards

Utilizing Bonus Immortals

  • Bonus Rewards: Deploy immortals that offer bonuses to significantly enhance your chances of obtaining rare items.
  • Regular Updates: Check for updates on bonus immortals and adjust your crew frequently to ensure you’re capitalizing on these opportunities.

Immortal Levels and Star Ratings

  • Reward Boosts: The level and star rating of your crew directly influence reward probabilities:
    • Basic Threshold: Five immortals at minimum level 1 and star level 1 for a 3% bonus.
    • Higher Thresholds: Bonuses increase as more and stronger immortals are assigned, up to a maximum of 25% with 16 immortals at level 60 and star level 8.

Ship Leveling and Crew Slots

Expanding Crew Capacity

  • As your ship levels up, additional crew slots unlock:
    • Level 10: 6 slots
    • Level 15: 7 slots
    • Continues in increments of 5 levels for each additional slot.

Maintaining Crew Quality

  • Ensure all assigned crew members meet or exceed the minimum level and star requirements corresponding to your ship’s level for maximum bonuses.

Rewards and Progression

Now to the more important bits, the rewards! This is where the information I mentioned, which was provided by Magic Mage, comes in handy. He has been collecting information about the rewards for a long time and we can now share up to level 52 rewards and unvail the fact that shadow, holy and even chaos immortal fragments are to be earned at quite frequent rates! This is a huge deal and massive thing for all but the biggest of whales. This means, that spender who are spending a lot but perhaps not enough to unlock all chaos spending 40K USD on immortals, can grind it out and still get those juicy immortals. Very nice!

Credit to Magic Mage for this information. Thank you to him for his work and make sure to check out his guides on the Gtarcade Forum.

Early Rewards

  • Initial ship levels yield:
    • Speedups
    • Gold
    • Resources
    • Random Immortal Fragments (summons an Epic immortal of a random element).

Progressive Enhancement

  • As the ship levels up, rewards improve significantly. At higher levels, you’ll begin earning rare fragments like Shadow, Holy, and Chaos Immortal shards more frequently.
  • Key Highlight: From level 51 onwards, ships start earning Chaos Immortal shards at the rate of 1 shard per sailing. This means you can expect to collect a full Chaos Immortal in approximately 80 days of continuous sailing. Rewards are expected to improve further as you climb beyond level 52.

Summary and Key Takeaways

  • Assign and rotate your crew strategically to optimize bonuses.
  • Regularly monitor for updates to bonus immortal rotations.
  • Level up both your ship and crew to unlock higher rewards and more slots.
  • Take advantage of weather conditions and plan your sails accordingly.

With careful planning and continuous improvement, even non-spenders can achieve significant progress and unlock valuable rewards. Thanks again to Magic Mage and the community for their contributions to this guide. Happy sailing!

title: Introduction and Tips for the Harbour
description: With the release of patch 2.6.8, Infinity Kingdom introduced a revamped Harbour feature, transforming it into a continuous exploration activity where players dispatch immortals on their ship to gather resources and experience. This guide delves into the mechanics of the new Harbour, offering strateg
html:
With the release of patch 2.6.8, Infinity Kingdom introduced a revamped Harbour feature, transforming it into a continuous exploration activity where players dispatch immortals on their ship to gather resources and experience. This guide delves into the mechanics of the new Harbour, offering strategies to optimize your rewards. This guide is a beginners guide to understanding the Harbour. I will include some recommendations with what I am doing as a player in Preperation stage on the verge of entering season 1 queueing. As such, this guide is most relevant for newer players who want to understand how it works as well as for players that are looking for quick tips on how to manage their Harbour.

Basics at the Harbour Mechanics

Continuous Sailing

  • Continuous Exploration: Unlike the previous long voyages, the new system allows the ship to continuously sail, collecting rewards and EXP.
  • EXP and Leveling: Experience points increase your ship’s level, which in turn enhances the quality and quantity of rewards.

Dispatching Immortals

  • Crew Assignment: Immortals assigned to the ship’s crew cannot participate in marches but remain available for Arena and Throne activities.
  • Rotating Immortal Compositions: Periodically, certain immortals will offer bonus rewards when dispatched. It’s crucial to rotate your crew according to these bonuses to maximize gains.

Weather Conditions

  • Impact on Rewards: Weather changes can affect the reward probability:
    • Sunny: +5% other rewards
    • Overcast: No change
    • Downpour: -2%
    • Windy: -3%

Strategies for Optimizing Rewards

Utilizing Bonus Immortals

  • Bonus Rewards: Deploying bonus immortals can significantly increase the likelihood of obtaining rare and other rewards.
  • Regular Checks: Always check for updates on the bonus immortals and adjust your crew accordingly to ensure you are receiving the optimal bonuses.

Immortal Levels and Star Ratings

  • Reward Boosts Based on Crew Quality: The level and star rating of your immortals can improve your drop rates:
    • Basic threshold: 5 immortals at minimum level 1 and star level 1 for a 3% bonus.
    • Higher thresholds: Increase in increments as your ship levels up and allows more immortals on board, with the highest being 16 immortals at level 60 and star level 8 for a 25% bonus.

Thresholds (bonus applies to both rare and other):
3% bonus: 5 Epic immortals at min. level 1, tier level 0 and at star level 0.
5% bonus: 6 Epic immortals at min. level 10, tier level 0 and at star level 0.
7% bonus: 7 Epic immortals at min. level 15, tier level 0 and at star level 0.
9% bonus: 8 Epic immortals at min. level 20, tier level 0 and at star level 1.
11% bonus: 9 Epic immortals at min. level 25, tier level 5 and at star level 2.
13% bonus: 10 Epic immortals at min. level 30, tier level 8 and at star level 3.
15% bonus: 11 Epic immortals at min. level 35, tier level 10 and at star level 4.
17% bonus: 12 Epic immortals at min. level 40, tier level 15 and at star level 5.
19% bonus: 13 Epic immortals at min. level 45, tier level 18 and at star level 6.
21% bonus: 14 Epic immortals at min. level 50, tier level 20 and at star level 7.
23% bonus: 15 Epic immortals at min. level 55, tier level 25 and at star level 7.
25% bonus: 16 Epic immortals at min. level 60, tier level 30 and at star level 7.

Needless to say, reaching the higher levels of bonuses requires a massive investment in terms of EXP, Gold and Immortal Fragments (that could have been Purple Crystals). As such, only in late conquest should anyone get anywhere close to reaching the higher end of these bonuses.

Preperation Stage Servers: In a preperation stage server, you will not have anything to spare. Everything you have should be used to max out your main and the little you spare goes into a secondary team once season 2 of arena comes out and in time to have something to use for season 1 of Legion of Frostborne in the secondary slot. This means you want to aim for a % bonus that is easily doable with minimal investment.

My personal favorite level is around 7% or 9%. This is because it requires relatively little EXP, getting level 15 or 20 is quite easily doable. Moreover, you do not have to invest any gold what so ever into tier levels and 7% requires no immortal fragments made into Star levels and 9% requires just a single star (30 fragments).

Season 1-2 ish an onwards: Once you progress into the next seasons with your server, resources quickly become more abundant. Therefore, you should begin moving a bit up the ladder on the bonus chart. I would aim for the 11% or 13% bonus by then, simply because they are not getting into the super Gold expensive tiers in terms of Tier Levels yet. You will need a bit of Fragments for this, but with the new Golden Path and having progressed beyond C40 at this stage, you should be able to collect enough. If you are strained for crystals for your ToK skills on your main and secondary team, stay at 7-9%.

As you progress into later seasons and eventually Conquest, you should be starting to stockpile EXP and Immortal Fragments are still abundance, hence you are able to move further if you want to. Gold may still be a strain, but if you do Infernal events correctly you should have plenty of that in the end on Conquest servers. Hence you can progress onto the later levels.

Is it worth the investment though? I would say so. As you upgrade your Harbour level past level 40 you begin to collect Shadow Immortal Fragments. Past level 45 you begin to collect Holy Immortal Fragments and after level 50 you even collect Chaos Immortal Fragments at a quite decent rate! That means that adding a few % bonus can yield a quite significant payout for end-game players and save you a lot of real money as you progress into Holy or even Chaos!

Rewards and Progression

  • Early Rewards: Initial levels yield speedups, gold, resources, and Random Immortal Fragments, which summon an Epic immortal of a random element.
  • Progressive Enhancement: Rewards improve as the ship levels up, emphasizing the importance of continuously upgrading and managing your crew effectively.

Conclusion

The new Harbour feature in Infinity Kingdom offers a dynamic way to engage with the game, providing continuous rewards while demanding strategic management of your crew and their assignments. By effectively utilizing the rotating immortal bonuses, adapting to weather conditions, and strategically leveling your ship and crew, you can maximize your gains from this feature. Stay tuned for future updates as more insights become available on later-tier rewards. Keep your crew prepared and ready to set sail on profitable adventures in the ever-expanding seas of Norheim!

title: Abyssal Temple (Midsummer Festival 2025)
description: The Midsummer Festival 2025 introduces the Abyssal Temple castle skin—a sleek Poseidon-themed design with real combat impact. What sets it apart is its fresh stat boost: Troop Attack rather than Immortal Attack. That shift may seem subtle but it reshapes the value hierarchy of all combat skins.
html:
The Midsummer Festival 2025 introduces the Abyssal Temple castle skin—a sleek Poseidon-themed design with real combat impact. What sets it apart is its fresh stat boost: Troop Attack rather than Immortal Attack. That shift may seem subtle but it reshapes the value hierarchy of all combat skins.

Why Troop Attack Takes the Crown

Infinity Kingdom recently spotlighted how troop attributes scale massively better than Immortal attributes: each point of troop attack is amplified by troop count, whereas Immortal stats apply once per hero. If you lead 60,000 troops, a 1% Troop Attack buff hits every one of them for an exponential output boost—compared to a single Immortal punch from an Immortal Attack buff.

Put simply: with more troops comes more multiplied value. The Abyssal Temple’s Troop Attack buff transfers power to your army’s very foundation, not just your heroes. That makes it the most impactful combat skin in history.

🛡️ Comparing Combat Skins

Infinity Kingdom combat skins fall into two camps: Immortal Attack-based and Troop-based boosts.

Immortal-Attack Skins (e.g., Skyriver Palace)

  • Effect: +% boost to Immortal Attack.
  • Value: Great for raw hero damage—but scales poorly with troop mass. Best early game or low-troop setups.

Troop Attack Skin (Abyssal Temple)

  • Effect: +Troop Attack %, scaling across every unit you lead.
  • Value: Far superior on heavy-march accounts. As your army grows, its bonus multiplies exponentially.

Hybrid Skins (e.g., Mt. Paradise)

  • Mixed buffs: Some balance combat and utility (health, speed).
  • Value: Good if you’re balancing PvE efficiency with PvP performance, but lack raw punch.

📊 The verdict: To dominate Conquest-level marching, nothing beats Abyssal Temple for sheer damage scaling.

🎯 Acquisition & Upgrades

You can get the Abyssal Temple skin exclusively via the Celebration Pass in the Midsummer Festival (July 11–20).

  • Base unlock: Premium Pass (~$49.99) grants the skin at level 1: +5% Troop Attack, –3% Death Rate.
  • Upgrade path: Level up to 10 (using duplicates from Treasure Hunter rewards), increasing stats to +15% Troop Attack, –6% Death Rate.
  • Leaderboard scope: Only top ranks earn fragments, making higher levels whale-friendly—but level 1 is strong enough for most.

📏 Strategic Considerations

  • Light Spend:
    Grab level 1. A permanent Troop Attack boost is valuable forever. You may skip further upgrades to conserve resources.
  • Heavy or Whale Players:
    Push for upgrades. Every percent of Troop Attack and Death Rate reduction amplifies massive troop numbers—maxing the skin is a serious advantage.
  • Early Game Users:
    Focus on leveling troops and your Immortal lineup; the skin’s value will grow with your march size.

OBS: Expect new skins to come out being better than this skin! There is a pretty clear pattern at this point, through the four years of this game, we have seen consistently new skins being released one more powerful than the last. So expect the next one to be slightly more powerful 😉

🧠 Why It Matters

From our guide on troop vs. Immortal attributes, investing in troop stats is an investment in scale—and the Abyssal Temple is the first skin designed to fully embrace that principle. By offering troop-centric combat buffs, IK is catering to the evolving meta, where mass marches and grand battles define Conquest—and where scale wins.

TL;DR

  • Abyssal Temple offers +Troop Attack (level 1) and extra Death Rate reduction at higher levels—no other skin delivers that.
  • Troop Attack scales dramatically stronger than Immortal Attack once you march tens of thousands of units.
  • Level 1 is solid for all; full investment is reserved for whales seeking dominance.
  • To obtain: get the Premium Celebration Pass, then chase Treasure Hunter leaderboard rewards.

Final Word: With troop count now king, Abyssal Temple shifts the balance—it’s not just a skin, it’s a statement on where IK’s future power lies. If you’re building your march for late-game supremacy, this castle conversion is unmissable.

description: Infinity Kingdom has a ton of cool city skins. Castle Skins serve two purposes: (1) they provide unique buff effects to specifi
html:
Infinity Kingdom has a ton of cool city skins. You get skins from purchases during events, performance from in game activities such as contention of relics and/or Legion of Frostborne, Throne of the Supreeme, and so on. Castle Skins serve two purposes: (1) they provide unique buff effects to specific activities such as e.g. tech speed, dragon speed, combat buffs, recovery speed, resource collection rate, etc. and (2) they provide unique cosmetic effects that change the way your castle looks inside the game. The cosmetic effects work in all aspects of the game, any game mode, and provides some awesome customization to make youself more unique and your castle look.. well.. more awesome!

In this article we shall look to one of my personal favorite cosmetic skins in all of Infinity Kingdom: Ancient Tribe

What does Ancient Tribe do?

Every castle skin has unique beneficial effects, from building speed to rss gathering and troop HP. The Ancient Tribe provides you a 3% increase to your Action Point recovery rate. AP is the most limited resource we have in Infinity Kingdom and as such having more AP simple mean you can do more things throughout your day in Infinity Kingdom!

That being said, this skin is not one of the “best” skins purely based on it’s effect. 3% increased AP means that while you would normally regen 1 AP every 30 seconds. Translating into 120 AP / hour or 2880 AP per day without the skin effect active. With the skin you instead regen 123.6 AP / hour with the skin on a daily total of 2966.4 and thus only a 86.4 AP more with the skin active.

86 AP is not a lot, translates into roughly a single action more per day, which is very neglectable and not really worth using this skin when you compare it to the effects offered by other castle skins. However, this skin is still one of my favorites simple because the look and feel of it is awesome!

How to get it?

There is only one way to obtain this skin: (1) Hunting Festival and (2) Golden Path seasonal shop

This skin was first released with the very first version of the Hunting Festival which occur every May in Infinity Kingdom. During this seasonal event, players have been able to complete quests and practice with your bow and arrow to become Legendary Hunter and earn the Tribe Casle Skin. You should beware that these seasonal events tends to change every year, and as such I cannot give any guarantees as to how or if you will be able to collect this skin from the seasonal even when May comes around again.

However, lucky for you guys there is a place where you can be sure to collect this skin – in the Golden Path seasonal shop!

Golden Path

Ancient Tribe can be found in the last and first rotation of the Golden Path shop. You will be able to find it there somewhere around the december-february timeframe (changes slightly ever year and based on server).

This skin is available in the golden path rotation! Check out my article here to read more about the Castle skins offered via Golden Path as well as the full rotation.

html:
Infinity Kingdom has a ton of cool city skins. You get skins from purchases during events, performance from in game activities such as contention of relics and/or Legion of Frostborne, Throne of the Supreeme, and so on.

Castle Skins serve two purposes: (1) they provide unique buff effects to specific activities such as e.g. tech speed, dragon speed, combat buffs, recovery speed, resource collection rate, etc. and (2) they provide unique cosmetic effects that change the way your castle looks inside the game. The cosmetic effects work in all aspects of the game, any game mode, and provides some awesome customization to make youself more unique and your castle look.. well.. more awesome!

In this article we shall look to one of my personal favorite cosmetic skins in all of Infinity Kingdom: Bon Voyage

What does Bon Voyage do?

Every castle skin has unique beneficial effects, from building speed to rss gathering and troop HP. The Harvest Song provides you a 3% increase to your honor gain. This is a massive buff that makes it arguable one of the most sought after castle skins in all of Infinity Kingdom. The effect is very simple, you just get more honor from killing the same amount of enemy troops.

For example, killing 100,000 worth of enemy troops will net you an added 3K honor – not a lot you say? Well for thoes who are stacking alts and using the Personal Talent Point skill “Rank Advancement” an added 3% provides a lot of value!

For example, in this image we are getting 278K honor per attack using the rank advancement talent. For this single hit alone, our Bon Voyage castle skin provides us 8K additional honor without loosing any more troops on our alts! That is quite a good chunck of honor and certainly something that stacks up when you are competing for a Kill Event or for Nobility Rankings.

If you can do around 1 million honor per day (which is doable if you run alts well) then you earn a daily 30,000 honor for free! Not bad for basically no effort!

All in all, a nice and powerful effect and one I recommend you to go after if you are looking to make a lot of honor consistently. It also have the added bonus of being a pretty cool look for you as you fly around killing people and looks even better when you are ratting 😉

Honor Boost

description: Infinity Kingdom has a ton of cool city skins. You get skins from purchases during events, performance from in game activities such as contention of relics and/or Legion of Frostborne, Throne of the Supreeme, and so on.
html:
Infinity Kingdom has a ton of cool city skins. You get skins from purchases during events, performance from in game activities such as contention of relics and/or Legion of Frostborne, Throne of the Supreeme, and so on.

In this article we shall look to one of the coolest and most sought after skins of Infinity Kingdom: Dark Fortress

What does Dark Fortress Sovereign do?

Every castle skin has unique beneficial effects, from building speed to rss gathering and troop HP. The Dark Fortress castle skin provides a 5% boost to Dragon Upgrade Speed and 5% Gold Production Speed of Dwellings. This is an amazing castle skin effect and one that makes this skin the third best skin effect of all skins in my opinion. As you are growing and developing your marches your dragon is one of the few things in Infinity Kingdom that truely takes an extreem amounts of time. Getting three dragons to level 50 requires an incredible amount of speed ups and as such a 5% speed buff makes a huge difference!

Moreover, as you grow your dragon you will quickly run out of gold. Dragon upgrades require vast amounts of gold and as such boosting your dwellings production rate (primary gold income unless you comfortably farm infernals) is a big big buff.

In fact, I know I just said this is the third best skin. If your goal is simply growth and you are not near the level 50 cap at the moment, then this castle skin is the absolute best skin. It drops off later on however, as you will finish your dragon levels well before you ever complete your technology. As such I rank the tech-skin Night Phantoms above this one. Also, this is not a combat buff and we have to rank the combat buff actually making your armies stronger than otherwise possible as the number one, hence The Great Celebration skin is unrivaled rank one.

This being said, as you grow you want to have this skin! The best growth buffs you can get are technology, dragon and buildings (in that order).

Troop cosmetic effect

This castle skin is one of only three skins that provide cosmetic skin effects for your troops as they march across the fields of Norheim and Frostborne.

How to get it?

There is only one way to obtain this skin: VIP level 15

There is only one way of obtaining this skin and that is getting to rank 15 VIP. You are going to have a rough time obtaining the required 1million VIP points to get here as a F2P. Spenders are going to get there eventually at which point you want to prioritize purchasing this box. The skin is simply very good value and something that I recommend you spend on if you are a spender. As a F2P you should not even try to get here. Spending 1 million gems on this is A LOT and you will still need to spend real money purchasing the Exalted Chest.

But if you do decide that you want to grind out the gems for free and get to VIP 15, consider this being your only purchase – money well spent.

If you do make it to rank 15 the Dark Fortress Castle skin is available along with the shadow dragon egg in the very last VIP unique bundle to be purchased at a price of 99$.

Golden Path

This skin is NOT available in the golden path rotation. Check out my article here to read more about the Castle skins offered via Golden Path as well as the full rotation.

description: Infinity Kingdom has a ton of cool city skins. You get skins from purchases during events, performance from in game activities such as contention of relics and/or Legion of Frostborne, Throne of the Supreeme, and so on.
html:
Infinity Kingdom has a ton of cool city skins. You get skins from purchases during events, performance from in game activities such as contention of relics and/or Legion of Frostborne, Throne of the Supreeme, and so on.

Castle Skins serve two purposes: (1) they provide unique buff effects to specific activities such as e.g. tech speed, dragon speed, combat buffs, recovery speed, resource collection rate, etc. and (2) they provide unique cosmetic effects that change the way your castle looks inside the game. The cosmetic effects work in all aspects of the game, any game mode, and provides some awesome customization to make youself more unique and your castle look.. well.. more awesome!

In this article we shall look to one of my personal favorite cosmetic skins in all of Infinity Kingdom: Harvest Song

What does Harvest Song do?

Every castle skin has unique beneficial effects, from building speed to rss gathering and troop HP. The Harvest Song provides you a 3% increase to your Resource Gathering Speed. What this means is often misunderstood by some players, and understandable so. There are many different ways to obtain resources in Infinity Kingdom and some of them blend togeather. What this skin does is it increases the rate at which your troops harvest resources at resource nodes. As such it provides NO buff to the rate at which your farms inside your castle produce resources, instead it allows you to be faster at collecting resources around the map of Norheim and Frostborne.

For example a level 10 node in Legion of Frostborne provides a gathering/harvest speed of 1M/hour. Without this skin active, you will harvest at a base speed of 1M/hour (not counting other tech, see below).

With this skin on, your collection rate increases by 30,000 resources per hour. What this means is, that per default it will take you 9 hours to collect all the resources in this node, but with the skin active you reduce that time to 8.7 hours.

The actual collection rate is a lot faster than the above, because you are getting strong modifiers to resource collection via Personal Technology as well as Alliance Technology. For instance, Stone gatherer provides a total of 20% increased collection rate to all Alliance members once max level.

Moreover Quick Mine provides you another 30% increased collection rate at max level (personal technology).

All in all, not a very powerful effect and certainly not an effect that I will recommend you to go after as one of the “best”… You should only get this skin if you think that the skin cosmetic effects are just too cool to pass on – which, I kinda get if you do! It is a very cute look.

How to get it?

There is only one way to obtain this skin: (1) Harvest Festival and (2) Golden Path seasonal shop

This skin was first released with the very first version of the Harvest Festival which occur every August in Infinity Kingdom. During this seasonal event, players have been able to complete quests and earn the Harvest Song Casle Skin. You should beware that these seasonal events tends to change every year, and as such I cannot give any guarantees as to how or if you will be able to collect this skin from the seasonal even when May comes around again.

However, lucky for you guys there is a place where you can be sure to collect this skin – in the Golden Path seasonal shop!

Golden Path

html:
🌸 Mt. Paradise Castle Skin Guide – Infinity Kingdom

The Mt. Paradise castle skin is the newest premium combat skin released in Infinity Kingdom, and it debuted during the Original Festival 2025 event (Easter event). Compared to previous skins, Mt. Paradise holds its own as a highly valuable addition for spenders looking to boost both their combat potential and utility on the battlefield.

🔍 What is Mt. Paradise?

Mt. Paradise is a permanent castle skin offering both a combat stat boost and a valuable utility perk:

  • +2% Troop HP
  • +5% Marching Speed

This combination makes it an extremely well-rounded skin for both PvP and PvE, rivaling some of the most powerful combat-oriented castle skins in the game.

🎯 What Makes It So Good?

💚 +2% Troop HP – A Straightforward Combat Boost

Troop HP is arguably the best all-around combat stat:

  • Increases your march durability in both PvP and PvE
  • Improves your frontline’s ability to soak damage
  • Stacks well with buffs from dragons, towers, and artifact effects

This is the same raw combat buff offered by other elite skins like Goddess of Victory and City of Glory, putting Mt. Paradise in top-tier territory from a stat perspective alone.

🕊️ +5% Marching Speed – Tactical Advantage

Speed can be just as powerful as stats in PvP. Here’s how:

  • Initiative Advantage: Strike first in mirrored fights by moving faster. If you and your opponent hit each other at the same time, your faster march hits first.
    • TIP: If against a player of equal power, you can recall your main before your enemy reaches your walls given that you have faster troop movement. Very powerful as you can use your main both offensively and defensively with the movement speed advantage!
  • Quick Repositioning: Faster movement helps you outmaneuver your opponent in real-time wars, sieges, or IB matches.
  • Faster Farming: Speed helps with PvE as well — gathering, raiding gnome camps, and boss rotation all benefit from march speed.

In fact, the march speed alone makes Mt. Paradise extremely attractive for aggressive PvP players.

🛍️ How Do You Get Mt. Paradise?

The Mt. Paradise skin is exclusive to the Original Festival 2025 event and can only be obtained by:

  • Purchasing the Premium Thriving Spirit Battle Pass during the event
  • Cost: $49.99 USD
  • Availability: April 18–27, 2025

🎁 What you get in addition to the skin:

  • 6,000 Gems
  • 60 Random Holy/Shadow Immortal Fragments
  • 10 Tokens of Light (used for Dazzling Wish pulls)
  • Various Speedups and Boosters

This bundle is outstanding value — you get a permanent castle skin, rare immortal fragments, and premium pulls for less than the cost of a standard $50 bundle. It’s essentially a massive discount on a combat skin with added high-tier extras.

🕒 Reminder: You must complete the full battle pass to earn the skin. That means doing daily missions and completing tasks over the 10-day period. You can skip up to one task per day and still finish in time.

⚔️ When to Use Mt. Paradise

Mt. Paradise is best used when:

  • You’re in PvP-focused events like Kill Events, KvK (Legion of Frostborne), or Illusion Battlefield
  • You want to secure the first hit advantage in mirrored PvP fights
  • You’re farming gnomes or world bosses quickly and want efficiency
  • You’re chasing fast deployment for critical sieges or backline raids

It’s also a great option to switch to when speed is more important than resource efficiency or reduced death rate.

🆚 How Does It Compare?

Here’s how Mt. Paradise stacks up against other popular combat skins:

Clearly, Mt. Paradise is positioned among the top combat skins for players who value speed and aggression.

🧠 Final Thoughts

The Mt. Paradise skin is an excellent addition to your skin rotation. If you’re a spender — even a light one — and you’re planning to buy anything during the Easter event, this skin is the smartest pickup available.

Not only does it boost your combat durability through Troop HP, but it also offers a unique utility that can give you a tactical edge in close fights. Combine this with its limited-time availability, and Mt. Paradise becomes a must-have for any serious Infinity Kingdom player.

🎯 Recommendation: Buy the $49.99 Premium Battle Pass before the event ends and make sure to finish all daily missions to unlock this skin. You won’t regret it.

Infinity Kingdom has a ton of cool city skins. You get skins from purchases during events, performance from in game activities such as contention of relics and/or Legion of Frostborne, Throne of the Supreeme, and so on.’

In this article we shall look to one of the absolute highest value skins of all – if not the single best skin in all of Infinity Kingdom: Night Phantoms.

What does “Night Phantoms” do?

Every castle skin has unique beneficial effects, from building speed to rss gathering and troop HP. The Night Phantoms castle skin provides a 3% technology upgrade speed boost. This is MASSIVE since technology is the single most time consuming activity/upgrade in all of Infinity Kingdom. Upgrading all of your buildings will be finished WAY before you ever get close to finishing even just the important combat tech, much less doing both growth, combat and defense.

For the most efficient upgrade path in Infinity Kingdom, a player must dedicate all universal speeds to Technology development. Simply, because there is so many many times more technologies to upgrade taking a lot more time. As such, I will argue that the single best buff for player growth is technology boost.

title: Sun Chariot
description: Sun Chariot Skin Guide – Pirate Event (September 2025)
html:
Sun Chariot Skin Guide – Pirate Event (September 2025)

Alright, so the Pirate seasonal event dropped a new skin this month called Sun Chariot, and it’s a new version of tank-skins not like previously released combat skins. Moreover, it is drop dead gorgeous, but that is just visuals ofcourse! Normally when we get a “tank” skin, it’s some mix of HP% and a sub-stat like troop death rate reduction, for example with Goddess of Victory. This one however changes things on its head and gives Immortal Physical Defense, Immortal Magical Defense, and March Speed. That last part is the kicker — march speed completely changes how you play out fights.

Obtaining Sun Chariot

You can get Sun Chariot straight up with the $50 battle pass, or you can try your luck with the Dazzling Wish, but that’s a 0.05% jackpot roll. I wouldn’t bank on that. If you want it, you’re basically buying it through the pass.

What makes Sun Chariot different

The Immortal defenses here are decent, and I actually like them more than the 2–3% HP we’ve had on earlier defensive skins. But the real standout is the march speed. Being able to move faster means you can hit someone and recall before their march lands, which is a huge advantage if you’ve got fast fingers. You can play poke games, stall out rallies, and just generally force your opponent to fight on your terms. That kind of mobility on a defensive skin is something we haven’t had before, and it makes Sun Chariot a lot more flexible than the usual “just tank longer” approach.

Personally, I am using the Mt. Paradise skin a lot for this very reason, as it gives me an option to fight with offensively and defensively with my main at the same time if at range against enemies who do not run a movespeed skin.

Comparing Sun Chariot to Abyssal and Skyriver

So let’s talk comparisons, because that’s the real question everyone has: is Sun Chariot actually better than Abyssal or Skyriver?

Abyssal Throne gives flat out Troop Attack (5-15)%, plus the little bit of death rate reduction. And honestly, troop stats scale way harder than Immortal stats. A 10% boost to Troop Attack gets multiplied by all 60k+ soldiers in your march late game, which is why Abyssal feels so insanely strong no matter what march you’re running. It’s just pure power, and since we’re seeing Abyssal fragments show up more often in passes, it’s also way easier to upgrade consistently than the new Sun Chariot.

Skyriver is a bit different. That one gives Immortal Attack % (both physical and magical) plus death rate reduction. So it’s kind of a hybrid: makes your Immortals hit harder while also softening troop losses. It’s not as universally good as Abyssal, but if you’re damage-focused it can still be a strong option.

Now, Sun Chariot gives Immortal Defense and march speed. Compared to Skyriver and Abyssal, the defenses are weaker long-term because they don’t multiply through your whole march. But that march speed is what keeps it in the conversation — if you’re the type of player who’s quick with recalls, Sun Chariot lets you play hit-and-run in a way the other two skins can’t.

Why troop stats win in the long run

Here’s the part that’s easy to miss: Immortal stats don’t scale nearly as well as troop stats. Your Immortal is just one unit. If you give them +10% defense, that makes them harder to kill, but it doesn’t do anything for the 60,000 troops backing them up. Troop Attack or Troop Defense, on the other hand, applies to every single soldier in the march. That means it’s multiplied across tens of thousands of units, and that multiplier makes troop stats exponentially stronger than Immortal stats once you’re late game.

That’s why Abyssal’s Troop Attack % is still the best skin bonus in the game in my opinion. And honestly, if we ever get a Troop Defense % skin — which feels like it’s only a matter of time — that’ll probably outclass Sun Chariot too (pure speculation, but would follow the current release pattern). Troop Defense would be like the perfect tank option, because it would scale across your entire march instead of just making your Immortals sturdier.

My personal take

So if you’re asking me straight up which skin to invest in, I’d say Abyssal Throne still wins every time and luckily, you get both the Sun Chariot unlock and the Abyssal Fragments in the Pirate Battle Pass! Yay, go ahead and get that. Should you in future invest in Sun Chariot if more options come available? Should you invest in the Dazzling Wish to upgrade it? No. It is not good enough for that.

That said, Sun Chariot isn’t worthless. If you’re already stacked on Abyssal and you’re looking for a situational tool, Sun Chariot can give you some really nasty tricks with march speed. The unlock will be useful to replace Mt. Paradise when speed is needed. Being able to smack an opponent and instantly recall before they hit you — that’s huge in IBL, KvK, or just castle brawls when you’re trying to bleed an enemy without over-committing. If you’re quick, it actually feels broken in the right situations.

But if we’re talking raw power, Troop Attack beats Immortal Defense. And if/when Troop Defense shows up, that’ll be even stronger. So for now, Abyssal is still the king, Skyriver has its place, and Sun Chariot is more of a specialty skin for people who want to play smart with mobility.

Final thoughts

At the end of the day, Sun Chariot is fun and unique, but it doesn’t dethrone Abyssal. Immortal Defense is nice, march speed is amazing if you can take advantage of it, but it doesn’t scale the way troop stats do. If you’re only picking one skin, go Abyssal. If you’re a spender and already have Abyssal maxed out, then yeah, Sun Chariot adds some spicy new options to your toolkit.

The bottom line? Abyssal is power. Sun Chariot is flexibility. And when troop defense eventually drops, that’ll probably be the new tank king.

title: When to use which combat battle skin?
description: In Infinity Kingdom, Castle Skins aren’t just for show – many of them offer powerful buffs that can make a real difference in both PvP and PvE scenarios. While some skins provide utility like increased march speed or honor gain, others grant direct combat boosts such as troop HP or death rate reduct
html:
In Infinity Kingdom, Castle Skins aren’t just for show – many of them offer powerful buffs that can make a real difference in both PvP and PvE scenarios. While some skins provide utility like increased march speed or honor gain, others grant direct combat boosts such as troop HP or death rate reduction. In this guide, we’ll take a closer look at the most valuable combat castle skins and how to make the most of them.

🌇 Castle Skins Overview

Castle skins in Infinity Kingdom come in many forms, and they fall roughly into two categories:

  1. Combat Utility Skins – These offer buffs that help with farming, marching, or event performance.
  2. Combat Strength Skins – These provide direct buffs to your troops, improving durability or reducing losses.

Understanding what each skin offers and how it fits your playstyle or event focus can make a big difference.

🏙️ Skins That Provide Combat Value

Mt. Paradise (Original Festival 2025)

  • Buffs: +2% Troop HP, +5% Marching Speed
  • Use Case: This skin is ideal for PvP, PvE, and sieges. The HP boost helps your troops last longer in battle, while the march speed allows you to:
    • Reach targets faster in PvP
    • Time attacks to land first in a mirror-fight scenario
    • Navigate the map more efficiently in PvE

City of Glory

  • Buffs: +2% Troop HP, +5% Honor Gained
  • Use Case: Excellent for PvP-focused players looking to farm honor efficiently. Climbing the Nobility Ladder grants massive boosts, so increasing honor gain passively with this skin is a smart strategy.
  • Best For: Players focused on Nobility Ranks and long-term PvP dominance.

Goddess of Victory

  • Buffs: +2% Troop HP, -3% Death Rate
  • Use Case: This is the most “efficient” of the combat skins. Reducing troop death rate means you lose fewer units in battle – a massive benefit during large-scale PvP fights or Immortal Battlefield (IB) where troop numbers are limited.
  • Best For: Farming gnomes, fighting bosses, or participating in IB formats.

🌎 Utility Skins Worth Mentioning

Colosseum

  • Buffs: +5% March Speed, +5% Honor Gained
  • Use Case: While it doesn’t provide a direct combat stat like HP or death rate, it’s still useful for Kill Events and farming honor.
  • Best For: Quick repositioning and utility farming setups.

📅 Which Skin Should You Use?

The answer depends on your focus:

  • PvP Fighters: Go with City of Glory or Mt. Paradise. Both offer troop HP, but the honor gain or faster marching may be more helpful depending on your style.
  • Efficiency Players & PvE Farmers: Goddess of Victory is best for troop conservation and gnome/boss farming.
  • Spenders in April 2025: Mt. Paradise offers great value with the Easter event’s Battle Pass. Grab it while you can!

🔄 Final Thoughts

Combat castle skins are a subtle but powerful part of progressing in Infinity Kingdom. The right skin can give you an edge in PvP or help you farm faster and smarter in PvE.

Whether you’re chasing honor, preserving troops, or rushing sieges, make sure you’re making full use of your castle skin buffs. And if you’re a spender, don’t miss limited-time skins like Mt. Paradise – the value you get for $50 is hard to beat, especially when paired with Tokens of Light and other premium rewards.

Stay strategic, and good luck in Norheim!

Infinity Kingdom has a ton of cool city skins. You get skins from purchases during events, performance from in game activities such as contention of relics and/or Legion of Frostborne, Throne of the Supreeme, and so on.

Castle Skins serve two purposes: (1) they provide unique buff effects to specific activities such as e.g. tech speed, dragon speed, combat buffs, recovery speed, resource collection rate, etc. and (2) they provide unique cosmetic effects that change the way your castle looks inside the game. The cosmetic effects work in all aspects of the game, any game mode, and provides some awesome customization to make youself more unique and your castle look.. well.. more awesome!

In this article we shall look to the cosmetic castle skin called: Wonderful World

What does Wonderful World do?

Every castle skin has unique beneficial effects, from building speed to rss gathering and troop HP. The Wonderful World provides you a 3% increase to hospitals healing speed. This is a very solid buff and when this skin was first released it was a major priority for me personally to unluck it as fast as possible purely for it’s effect. You are going to be healing millions of troops spending a ton of speed-ups. This saves you 3%. That’s solid!

HOWEVER. There is a major change since this skin was first released. We have gotten a new skin in Norheim: the Frozen Dragon Hive. This skin does the same as Wonderful world, just better. It’s 5% as well as a solid 5% boost to production of resources. This obviously makes our Wonderful World skin a lot less powerful by comparison. However, it remains a solid skin if you are unable to obtain the Frozen Dragon Hive.

How to get it?

There is only one way to obtain this skin: (1) Original Easter Festival

The Original Easter Festival of Infinity Kingdom is an annual event that offers players a chance to obtain the exclusive Castle Cosmetic skin “Wonderful World.” This skin can only be obtained during the festival and is not available through any other means.

The 2023 edition of the Easter Festival is on it’s first day as I am writing this, and players can acquire the “Wonderful World” skin for a price of $185. While this may seem steep, the skin is highly coveted among players, and this is the only opportunity to obtain it.

Players can participate in a variety of festive activities during the event, including Easter egg hunts, special battles, and more. They can also earn rewards such as in-game currency and rare items.

Overall, the Original Easter Festival of Infinity Kingdom is a highly anticipated event among players, as it offers a unique opportunity to obtain the exclusive cosmetic skin Wonderful World that cannot be obtained through any other means.

For commanders struggling with gem upkeep, prioritize the cheaper tiers to maintain a steady influx of Stardust without compromising overall gem management.

Maximizing Stardust gains from the Deep Sea Merchant requires a delicate balance between gem investment and strategic planning.
