description: I get a lot of players sending me requests for march setups, lately I have been getting a lot of interest in running a F2P version of the earth-wind hybrid as a second or third team. Furthermore, many people seem to be running water mains where they have spent a little to get Attila and Merlin then
html:
I get a lot of players sending me requests for march setups, lately I have been getting a lot of interest in running a F2P version of the earth-wind hybrid as a second or third team. Furthermore, many people seem to be running water mains where they have spent a little to get Attila and Merlin then pure free to play from there on. Other prefer fire or lightning marches but many players are writing saying they have water main since the beginning of the game, but don’t know what to do with it to make it fit with a second and third march build.

For the purpose of this guide I shall use a real player from the community. This player reached out and asked me to setup a complete three-march-setup that fits with what he has going for him at the moment. If you are a F2P or low-spender and is looking for inspiration for how to setup your marches, this guide may just be for you!

Togeather with the community I ended up with this three-march-setup to recommend for our requesting-player: (1) Water main (2) Fire secondary and (3) Earth/Wind Hybrid third.

In addition to these builds and collective setup, I will include a link to future work on how these builds can improve and develop if you choose to spend to unlock new Immortals.

Message to the trolls: Yes this is considered F2P builds. Yes, this is technically not true since u pay a couple bucks unlocking the third builder to get Merlin. No I do not care that i’m technically incorrect, I consider the third builder “the price of installing the IK app” and No that does not make anything P2W… Aight… With that out of the way, let’s dive in and actually enjoy some content!

Current player setups

First up, we have got four different elements going here but only want three marches fit for combat. We are going to be leaving out Lightning, simply because we do not have any solid replacements for Peter. Peter is spearman tech as our only Immortal, this is terrible simply because we want to eliminate one troop tier to make a more slim technology progression path.

While the best options would be to replace Peter with William or Hippo, we would also have multiple magic passives in reserve since we do not have access to a Hammurabi. If you have Hammurabi yourself and a high level lightning dragon, you can go Hammu-YSG-William-Richard. But since that is not the case for our player here, it is easy to eliminate lightning from our combat roster.

The second thing we need to do is figure out what we want to focus on. You always want to focus on a main, then a second then a third. Doing all three marches at the same time (upgrading dragons and ToK passives equally) is a huge disadvantage. Since this player is invested in water dragon having it at max level progressing through the dragon talents, we are going to stay the course and keep water for main. For the second and third team, we are actually for once going to be not focusing on them as either or. Instead we will be setting up builds that fit each other so well that there is no overlap between the skills you want to run and as such can consider either one of them your second. Complete player preference.

My recommendation for all three builds

We got some pretty scattered passive combinations going on however a decent setup for water as is. What I am going to do is move around a bit making small ajustments to the water team to fit in the current meta. Moreover, we are going to make a clear goal for how our second and third are going to look once we finish building it out. This sets up a nice goal for our player to work towards, and once achieved is an excellent position to further improve on with the later game P2P immortals, if he so chooses. Either way, a solid position for a basic setup with a good division of tok skills which means you can easily change it to fit your current server meta and also means that you are not running multiple setups that all need the same passives to work.

I will show the builds visually from an IB-league formation. So disregard the power and lack of artifact. The images are only to visually show you the Tower of Knowledge builds. Beware that Gilga = Arash!

We are turning the water into a standard control-centric setup with Merlin as our core dps. As for the fire, we are building full offense and maxing its burst crit potention, with a bit of luck you can take down a huge chunck of HP on even marches with much higher power with an offensive fire. Lastly our hybrid will be a standard wind-earth hyrbrid with a few modifications since we are not running it as a main. Basically this hybrid is able to get massive value out of a lot of tok skills which are terrible anywhere else. Running it in this way means that we are using top tower of knowledge skills on all three marches instead of having a third with nothing going on (as is often the case)

— WATER —
Merlin: Concentration + Annihilation + Death Breath
Yoshi: Assist + Malice + Absolute Defense
Herald: Missleading + Energy Suppression + Oaken Guard
Attila: Adrenaline rush + Fighting Will + Fighting Master

— FIRE w. GILGA —
Gilga: Anger + Chaotic Blade + Onslaught
Wu: Chase + Toxic Nova + Rage (if you have enough crit to consistently proc chase, you can go double nova over rage)
Hippo: Energy Burst + Sacrifice + Garrote
William: Weakness + Blessing of Rage + Resist

— EARTH-WIND HYBRID —
Zeno: Berserk + Blessing of Speed + Life-link/After Image (depends on phys. enemy vs backline nuke mages)
Qin: Coercion + Blessing of War + Blessing of Defense
Hannibal Barca: Cleave + Shelter + Heavenly Thunder
Alexander: Duel Master + Combo + Absorb

While I have not played these myself, the respons I have gotten back from the Player who sent in the request are overwhelmingly positive. The setups seem to work very very well for him. Versus other waters and fires he prefers Life Link on Zeno and is running with double nova on Wu for the best result.

Further development and build progression

Like I said in the beginning of this guide, this is tailored for one particular player and then made into a generalized guide for others to seek inspiration from. Your Immortals roster, willingness to spend, server PvP meta may be a lot different from this player’s and as such you should as always make careful decisions that fit your situation. Use the above as inspiration!

In addition to the three-setup-builds we have gone other in this guide, I have made some progression pathways as part of a broader series on low-spender-three-march-setups: Read more here.

Fitting with this particular three-march-setup with Water main, Fire and Hybrid second/third, you may want to consider a progression path that develops and evolve into: Water w. Bath/Himiko + Fire w Gilga/Seon + Hybrid.

title: Water-Fire-Hybrid setup progression path
description: WATER, FIRE and HYBRID progression path
html:
WATER, FIRE and HYBRID progression path

Okay guys, welcome to a wierd one! I have been asked a lot to make free-to-play and low-spender setups and builds for people, and honestly I think they can be pretty tricky to get right. You are in a power disadvantage to many players spending making your only chance to compete having stronger builds and countering what your enemy is running. There is a huge focus on builds in Infinity Kingdom – and it is what makes this game so amazingly interesting to me.

So, for this article I am going to be sharing some of my ideas for builds in different spender-tiers. They are all focused on players who continued with developing water right from the beginning as a main, and they are all low-spender friendly, beginning from Free-to-Play and moving into builds that require some of the spender Immortals, while staying in the cheap-march-tier.

Progression path / Build versions

(1) Water + Fire w Gilga + hybrid
Water: Merlin + Yoshi + Herald + Attila
Fire: Gilga + Wu + William + Hippo
Hybrid: Zeno + Qin + Alex + Hannibal

We are beginning with a free to play build that can perform just fine. You are running a very standard water team, which may perform a bit underwhelming as a main. However, your fire and hybrid teams can do well as your second and third. Furthermore, as you progress and develop, you can choose to move further down the progression ladder staying with Water as a main OR swap into a Fire or Hybrid F2P main. I do think that both fire and hybrid is stronger as a complete free to play. However, getting Bathory or later Himiko Ragnar will enable you to continue running a viable strong water main.

(2) Water with Bath + Fire w Gilga/Seon & Wu + Hybrid
Water: Merlin + Bath + Herald + Attila
Fire: Gilga/Seon + Wu + Hippo + William/Trajan
Hybrid: Zeno + Qin + Alex + Hannibal

Version 2 here is a development on the very first setup version we went over here. We have grown and become able to use Bathory and possibly also Seondeok and Trajan. With Bathory instead of Yoshi your Water team become A LOT more powerful and you will increase your performance significantly in both PvP and PvE content. You can choose to keep Yoshi for boss-killing-builds, but other then that melt him.

If you are able to obtain both Seondeok and Trajan for your fire team, you can choose to run this as your new main. I would personally prefer this, however your dragon may be giving you problems. Without either of them (they are around 350$ each via bundles only) you can keep your Gilga Fire as a solid free second/third.

(3) Water w. Himiko + Fire + Hybrid
Water: Merlin + Himiko + Ragnar + Attila
Fire: Seon + Wu + Hippo + Trajan
Hybrid: Zeno + Qin + Alex + Hannibal

Okay okay okay, at this point you are becoming a true beast. Running three top tier builds, all of which pair perfectly with each other providing huge synergies from ToK-dispersion. These marches are ALL amazing and you can choose to run either one of them as your main. Go for whichever dragon you have highest level and once you have all three dragons maxed you can simply choose which one you want to main.

If you are able to hit true-max on dragon talents, you literally have three “main” marches. A very very powerful 3-march-setup that will perform well at the highest levels of play in even the most competitive servers.

Merlin: Concentration + Annihilation + Death Breath
Bathory: Assist + Malice + Absolute Defense

Attila: Adrenaline rush + Fighting Will + Fighting Master

— FIRE w. GILGA —

Wu: Chase + Toxic Nova + Rage (if you have enough crit to consistently proc chase, you can go double nova over rage)
Hippo: Energy Burst + Missleading + Garrote.

Qin: Coercion + Blessing of War + Blessing of Defense

Further development and build progression

Like I said in the beginning of this guide, this is tailored for one particular player and then made into a generalized guide for others to seek inspiration from. title: Countering Blade Vortex Executioner combo
description: Player Guide: Countering the Blade Vortex and Executioner Combo
html:
Player Guide: Countering the Blade Vortex and Executioner Combo

The Blade Vortex and Executioner combo is currently dominating the meta in Infinity Kingdom, achieving insane damage numbers and quickly nuking down anything in its path. However, this combo has a key weakness: it relies heavily on negative effects in the form of DoTs (damage over time) plus damage amplification debuffs. This gives us a few tools to counter this devastating combo effectively. Here are some ideas and concepts to counter the Blade Vortex and Executioner meta.

Key Counters

Most of these “how to counter” guides will give you an explanation of how to render something obsolete. This however is not the case, while Athena does render this combo obsolete, she is not available for everyone and therefore most players should expect to take significant damage from the combo. However, that does not mean you must have Athena to counter. There are many more ways to get advantages against an enemy Blade Vortex + Execution combo.

1. Theodora

Theodora is a powerful Holy Immortal healer who has been a staple in sustain Holy teams for years. Her unique ability to heal is rivaled only by her capacity to dispel damage over time effects, making her an excellent counter to Blade Vortex and the DoTs that activate Executioner.

  • Healing and Dispel: Theodora’s healing ability, combined with her capacity to remove DoTs, makes her an effective tool against this combo. By consistently dispelling these negative effects, she mitigates a significant portion of the damage output from Blade Vortex and Executioner.

2. Purification

Purification is a top-tier Tower of Knowledge skill that can activate on any Immortal, giving you a 25% chance to clear debuffs from each Immortal every cycle. While Purification alone may not be strong enough to hard counter the combo, it can still dampen the ramp-up damage from Blade Vortex and Executioner.

  • Debuff Removal: By regularly dispelling some of the DoTs, Purification can reduce the overall damage your team receives. This makes it a useful skill to include in your strategy, especially when combined with other countermeasures.

3. Athena

Athena is an absolute beast of an S-tier Immortal and the true hard counter to the Blade Vortex and Executioner combo. Her ability to remove all negative effects from all allies consistently makes her the best counter against this combo.

  • Comprehensive Cleanse: Athena’s ultimate ability to cleanse all negative effects from her team makes her incredibly powerful against debuff-reliant strategies like Blade Vortex and Executioner. However, Athena is a Chaos Immortal, meaning she is more challenging to obtain and upgrade.

Effective Strategies

For most players, having access to Athena may not be feasible. Here’s a strategy that combines Purification and Theodora to effectively counter the Blade Vortex and Executioner combo:

Combination of Theodora and Purification

  • Theodora + Adrenaline Rush: Using Adrenaline Rush to activate Theodora’s ultimate ability more frequently ensures that her healing and dispel capabilities are maximized. This combination helps to mitigate a significant portion of the damage from Blade Vortex and Executioner.
  • Purification: Including Purification in your setup adds an additional layer of debuff removal, further reducing the impact of the DoTs and damage amplification debuffs from the combo.

Conclusion

In practice, you will still receive significant damage from the Blade Vortex and Executioner combo, but by mitigating it effectively with Theodora and Purification, your own physical damage dealers, such as Bathory or Alexander, can ramp up and overtake the opponent’s damage output, ultimately winning the fight.

By using these strategies and counters, you can effectively manage and counter the current Blade Vortex and Executioner meta, ensuring your team remains competitive and resilient in battles.

Player Guide: Adapting to Fu Fei’s Balance Change in Infinity Kingdom

Fu Fei, a renowned chaos immortal in Infinity Kingdom, known for her potent healing abilities and control immunity, has recently become even more formidable following a balance update to her ultimate ability. This change significantly enhances her strategic value, particularly in countering control-based strategies that have previously served as viable methods to challenge chaos immortal setups, notably those involving Himiko.

Understanding Fu Fei’s Enhanced Ultimate Ability

Before the Update

Fu Fei has been absolute top ranked for healing done since her release but that is not all there is to her!

Previously, while Fu Fei provided a broad spectrum of control immunity, her protections did not extend to the unique control effects of Himiko’s ultimate ability. This allowed for strategic counterplay against chaos immortal setups, leveraging Himiko’s control capabilities.

After the Balance Change

The recent update has augmented Fu Fei’s ultimate ability, enabling it to grant immunity even against Himiko’s controls. This development closes a critical loophole, significantly reducing the effectiveness of previously viable counter-chaos strategies.

Strategic Implications

The enhancement of Fu Fei’s ultimate ability has considerable implications for players across the board, particularly affecting the strategic landscape in PvP battles:

  • Strengthened Chaos Setups: Fu Fei’s enhanced ability solidifies the dominance of chaos immortals by providing a comprehensive defense against one of the few weaknesses chaos setups had.
  • Reduced Counterplay Options: The update narrows the strategic options available to players aiming to counter top-tier, Pay to Play chaos immortal lineups, challenging the community to innovate new strategies.

Looking Forward: Strategies Against Enhanced Chaos Immortals

With direct control counterplay options dwindling, players must explore alternative strategies to compete against the enhanced capabilities of chaos immortals like Fu Fei:

  • Focus on Damage Mitigation and Sustain: Since direct control counterplay has been diminished, building lineups that prioritize damage mitigation and sustain can help withstand the onslaught from chaos immortals.
  • Leverage Speed and Debuffs: Speed manipulation and debuff strategies (outside of control effects) may offer a new avenue to challenge chaos setups, focusing on outpacing and weakening opponents before they can leverage their full potential.
  • Innovative Immortal Synergies: Exploring less conventional immortal combinations and synergies that can exploit subtle vulnerabilities in chaos setups might emerge as a viable strategy.

Community’s Role in Evolving Strategies

The balance change to Fu Fei’s ultimate ability presents a new challenge for the Infinity Kingdom community. It encourages players to engage in deeper strategic thinking and theorycrafting to devise methods to compete against the strengthened chaos immortal lineups. This evolving dynamic underscores the game’s complexity and the continuous interplay between different strategies, urging players to adapt and innovate.

Conclusion

Fu Fei’s recent enhancement marks a significant shift in the strategic balance of Infinity Kingdom, particularly affecting the dynamics of PvP combat. While this change bolsters the power of chaos immortals, it also serves as a catalyst for strategic innovation among players. As the community navigates this new landscape, the effectiveness of emerging counter-strategies will undoubtedly shape the future of competition in Infinity Kingdom, highlighting the ever-evolving nature of its strategic depth.

The Ultimate Guide to Countering Hybrid builds and Physical Damage in Infinity Kingdom

In the dynamic battlefield of Infinity Kingdom, mastering the art of countering can be the key to your triumph. Today, we’re delving into a comprehensive strategy to neutralize physical damage dealers, especially formidable immortals like Alexander and Hannibal Barca, using the potent Tower of Knowledge skill: Weakening Curse. This guide is your secret weapon against the onslaught of physical damage, holy, and hybrid builds dominating the arena.

Understanding Weakening Curse: A Game Changer

Weakening Curse is not just another skill; it’s a tactical nuclear option for players seeking to disrupt the enemy’s offensive capabilities significantly. Available exclusively through Triss, this Pay-to-Play skill embodies the definition of a game-changer in player matchups.

What It Does: After the battle commences, Weakening Curse disarms the entire enemy team, slashing the damage they deal by a staggering 70% until they cast an ultimate skill. This effect can last up to 45 seconds, a near eternity in the fast-paced clashes of Infinity Kingdom.

Why It’s Considered Overpowered: The sheer impact of Weakening Curse on Alexander and Hannibal Barca is monumental. Their Unique Artifacts (UA) transform their ultimate abilities into passives, rendering them incapable of casting ultimates. Consequently, they suffer a 70% damage reduction for the full duration of 45 seconds, essentially neutralizing their threat. This strategic advantage renders Weakening Curse the ultimate countermeasure, particularly against hybrids, leaving them floundering.

Crafting a Counter-Strategy

To effectively leverage Weakening Curse, understanding its synergy with other skills is crucial. Here’s a step-by-step strategy to maximize its potential:

  1. Initiate with No Escape: Start the battle by silencing your opponents for the initial 6 seconds with No Escape. This ensures that enemy immortals cannot generate energy to cast their skills, setting the stage for Weakening Curse.
  2. Apply Energy Suppression: Following the silence, Energy Suppression plays a pivotal role by further inhibiting energy regeneration. This extended energy drought means that opponents struggle even more to cast their ultimate skills, perpetuating their weakened state under Weakening Curse.
  3. Strategic Implementation: The timing and sequence of these skills are critical. The initial silence from No Escape, followed by Energy Suppression, creates a window where Weakening Curse can drastically reduce the enemy’s damage output, particularly against high-impact physical damage dealers.
  4. Target Selection: While Alexander and Hannibal Barca are prime targets due to their passive ultimates, don’t overlook the potential against other physical powerhouses. Holy, Seon Fire, and Khan Lightning builds, known for their rapid physical damage, can also be effectively countered.
  5. Adaptation and Flexibility: Remember, the battlefield is ever-changing. Adapt your strategy based on your opponents’ compositions and the immortals at your disposal. While Weakening Curse offers a powerful tool, its optimal use requires careful consideration of the broader battle context.

Conclusion

Weakening Curse stands as a testament to strategic depth in Infinity Kingdom, offering players a powerful means to counter prevailing physical damage strategies. By integrating this skill with a thoughtful approach to skill synergy and timing, you can turn the tides of battle against even the most formidable foes. Embrace this strategy to not just survive but thrive against physical damage dealers, securing your place among the legends of the Infinity Kingdom.

Player Guide: Countering Lightning Builds in Infinity Kingdom with Purification

Lightning builds in Infinity Kingdom are notorious for their reliance on debuffs to amplify damage and trigger powerful effects, making them formidable in battle. These builds often utilize a combination of negative effects like wounds, stuns, and damage modifiers to activate dragon bonuses and maximize the output of immortals like Hammurabi. However, their strength can also be their vulnerability. By effectively disrupting their debuff application, you can significantly weaken the impact of lightning builds. This guide will explore how to use the skill Purification to counter lightning strategies effectively.

The Role of Debuffs in Lightning Builds

Lightning builds excel by applying various debuffs to gain significant advantages:

  • Debuff Application: Key to their strategy, debuffs activate specific immortal abilities and enhance dragon effects, crucial for scaling their damage.
  • Immortal Synergy: Lightning immortals are often tailored to maximize the impact of these debuffs, with many of their abilities either applying or capitalizing on these effects to inflict massive damage.

Dragon Synergy: Lightning dragon furthermore add to the power of debuffs in lightning with the added damage effects

Countering with Purification

Understanding Purification

Purification isn’t just another skill; it’s a strategic asset that requires mastery to optimize its potential. Here’s how it functions:

  • Activation and Timing: Purification triggers swiftly with a 3-second cooldown and targets a random team member.
  • Primary Function: Its main role is to clear any debuffs or abnormal effects from the targeted immortal. In the absence of debuffs, it provides a minor healing effect.

Strategic Implementation

To counter lightning builds using Purification, consider the following tactics:

  • Team Composition: Incorporate immortals that can benefit from or support the use of Purification. This may include immortals with passive abilities that enhance resistance to debuffs or others that can provide additional cleansing or support.
  • Monitor Debuff Application: Keep a close watch on the types and timings of debuffs applied by the enemy. Understanding when and how your opponent likes to deploy their debuffs can help you anticipate and counter their moves more effectively.

Additional Tips

  • Multiple Cleansers: Considering the randomness of Purification’s targeting, having multiple sources of debuff cleansing on your team can ensure more consistent removal of debuffs.
  • Skill Synergy: Pair Purification with other skills that either prevent debuff application or mitigate its effects, such as shields or immunity-granting abilities.
  • Adapt and React: Be flexible and ready to adapt your strategy based on how the battle progresses. The effectiveness of your countermeasures might require adjustments mid-fight depending on your opponent’s tactics.

Conclusion

By mastering the use of Purification and integrating it strategically into your battle plans, you can effectively neutralize the core mechanics of lightning builds in Infinity Kingdom. This approach not only disrupts your opponent’s strategy but also enhances your ability to control the battlefield, turning the tide in your favor against one of the most debuff-reliant setups in the game. As always, success will depend on your ability to adapt and fine-tune your strategies to the evolving meta and specific challenges posed by your opponents.

description: Holy immortals have long been seen as the go-to counter for shadow teams in Infinity Kingdom, but recent updates and the rise of Tutankhamun have made shadow the clear meta leader in Season 1. Once upon a time, Holy offered a clean 25% damage boost and reduction against shadow, which made it the bes
html:
Holy immortals have long been seen as the go-to counter for shadow teams in Infinity Kingdom, but recent updates and the rise of Tutankhamun have made shadow the clear meta leader in Season 1. Once upon a time, Holy offered a clean 25% damage boost and reduction against shadow, which made it the best hard-counter strategy. However, developer changes have adjusted the elemental multipliers, making Holy less dominant. Even so, Holy builds remain viable, especially for high-spending players (whales) who want to run both a maxed shadow and holy team for flexibility and power. This guide outlines a powerful Holy build optimized to deliver maximum performance while leaving key skills free for your shadow team.

Why Holy Still Works

Despite the recent meta leaning heavily into shadow and Tutankhamun builds, Holy still brings unique strengths to the table. It is one of the best anti-control elements in the game. Theodora, a cornerstone of Holy, can cleanse status effects like Confuse and Blade Vortex, while also providing massive healing output. The ramp-up nature of Holy teams means you won’t see explosive damage early in the fight, but if you survive the first 20 seconds, you gain powerful momentum and become incredibly hard to stop.

In addition to its sustainability, Holy gives you counterplay options against specific meta strategies. Confuse from Tomyris? No problem. Bleeds and DoTs from Blade Vortex? Theodora can cleanse them. Burst from Himiko? We snipe her with Nebuchadnezzar.

Optimal Whale Holy Setup (Paired With Max Shadow)

This specific setup is tested and built for players who already have a separate maxed-out shadow team and want to preserve key ToK skills like Fighting Master and Guard for that team. It provides ramp-up defense and output while protecting your main damage dealer, Manco.

Theodora

  • Purify: Removes debuffs including Blade Vortex, stuns, wounds, etc. Consider placing Purify in your shadow team if Theo’s ultimate is enough for cleansing.
  • Shelter: Provides substantial healing over time. In extended battles, this outperforms Vitality Touch in raw healing.
  • Vitality Touch: Boosts healing and gives a defensive buff.

Nebuchadnezzar II

  • Snipe: Target positioning so that you snipe key enemy backliners like Himiko.
  • Malice: Prevents high crit bursts from enemy teams.
  • Rage Blessing: Enables faster skill cycling early. If your shadow needs Oaken Guard, this is a good alternate defensive boost.

Khubilaikhan

  • Full Coverage: Helps defend Manco while adding support.
  • Spear Impale: Delivers physical damage, maintaining pressure.
  • Life-Link: Soaks damage and redirects it. Optional for synergy. Consider replacing with Physical Shield if you don’t need it in your hybrid team.

Manco

  • Void Realm: Provides immunity for 18s—the ramp-up window you need.
  • Victorious Pursuit: Incredible synergy with Manco’s ultimate for ramping damage.
  • Demonic Contract: Boosts damage the longer the fight goes.

This build is especially strong because it reserves Fighting Master and Guard for your shadow team. With this configuration, the Holy team still delivers devastating late-game damage and top-tier sustain.

Performance

This Holy setup has been tested in live PvP with exceptional results. It took down multiple maxed-out marches from top whales, even eliminating all four armies in some cases. This confirms that the right skill allocation and strategy can make Holy a serious threat in the current Season 1 meta, even if it’s no longer the go-to hardcounter it used to be.

Alternatives for Holy-Only Whales

If you don’t have a strong shadow team and want to optimize Holy alone, consider shifting your skills:

Build Variant 1 (Pure Holy)

  • Theo: Oaken Guard/Assist, Vitality Touch, Weakness
  • Neb: Blade Vortex, Fighting Master, Malice
  • Manco: Void Realm, Demonic Contract, Victorious Pursuit
  • Khubilai: Energy Burst, Spear Impale, Full Coverage

This version gives you stronger early-mid fight output and better control resistance on Neb. Blade Vortex also provides a reliable DoT pressure tool.

Strategic Considerations

  • Skill Allocation Between Teams: If you run both a shadow and a holy team, think of your ToK skills as a limited pool. Assign Guard, Fighting Master, and Oaken Guard wisely.
  • Enemy Composition: Adapt based on opponents. Facing Tutankhamun? Snipe him with Alex or Neb. Facing Himiko? Use Fighting Master or position properly to avoid Confuse.
  • DoT Mitigation: Purify and Theo’s ultimate are key to countering Blade Vortex.
  • Dragon Strategy: pairing this team with Holy Dragon for added healing, or Earth if you cannot upgrade holy fully, providing good improved troop durability.

Final Thoughts

Holy may no longer be the default anti-shadow answer, but in the hands of a whale with access to maxed skills and high-end immortals, it can still dominate. This build lets you extract maximum value from your Holy march while preserving crucial skills for a powerful shadow team. Whether you run it as your main or second march, Holy is very much alive and viable in Season 1—especially for those willing to play the long game.

Stay tuned for the full triple march composition guide for whales, where this Holy setup will be featured as part of a rotation alongside a shadow and hybrid build.

title: Darius Lightning Build (2.6.3)
description: Unleashing the Thunder: Lightning Build Guide in Infinity Kingdom
html:
Unleashing the Thunder: Lightning Build Guide in Infinity Kingdom

Prepare to electrify the battlefield with a lightning-themed build in Infinity Kingdom. This guide will walk you through the intricacies of creating a potent lineup that revolves around Immortals Genghis Khan, Hammurabi, Darius, and Tokugawa/Bjorn.

With a focus on delivering quick wounds from Khan and enhancing the damage output of Darius and Hammurabi, this build is a versatile powerhouse that excels against Earth and hybrid builds.

It also holds its ground against Holy builds and serves as a strong all-around option for both mid-game and end-game content.

Build Composition

  1. Hammurabi (Damage Dealer): Equip Hammurabi with skills that amplify his damage potential. Consider using Spell Disintegration, Concentration, and Annihilation. This setup ensures he unleashes devastating area-of-effect damage.
  2. Genghis Khan (Wound Inflictor and Burst Damage): Khan’s role is to inflict wounds swiftly on the enemy while delivering a significant first-attack burst before his troop count decreases. Utilize skills like Fighting Master, Adrenaline Rush for fast wound infliction. You can also opt for the Assist skill if you have Guard for frontline support. Or you can boost his damage with Anger.
  3. Tokugawa/Bjorn (Support and Utility): Tokugawa or Bjorn serves as a versatile utility Immortal, adapting to your specific enemy composition. As a baseline, skills like Weakness, Defense Blessing, Oaken Guard, and Resist are potent choices. However, you can also incorporate newer defensive skills like Energy Shield, Weakening Curse, or Siren’s Gaze based on the meta in your server. The key is to mitigate the damage type dealt by your primary adversaries. If you have Guard, pairing it with Void Realm provides optimal protection for Darius, especially if Khan is running Assist.
  4. Darius (Damage Dealer): Focus on maximizing Darius’s damage output. Select skills such as Anger, Desire of Life, and Toxin Barrier. This combination empowers him to deliver substantial area-of-effect damage. If the need arises for more defense, consider replacing Desire of Life or Toxin Barrier with skills like Physical Shield, adjusting your build to counter the specific enemy you face.

Results and Strategies:
The results of this lightning-themed build are nothing short of remarkable. Darius shines as a damage dealer, while the combination of Fighting Master and Adrenaline Rush on Khan ensures immunity to control effects and rapid energy regeneration. This synergy leads to swift wound infliction on your enemies.

With a substantial troop count, both Hammurabi and Darius emerge as top-tier damage dealers in the game. However, it’s vital to address their vulnerability, as they can be relatively squishy and susceptible to enemy damage.

To enhance the longevity of Hammurabi and Darius on the battlefield, consider further support from Tokugawa or Bjorn, with an emphasis on defense and crowd control skills to deter enemy threats. This lightning build’s adaptability to counter the most prominent threats in your server’s meta, such as Earth and hybrid builds, ensures its effectiveness in various scenarios.

In summary, the lightning-themed build featuring Genghis Khan, Hammurabi, Darius, and Tokugawa/Bjorn is a powerhouse that combines rapid wound infliction, massive area-of-effect damage, and adaptability to counter diverse enemy compositions. Mastering this build will undoubtedly make you a formidable force in the Infinity Kingdom battlefield. Electrify your foes and emerge victorious!

title: Double Tank Lightning (2.8.6)
description: Lightning marches have always had a special place in Infinity Kingdom. While newer strategies and Chaos immortals have since overshadowed it, this build still deserves
html:
Lightning marches have always had a special place in Infinity Kingdom. For a period two years ago, Double Tank Lightning dominated the meta as one of the most consistent and versatile builds in the game. While newer strategies and Chaos immortals have since overshadowed it, this build still deserves attention — especially for players who want a spender-friendly setup that doesn’t require Chaos immortals or heavy investment into legendary skills.

In this guide, we’ll revisit Double Tank Lightning, explain its strengths and weaknesses in today’s Conquest meta, and outline exactly how to build and run it effectively.

🔎 Introduction: Why Double Tank Lightning?

Double Tank Lightning is exactly what the name suggests: a Lightning march anchored by two frontline tanks that keep the backline damage dealers safe long enough to win fights.

  • The tanks (Tokugawa + El Cid) bring durability, disruption, and defensive utility.
  • The backline (Khan + Hammurabi) supplies a combination of physical burst and sustained magical DPS.

The result is a balanced, grindy team that can survive physical-heavy opponents and dish out dangerous counterpressure over time.

While not the absolute peak of Conquest, it remains one of the most accessible strong spender builds because it avoids Chaos immortals and focuses on obtainable pieces.

🏛️ Place in the Meta

Strengths

  • Budget Friendly: No Chaos immortals or expensive legendary skills required.
  • Tanky & Reliable: Double tank + defensive skills buys time for your DPS to shine.
  • Flexible: Can be adapted for crit builds, hybrid setups, or sustained ramp play.
  • Anti-Physical: Excels versus Alex, Hannibal, and other physical burst teams.

Weaknesses

  • Mage Weakness: Fire and Water magic teams often overwhelm this setup.
  • Scaling Limitations: Without Chaos skills like Energy Mastery or Infinite Firepower, damage ceiling is lower than top-tier Conquest builds.
  • Skill Dependent: Needs careful skill selection (Berserk Aura, Weakness, Energy Shield) to stay competitive.

Who Should Use It?

  • Mid-to-High Spenders who want a competitive but not whale-exclusive build.
  • Players looking to bridge the gap into Conquest without relying on Chaos.
  • Veterans nostalgic for Lightning,
  • or players progressing into max Cao Cao or Fu Fei (where Double Tank Lightning gets a new power jump).

⚔️ Core Build Breakdown

Frontline – The Double Tanks

Tokugawa Ieyasu

  • Specialization: Iron Will (core tank talent).
  • Skills: Fountain of Life (big upgrade vs No escape enemies) alternatively Heart of Arcana, No Escape, Guard or Oaken (or mix in Weakness/Malice depending on matchup).
  • Role: Primary stall tank, holding the line and disrupting enemy DPS.

El Cid

  • Specialization: Iron Will.
  • Skills: Physical Shield, Energy Shield, Weakening Curse.
  • Role: Anti-physical wall, especially effective vs Alex/Hannibal teams.
  • Note: El Cid artifacts and fragments are now easier to farm, making him more practical.

OBS: While Cid is amazing in an earth-wind based meta which you are likely in in season 2. You are going to want to replace Cid with Bjorn eventually. Use those holy/shadow chests to max Bjorn on the side.

After this we progress into possibly himiko instead of hammurabi while you build Fu Fei to complete the lightning build journey.

Backline – The Damage Dealers

Genghis Khan (Secondary DPS)

  • Build Options:
    • Crit Khan Build: Weakness Aura, Adrenaline Rush, with Flexible third slot: Blade Vortex, Death Breath or Anger. Can also also be upgraded with Ambush or Time to Shine if available.
  • Balanced Build: Chaos Storm (if unlocked) to give both physical and magical damage support.
  • Specialization: Deadly Aim (crit rate + crit damage).
  • Role: Provides physical burst and wound, crit-based one-shots when lucky.

Hammurabi (Primary DPS)

  • Core Skills: Corrosive Power, Psionic Tide, Infinite Firepower (if possible).

Note: If you have a maxed Himiko, she is an improvement over Hammurabi one to one. Later we will replace this slot entirely though as we move into Khan – Fu Fei, read more here.

Optional: skip Himiko if you do not spend enough to unlock and max Fu Fei run Theo instead of Hammurabi once you can max her.

  • Budget Alternatives: Annihilation, Spell Disintegrator, Concentration.
  • Specialization: Stormeye in combination with a Crit % artifact (for crit synergy).
  • Role: The main carry in most games, scaling damage with mage skills and chaos-like combos.

🧩 Skill & Specialization Notes

  • Assist + Lifelink: Older combos that helped tanks soak for the backline. Still usable, but weaker than before.
  • Physical Shield: Still one of the best tank skills in the game — mandatory on El Cid.
  • Weakness & Malice: Swap in depending on whether you face heavy crit or ult-reliant enemies.
  • Chaos Skills (Optional): If you do spend, adding Energy Mastery or Infinite Firepower will massively improve Hammurabi’s carry potential.

🧪 How It Performs Today

  • Against Physical Teams (Alex, Hannibal, Wukong): Excellent. Double tank front plus El Cid’s shields give strong survivability.
  • Against Earth (Alex + Charles + Himiko): Performs decently, though Himiko scaling eventually pressures you.
  • Against Fire & Water Mage Teams: Struggles. Without Chaos regen or burst skills, mages can cut through sustained defense.
  • Arena & Conquest: Still a solid march for spenders who want reliability and flexibility without Chaos investment.

🏆 Conclusion

Double Tank Lightning may no longer be the undisputed king of Infinity Kingdom, but it remains a strong, spender-friendly build in Conquest.

  • It’s budget competitive: no Chaos immortals or legendary skills required to work.
  • It’s reliable against physical-heavy metas, with strong counters to Alex/Hannibal teams.
  • It’s flexible, allowing for crit builds on Khan or ramp setups for Hammurabi.
  • Its main weakness is against top-tier mage comps, but with careful play and future Lightning supports like Xiaoxiao, Double Tank Lightning could see a full revival.

👉 If you’re a spender looking for a safe, flexible, and competitive setup without going full whale, Double Tank Lightning is still one of the best options available.

description: Unleashing the Power of Immortal Darius: A Comprehensive GuideThe latest update in Infinity Kingdom has introduced a new powerhouse, Immortal Darius, who is now available as a reward in the Legion of Frostborne Season’s Conquest P5. In this guide, we’ll delve into the remarkable abilities of Darius
html:
Unleashing the Power of Immortal Darius: A Comprehensive Guide
The latest update in Infinity Kingdom has introduced a new powerhouse, Immortal Darius, who is now available as a reward in the Legion of Frostborne Season’s Conquest P5. In this guide, we’ll delve into the remarkable abilities of Darius and provide insights on how to make the most of his incredible powers on the battlefield.

On Paper: Unveiling the Potential
On paper, Darius is an exceptionally powerful immortal with a set of abilities that make him a formidable force. His ultimate ability deals 360% physical damage to all enemies in a full area of effect, making him one of the few immortals capable of such widespread devastation. Additionally, his ultimate has a 30% chance to reduce the physical damage dealt by enemies by 30% for 6 seconds.

Darius’s first skill cast is equally impressive, as it doubles down on his utility by reducing the enemy’s physical attack by a whopping 60%. This attribute makes him particularly potent against the current meta, which is predominantly dominated by physical attack damage from Earth-Wind hybrid builds and Holy builds. His abilities synergize seamlessly with the concept of Lightning elemental builds, as Darius is of the Lightning element and deals additional damage to Earth immortals. This combination, along with his ability to carry Khan with wounds, provides players with a variety of tools to combat physical damage-oriented builds.

In Testing: A Force to be Reckoned With
In practice, Darius lives up to the hype. He performs exceptionally well on the battlefield and aligns with the expectations set by his on-paper capabilities. Darius can deal staggering amounts of damage to enemies while his damage reduction debuff effectively counters physical damage-based opponents, particularly those who aim to deal damage at the outset of the battle, such as hybrid builds.

However, it’s important to note that Darius appears to be somewhat fragile and can be taken down quickly. To mitigate this vulnerability, players should focus on building his defenses. There are two main approaches to consider: equipping single-immortal defense skills on Darius for greater durability or creating a balanced build by incorporating defense from other support immortals and emphasizing damage skills on Darius himself.

Building for Success: Strategies and Synergies

  1. Defense-Centric Build: To maximize Darius’s survivability, equip him with single-immortal defense skills. These skills significantly enhance his ability to withstand enemy attacks, making him a formidable presence on the battlefield.
  2. Balanced Build: Alternatively, you can adopt a balanced approach by leveraging Darius’s high damage output. Pair him with other support immortals who can boost his defenses and focus on his damage-dealing skills. Running skills like Anger, Toxin Barrier, Desire of Life, and energy regeneration can be incredibly effective in this setup.
  3. Synergies: Darius synergizes particularly well with the shadow immortal, Bjorn. Bjorn provides additional damage buffs and enhances Darius’s defensive capabilities, creating a dynamic duo. Consider investing in builds that guarantee Guard will activate on Darius 100% of the time, especially if you have access to immortals like Bjorn or Tokugawa. This combination has the potential to become a top-tier build in the current meta.


Immortal Darius is a game-changer in Infinity Kingdom, offering players the opportunity to harness unmatched area-of-effect damage and crowd control. When used strategically and in the right team compositions, he can be an invaluable asset on the battlefield. Experiment with different build approaches and synergies to unlock the full potential of this electrifying new immortal. Darius has arrived, and he’s here to make a thunderous impact!

title: Lightning Immortals
description: Lightning element is the counter to earth. This is primarily what drives the strenght of the element. It is not very strong in PVE content, so you should go earth/water for gnome farming and fire/water for boss killing.
html:
Lightning element is the counter to earth. This is primarily what drives the strenght of the element. It is not very strong in PVE content, so you should go earth/water for gnome farming and fire/water for boss killing.

What it does extreemly well however, is counter earth teams. Most servers see a ton of water mains in the beginning, then moving into more and more earth mains. This is because earth is the third cheapest march to build out (first being water and fire) and because many people build earth mains to counter all the water teams.

Lightning is a PVP element. As stated, it has elemental bonuses when fighting earth, but it also performs very well versus other teams and is one of (if not THE) strongest setup versus holy, provided you unlock Genghis Khan.

  • Genghis Khan provides wounds debuff to the enemy, which means the enemy team cannot recieve any healing. This is extreemly powerful and hard counters water dragon and holy dragon as well as all healers such as e.g. Zenobia and Theodora.
  • Peter the Great is one of the best physical damage dealers in the game, putting his front line opponent under heavy dmg pressure. Additionally, his despell ability provides insane value in PVP encounters, when playing against teams with shields and/or buffs.

YSG is decent IF you choose to build towards the assist-meta, because he has strong defenses from his skill. This means that he can be running assist passive to protect Genghis Khan (Genghis Khan is squichy and dies quickly).

Richard and Cid are the only other epic front line immortals for lightning. However, none of them are particularly good right now.
In the future, Richards new artifact may make him viable to use. Likewise, IF you are playing lightning to counter physical damage setups (in a physical damage meta) Cid could potentially be strong, also given artifact. At the moment of writing however, I prefer to run an out-side-element immortal as the 4th spot in lightning. Strong candidates for the spot are: Bjorn, Attila and Hippolyta.

Highlighted Lightning Immortals

Genghis Khan

Ultimate skill: Arrow Storm
Inflicts Physical Damage (damage rate 440%) to all enemies, and couses Would-enemies cannot be healed for 10 seconds.

Scaling:
Damage rate – 132% / 176% / 220% / 264% / 308% / 352% / 396% / 440%

Peter the Great

Ultimate skill: Mighty Thunder
Purifies the enemy targets directly ahead, despelling all buffs and inflicting Physical Damage (damage rate 550%).

Scaling:
Damage rate – 165% / 220% / 275% / 330% / 385% / 440% / 495% / 550%

Richard I

Ultimate skill: Heaven’s Wrath
Inflicts Physical Damage on enemy targets within a certain range (Damage Rate 170%) and has a 40% chance of Stunning them so that they cannot move or recover Energy for 4s.

Scaling:
Damage rate – 51% / 68% / 85% / 102% / 119% / 136% / 153% / 170%
Silence Rate – 12% / 16% / 20% / 24% / 28% / 32% / 36% / 40%

Speculation: Reportedly, a “certain range” means 3/4 immortals with the diagonal enemy being “out of range”. Please contact me if you prove/disprove this!

El Cid

Ultimate skill: Conquest
Reduces the physical damage inflicted on your front row teoops by 9%, and when they are targeted by normal attacks, there’s a 65% chance of inflicting physical damage on the enemy (damage rate 30%) for 12s.

Scaling:
Damage rate – 30% / 40% / 50% / 60% / 70% / 80% / 90% / 100%

Recieved damage reduction:
Damage rate – 9% / 12% / 15% / 18% / 21% / 24% / 27% / 30%

Louis IX

Ultimate skill: Howling Thunder
Replaces magical attacks with your own physical attacks and have a 55% chance to trigger lightning with each attack, dealing magical damage to the target and 1-2 nearby units (damage rate 60%) and increasing the magical damage they recieve by 6% for 3s.

Scaling:
Damage rate – 60% / 80% / 100% / 120% / 140% / 160% / 180% / 200%

Recieved damage reduction:
Damage rate – 6% / 8% / 10% / 12% / 14% / 16% / 18% / 20%

This build in full F2P beats my main earth-wind hybrid and my holy-charles.

Immortal Setup – how does it work?

This setup is built to counter earth-pure, earth-wind-hybrids and holy (w or w/o Charles). It relies on Khan to deal large amounts of damage while being protected by YSG and Charles. It also works well, because of how strong the wounds debuff that Khan applies is. Would negates 100% of all healing effects on the target (besides shields and blocks). This means, Theodora or Zeno healing is reduces to 0%.

Furthermore, your YSG debuffs your enemies making them take additional physical damage from all three of your DPS Immortals + also it is important to note, that YSG transfers phys and magic defense, meaning he is an amazing Immortal to run Assist on, as he has insanely strong defense stats when we steals from the enemy!

You want to run Peter for his off-dps (he will deal around 2x more than YSG and around half of what Khan does). But he is important because he despells all buffs from our enemies. This means, Grace effects and shields from Charles.

Lastly, you want Charles as your last Immortal. Charles is amazing for his defense support. He is the strongest support Immortal in the game, simply because he cannot be hard countered by applying wounds. His shields will keep you safe for a long time!

If you run this on a budget and can’t be asked to farm Charles for free – then you can run is with Richard. Just make sure you have enough energy regen tech to have him stun before dragon hits. If you do not have enough tech to do that, you MUST run Richard with Adrenaline Rush.

Passive loadout

You want to run this passive loadout:

Yi Seong Gye: Assist + Absolute Defense + Malice

Genghis Khan: Anger + Energy Burst + Death Breath

Peter: Fighting Will + Shelter + Physical Defense (because we are countering earth and holy).

Charles/Richard: Oaken Guard + Coercion + Adrenaline Rush

html:
Hey everyone! Today, we’re diving into Earth teams, one of the most durable and well-rounded builds in Infinity Kingdom. While Earth teams are often known for their tankiness, there’s a lot more depth to them. Earth is a powerhouse because it blends high single-target damage from Alexander, AoE damage from Cleopatra (and later Himiko or Bathory), sustain from the Earth Dragon’s damage reduction, Zenobia’s healing, and Charles’ insane shielding. On top of all that, the Earth Dragon brings some serious control with its stuns.

Stunning isn’t just about stopping an opponent for a moment; it can actually interrupt skill casts. When an immortal reaches max Energy, they start casting their ultimate. Their Energy gets drained at the start, and there’s a brief cast time before the ability activates. If you land a stun during this window, the cast is canceled, and they lose their Energy. This is why Earth is so strong—its consistent stuns (especially with Bathory added later) give you a solid chance to interrupt key ultimates.

Now, let’s get into the details of how to build Earth, from early preparation all the way into late-game seasons.

Is Earth Right for You?

Before we get too deep, let me be clear: Earth is NOT a Free-to-Play (F2P) friendly build. If you’re not willing to spend at least a little (to get Charles, who is pretty cheap these days), you should consider Earth-Wind Hybrid, Lightning, or Fire instead. If you’re set on Earth, though, let’s break it down step by step.

Earth Team Progression

1. Preparation Phase (First Weeks of the Server)

Your priority is to get these four immortals as fast as possible:

  • Zenobia (Healer)
  • Cleopatra (AoE Mage)
  • Alexander (Frontline DPS)
  • Charles (Tank, Shields)

This gives you a well-rounded team with sustain, damage, and control. During preparation, Earth is very common, and troop stats are still low, making burst damage extremely strong. Because of this, adding Genghis Khan as a temporary replacement for Cleopatra can be devastating due to his high burst and Wounds effect (which reduces healing).

2. Early Game Build Choices

  • If you want to dominate early wars: Use Khan-Zenobia-Alex-Charles.
  • If you’re a spender: You can get Bathory early through the VIP shop and Marketplace and use Cleo-Bathory-Alex-Charles.
  • If you’re following meta trends: Stick with Zenobia-Cleo-Alex-Charles, then swap Cleo for Himiko once available.

Bathory works well until Castle 39 (C39) when you unlock Assist, making her even stronger. However, as Shadow immortals become available (~3-4 weeks in via Theia’s Roulette), Himiko becomes the best Earth AoE option.

3. Mid-Game (Around 3-4 Weeks In)

Once Himiko is available, the strongest Earth team becomes:

  • Himiko (AoE Mage, Control)
  • Zenobia (Healer, Sustain)
  • Alexander (Frontline DPS, Lifesteal)
  • Charles (Tank, Shields)

This is one of the best Earth builds, viable all the way through Conquest. It provides:

  • Excellent sustain (Zenobia + Charles)
  • High AoE and burst damage (Himiko + Alex)
  • Reliable CC and interrupts (Earth Dragon + Himiko)

If you still want to use Bathory instead of Himiko, Cleo-Bathory-Alex-Charles remains solid and Theodora-Bathory-Alex-Charles becomes incredibly powerful. In fact, if you build it right (by baiting Himiko’s control onto Zenobia), it counters Himiko teams.

4. Late Game (After Conquest Starts)

Once Executioner and Blade Vortex skills become available, Bathory makes a comeback. Her synergy with late-game skills is very strong, making her a viable swap-in over Himiko for certain matchups.

Best Skills for an Earth Team

A common mistake players make is wasting Purple Crystals on skills that won’t be used in the long term. Here’s a safe skill progression path to follow:

Zenobia (Sustain & Defense)

  • Early: Berserk, Resist, Oaken Guard
  • Late: Energy Shield, Spring of Life (for better sustain)

Cleopatra/Himiko (AoE Damage)

  • Early: Concentration, Toxic Nova, Chase or Fire Nova (depends on crit rate)
  • Late: Drop a Nova for Dragon’s Breath (DB) and the other for Annihilation

Alexander (DPS & Lifesteal)

  • Early: Cleave, Combo, Duel Master
  • Late: Keep Cleave/Combo, but upgrade as new KvK and Triss skills become available

Charles (Tank & Shielding)

  • Early: Adrenaline Rush, Fighting Master, Malice
  • Late: Swap Malice for No Escape and Weakening Curse (for late-game debuff control)

Final Thoughts

Earth is an amazing all-rounder build, with sustain, damage, control, and durability. It performs well in all phases of the game but requires some investment to truly shine.

Summary Progression Path:

  1. Start with Zenobia, Cleopatra, Alexander, and Charles.
  2. Use Khan early (optional) for burst-heavy fights.
  3. Swap Cleopatra for Himiko once Theia’s Roulette unlocks her.
  4. Stick with Himiko-Zeno-Alex-Charles as your core build.
  5. Consider Bathory later for a late-game switch.
  6. Follow the skill progression path to avoid wasting Purple Crystals.

By following this guide, you’ll be able to maximize your Earth team’s potential and stay competitive across all seasons. Adapt your build based on your server’s meta and your playstyle, and you’ll dominate battles in no time!

Good luck, and see you on the battlefield! 🚀

title: Basic Fire Build – How to Build Fire from Preparation into Seasons
description: Hey there, fellow Infinity Kingdom player! Today, I’m going to walk you through my approach to building and preparing a Fire team as we move through the preparation stages and into the early seasons (especially Season 1). Fire is one of my favorite elements to play because it’s packed with high-impa
html:
Hey there, fellow Infinity Kingdom player! Today, I’m going to walk you through my approach to building and preparing a Fire team as we move through the preparation stages and into the early seasons (especially Season 1). Fire is one of my favorite elements to play because it’s packed with high-impact damage, strong control, and a lot of flexibility in how you build your lineup. Whether you’re free-to-play (F2P), a mid-tier spender, or somewhere in between, Fire can make a huge impact in large-scale PvP. Let’s dive in!

Why Choose Fire?

Fire has always been appealing due to its massive burst damage and the potential for surprisingly strong control setups. Even if you’re on the losing side of a rally or a large battle, the Fire Dragon’s breath and your Immortals’ fast burst abilities often ensure you still deal meaningful damage. This makes Fire extremely accessible for F2P and mid-tier players who want a team that consistently leaves its mark.

Another big perk is that Fire is effectively the only “true” free-to-play element in Infinity Kingdom. You can build a complete Fire lineup from scratch without spending money, thanks to Gilgamesh or Cyrus (obtainable through King of the Hill and other in-game activities). Granted, it won’t let you outclass top-tier spenders, but it does give you the highest possible ceiling for a F2P build.

For mid-tier spenders, Fire is also a great choice, especially later in the game when you can combat whale-level Shadow or Holy teams more effectively. Historically, Fire was even the go-to meta for some top players before certain nerfs and adjustments, which shows just how potent it can be.

Early Progress and Immortal Choices

During the preparation stage and early seasons, you’ll likely start piecing together your Fire Immortals and gradually refine their skills.

Right now, the biggest challenge is that Wu Zetian can be a bit harder to obtain compared to before because other immortals have become faster to build. However, she remains incredibly powerful, and you do get her for free over time, so it’s worth the investment if you plan to run Fire.

To fill in gaps while you’re building Wu Zetian, you can use other spellcaster immortals like Merlin, Medb, or Gilgamesh in the meantime.

Read more on alternative immortals here.

I personally spent a bit to unlock Seondeok for my backline, but with her recent nerf, I’m leaning more toward switching to Cyrus later on. That said, Seondeok can be very convenient early in the game because she’s easy to get from the Golden Path and Daily Coins store.

Recommended Fire Compositions

Below are some composition goals you can aim for as you head into Season 1. These examples are tailored to varying budgets, so you can pick whatever best fits your style:

  1. Wu, Seondeok, Trajan, Hippolyta
  2. Wu, Cyrus, Trajan, Hippolyta

Or, for more free-to-play oriented versions:

  1. Wu, Cyrus, William, Hippolyta
  2. Wu, Gilgamesh (or Medb), William, Hippolyta

These lineups give you high burst potential and some control, especially if you decide to emphasize Cyrus’s stuns or Seondeok’s crit bursts.

Note that before you unlock unique artifacts, you can run highly succesful fire setups without Hippo by stacking crit synergies. Note that this guide is from before unique artifacts where released. Once you obtain Unique Artifacts you should revert into a Hippo-Trajan frontline if possible or run a William-Hippo frontling. Read more about the old crit-build here.

Skill Selection and Early Game Strategy

Fire teams depend on skill synergy, so unlocking and placing the right skills early on is crucial. Many skills you pick up for Fire can later transition to a secondary or hybrid lineup as you gather better Fire-specific skills. Some early and universally useful skills to invest in include Combo, Onslaught, Wisdom, Rage, Adrenaline Rush, Blessing of War, Blessing of Defense, Fighting Master, Oaken Guard, Resist, Berserk, Toxic Nova, Chaotic Blade, and Chase.

Once you start unlocking more advanced skills, consider Malice, Weakness, Energy Suppression, and Rage Blessing for your Fire team, gradually moving older skills like Onslaught and Combo onto your hybrid lineup. If you opt for a Cyrus-based control team, you might want to grab Purification and Assist to handle debuffs and prolong battles, which can be a lifesaver against powerful Shadow teams.

Personally, I’m picking up Demonic Contract and Purification from the Wisdom Well. If you’re on a tight budget, don’t worry—you can wait until these skills appear in cheaper five-day bundles later on.

Planning for Season 1

I’m excited to test both Seondeok and Cyrus builds when I hit Season 1. These are my current skills working pretty well as I am leveling into the later levels of the Tower of Knowledge.

Here’s a peek at how I am going to re-arrange their skills once possible:

  • Cyrus Version
    • Wu Zetian: Annihilation, Chase, Fighting Master
    • Cyrus: Assist, Weakness, Oaken Guard (or Resist), and possibly Purification later
    • Trajan: Energy Suppression, Blessing of Rage, Malice
    • Hippolyta: Adrenaline Rush, Demonic Rage (plus possibly Death Breath or Energy Burst)
  • Seondeok Version
    • Wu Zetian: Annihilation, Chase, Rage
    • Seondeok: Fighting Master, Anger, Adrenaline Rush
    • Hippolyta: Malice, Energy Burst, Death Breath
    • Trajan: Weakness, Rage Blessing, Energy Suppression

I’m still experimenting with Demonic Contract to see whether it fits better on Wu, Seondeok, or Hippolyta. Results will vary depending on how quickly the battles end, so I’ll keep testing and refining the lineup.

An Older, Proven Free-to-Play Setup

If you want a tried-and-tested option without fussing over the newer skill changes, you can use something like:

  • Seondeok (or Gilgamesh) with Death Breath, Anger, Fighting Master
  • Empress Wu with Annihilation, Chase/Concentration, Toxin Nova
  • Hippolyta with Weakness, Oaken Guard, Blessing of War
  • William (or Trajan) with Malice, Energy Suppression, Blessing of Rage/Fighting Will

This setup has proven effective in the past, although I believe you can squeeze out even more power with the newer strategies mentioned above.

Dragon Focus

Don’t forget that your Fire Dragon is a critical part of this element’s power. Focus on upgrading the dragon’s breath attack first, then the passive skill, and lastly its crit modifier. As the game progresses, you’ll unlock more specializations for the dragon, but we’ll talk about that in a future guide once I have some in-season experience to share.

Summary

Building a Fire team in Infinity Kingdom is a blast. It gives you massive burst damage, potent control options, and an accessible path to endgame viability—especially for F2P or mid-tier spenders. You can adapt your composition and skills to fit your budget and playstyle, whether that means going all-in on Wu Zetian’s magic damage, focusing on Cyrus’s stuns and control, or mixing in Seondeok’s crit bursts to keep your opponents off-balance.

As you head into Season 1 or beyond, remember to prioritize skill synergy and keep refining your Immortal lineup. The flexibility of Fire means you have plenty of room to experiment, and if you invest wisely in Immortals and skills, you’ll find yourself well-prepared for the challenges ahead. Good luck, and may your Fire Dragon’s flames scorch all who stand in your way!

title: Basic Hybrid Build – How to build Hybrid from Preperation into seasons
description: The Earth-Wind Hybrid build has been a dominant force since its inception in the early seasons. It remains a popular choice due to its ability to challenge high-spending players without requiring as much investment. While it is possible to run this build as a free-to-play player, achieving peak perf
html:
The Earth-Wind Hybrid build has been a dominant force since its inception in the early seasons. It remains a popular choice due to its ability to challenge high-spending players without requiring as much investment. While it is possible to run this build as a free-to-play player, achieving peak performance will take time, especially when it comes to maxing out Immortals and unique artifacts.

The key to the Hybrid build’s success lies in artifacts. While it is functional in a preparation server, its true power only emerges when all four Immortals have their unique artifacts. Scaling attack speed to extreme levels is what makes this setup shine. Additionally, you need high-level Tower of Knowledge skills to fully optimize its potential. The good news is that the necessary skills and artifacts are available within the preparation server limits (under c40), making it a viable long-term investment as you progress through the tiers.

Once fully online, this build excels because it utilizes two powerful normal-attack Immortals—Alexander and Hannibal Barca—who synergize with Qin Shi Huang and Zenobia, both of whom provide game-changing buffs to normal attacks, especially when enhanced by their unique artifacts.

Core Hybrid Build Progression (Preparation Phase)

As you work towards a complete Hybrid build, aim for the following Immortal and skill setup:

  • Alexander the Great: Duel Master, Combo, Absorb/Physical Shield (for defense) or Heavenly Thunder (for offense).
  • Hannibal Barca: Cleave, Anger, Malice Aura (swap to Fighting Master if facing strong control setups).
  • Zenobia: Berserk Aura, Blessing of Speed, Oaken Guard.
  • Emperor Qin Shi Huang: Coercion Aura, Blessing of War, Blessing of Defense.

Early Game Adjustments:

  • Use Onslaught on Barca before acquiring Malice.
  • Silence or Instigation can provide early crowd control on Zenobia or Qin until better Tower of Knowledge skills are unlocked.

Once you hit late-game your hybrid will remain extreemly powerful and highly competitive – checkout my guides for higher level Hybrid Builds here on the page!

The Importance of Unique Artifacts

The unique artifacts are essential for unlocking the full potential of the Hybrid build. Prioritize obtaining unique artifacts for all four Immortals first, as they provide exclusive bonuses that dramatically increase their power.

Artifact Prioritization:

  • Alexander & Hannibal Barca: Rapid Bonus artifacts with physical attack as the main stat.
  • Qin & Zenobia: Surge Bonus artifacts.
  • Once all four have their unique artifacts, focus on upgrading Alexander’s artifact first, followed by Hannibal’s. If you obtain two strong artifacts for both, upgrade them simultaneously, but ensure Hannibal’s artifact has at least a unique physical damage top stat.

Why Hybrid Works as a Primary or Secondary Build

One of the major advantages of Hybrid is that it does not require as many premium Tower of Knowledge skills compared to other meta setups. This makes it an excellent secondary team option that can complement any main build.

The core attack speed skills (Berserk, Speed Blessing) and normal attack modifiers (Cleave, Combo) are rarely used outside of Hybrid. This means that even if you are running another main setup, investing in Hybrid will not drain key skills from your primary build.

TIP: Think About Team Synergy

When planning your first and second team, Hybrid is an excellent choice because it efficiently utilizes skills that do not interfere with other strong compositions.

Conclusion

The Hybrid build is one of the best long-term investments for players of all spending levels. While it takes time to reach its peak potential, the payoff is immense, allowing you to take on stronger opponents with a well-balanced setup. By focusing on obtaining unique artifacts and optimizing attack speed synergy, this build will carry you far into the seasons, whether as a main or secondary lineup.

Start building your Hybrid team early, invest in the right artifacts and skills, and you’ll have a powerhouse formation ready to challenge the best in the game!

title: Basic Lightning Build – How to Build Lightning from Preperation into Seasons
description: Lightning may seem like a build that requires heavy spending due to the power of Genghis Khan, Louis, and Tokugawa, but in reality, it is one of the best Free-to-Play (F2P) friendly setups in the game. Lightning offers a highly effective alternative build that can be strong even without massive inve
html:
Lightning may seem like a build that requires heavy spending due to the power of Genghis Khan, Louis, and Tokugawa, but in reality, it is one of the best Free-to-Play (F2P) friendly setups in the game. Lightning offers a highly effective alternative build that can be strong even without massive investment. In this guide, we’ll go over how to use Lightning early on and how to adjust and improve it through the seasons.

Early Days in Preparation

Lightning teams are extremely versatile, which makes them one of the best options for F2P players and low spenders. Unlike some other elements that have rigid compositions, Lightning allows for multiple competitive setups.

Early Game Lineup Options to aim for as you develop and summon new Immortals:

  • Frontline: Richard & Tokugawa or Richard & Peter
  • Backline: Louis & Tokugawa (solid starter combo) OR YSG & Gilgamesh (if you get lucky with summons)
  • Alternative: If you pull Hammurabi early, he can be a fantastic backline addition.

Genghis Khan is obviously one of the most powerful backline damage dealers, but you can perform well without him. If you get Gilgamesh or Hammurabi early on, you can substitute him in until you acquire Khan. The beauty of Lightning is that many of its key immortals are accessible through events, summons, and the Golden Path.

Understanding the Lightning Dragon

One of the most important things to keep in mind when running Lightning is how the Lightning Dragon‘s passive works. Every time you apply a debuff to the enemy, you gain a stacking damage buff. This means that skills like Novas, Garrote, and Chaotic Blade are extremely valuable because they trigger the Lightning Dragon’s bonus damage.

If you build your Lightning team without enough debuffs, you’re leaving a lot of damage on the table. Prioritize immortals and skills that help stack the dragon buff.

Skill Setup for Early Game

I was asked by a player using this to recommend progression for him. I think this information could be valuable for others building their lightning.Player is using these now (image below) which are quite good to be honest. I would recommend that Peter or alternatively Louis is better suited for some debuffs.

Dropping Life-Link and Duel Master for Garrote and Chaotic Blade will serve well. Remember to position him not against enemy Alexanders.

  • Genghis Khan: Anger, Adrenaline Rush, Fighting Master
  • YSG: Coercion, Assist, Absolute Defense
  • Richard/Tokugawa: Oaken Guard, Sacrifice, Rage Blessing
  • Peter/Louis: Malice, Chaotic Blade, Garrote

Notes:

  • If you’re running Gilgamesh instead of Genghis Khan, build him with Anger, Chaotic Blade, and Garrote. Then move Physical Shield and another defensive skill to Louis/Peter.
  • If using Louis, he should focus on debuffs like Weakness, Chaotic Blade, and Garrote (until Executioner and Blade Vortex become available).

Mid to Late Game Lightning Progression

As you move into later stages of the game, your goal should be to secure Hammurabi and optimize your damage output. A strong mid-game Lightning team could look like this:

  • Hammurabi: Annihilation, Nova, Chase/Concentration (based on crit tech)
  • Genghis Khan: Death Breath, Anger, Adrenaline Rush
  • Richard/Tokugawa: Oaken Guard, Malice, Energy Suppression/Life Link (Defense vs. Offense)
  • Louis/Peter:
    • If using Peter: Fighting Will, Weakness, Cleave
    • If using Louis: Weakness, Chaotic Blade, Garrote (until Executioner & Blade Vortex become available)

Progression Notes:

  • Mid-Game Buffs: Garrote and Chaotic Blade become even stronger as your dragon gets better.
  • End-Game Adaptation: Louis can be swapped out for Khubilai Khan once Holy comes out, giving a substantial boost.
  • Late KVK Skills: Executioner & Blade Vortex become core picks, making Louis even more devastating.

Final Thoughts

Lightning is an extremely fun and flexible team to play, with strong early-game performance and great adaptability through the seasons. While the spender-builds will have a natural edge, F2P and low-spenders can still build highly competitive Lightning teams by focusing on debuff stacking, dragon synergy, and skill optimization.

If you want to play a F2P-friendly, high-damage setup that scales well into the later stages of the game, Lightning is a fantastic choice. Get started, experiment with your summons, and adapt your strategy as your server evolves!
