Title: Pirate Festival 2023: Cost, Value, and Player Choices

The Pirate Festival, an annual seasonal event, has set sail once again, bringing with it a treasure trove of rewards for players. In previous years, participants could acquire coveted items like the Bon Voyage skin. This year, the event offers new frame and chatbox designs, making it a must-attend occasion for collectors and enthusiasts.

Daily Rewards: The festival spoils players with daily sign-in rewards, including 5 Explosive Cannonballs, 300 gems, one 8-hour bubble, and three philosopher stones.

Daily Tasks: As part of the festival experience, daily tasks present players with a series of objectives such as training troops, engaging in the Well of Time 50 times, and summoning immortals. Completing these tasks yields rewards, notably 5 Athena shards per day. It’s worth noting that these tasks are time-sensitive, disappearing once the day rolls over. Completion of all tasks is required to claim the rewards. Some players may find the speedups and action points required for these tasks not worthwhile unless they are specifically building Athena or have surplus resources.

Missions and Bounty: The Pirate Festival introduces missions that send immortals on elemental requirement-based quests and tasks players with eliminating gnome camps. These missions and tasks offer cannonball crafting materials and various speedups as rewards. Each completed mission or task earns stars that accumulate and can be redeemed for rewards such as cannonballs, cannonball crafting materials, and speedups. Tasks can be refreshed for free every hour or for 20 gems.

Ocean of the Dead: A central feature of the festival is the Ocean of the Dead, where players utilize two types of cannonballs, Explosive and Solid, each with a 25% chance of dealing double damage. Solid Shots deal 20 damage, while Explosive Shots deal 50 damage on average. Based on these statistics, it can be inferred that every Explosive Shot is equivalent to 2.5 Solid Shots, and thus, every Solid Shot is valued at 40 gems.

The festival introduces progressively challenging levels, each with varying HP requirements.

Levels
1 – 50 HP
2 – 70 HP
3 – 90 HP
4 – 110 HP
5 – 130 HP
6 – 150 HP
7 – 170 HP
8 – 200 HP
9 – 230 HP
10 – 260 HP
11 – 290 HP
12 – 320 HP
13 – 360 HP
14 – 400 HP
15 – 450 HP
16 – 500 HP
17+ – 550 HP

Players are able to obtain some Canon Balls and Explosive Canon Balls for free, but not enough to complete the event. Gem spend is a requirement to obtain the end rewards. Let’s have a look at how much it is going to cost ya.

Please make note, that these calclations DO NOT take overkill into consideration, as such you are going to waste a little and spend just a few more. But it gives us a clear indication of what to expect.

All levels in total have 16980 HP.

Explosives and Canon Balls have their 25% chance to crit, making their avg. damage respectively 62.5 and 25 damage.

Canon Balls can be obtained in a finite number: We get 50 from Island Adventure and 50 from Kingdom Bounty. At a total of 100 canon balls with an avg. damage of 25 hence a total of 2500 damage all in all.

This will take us to around level 12-13 on it’s own. But no where near the level 40 we need if we want to complete the event. As such, we need to include some Explosive Balls! These are obtained free via Island Adventure and Kingdom Bounty, but only a total of 15 are awarded for free. Let’s see how many we need to buy using gems.

Total HP: 16980 minus 2500 damage from canon balls, divided by the avg. dmg of explosives 62.5 = gives us a total need for 232 Explosives on average with the 15 free, that means we need to buy 217 using gems = at 100 gems each that nets us a total average cost of 21.668 gems to max this event (not including overkill).

Gem cost analysis: To assess the value of the Ocean of the Dead event, we’ll consider gems, philosopher stones, and speedups (converted to their gem equivalent) since these are the primary items of interest for most players.

  • For the free path, you’d get 400 gems, 7 philosopher stones (roughly 2,100 gems based on their cost), and four 1-hour speedups (280 gems or roughly 70 gems each based on market prices) for a total of 2,780 gems of value.
  • For the 3,500 gem path, you’d get 1,600 gems, 12 philosopher stones (roughly 3,600 gems), and four 3-hour speedups (1,080 gems), totaling around 6,280 gems of value without including the exclusive artifact chest you would also get.
  • For the $20 path, you’d get 18 philosopher stones (5,400 gem value) and ten 3-hour speedups (2,700 gems value), totaling 8,100 gems. You would also get the frame, chatbox, exclusive artifact chest for Alex, and 60 chests for light and dark immortals pieces.

Conclusion: The Pirate Festival presents players with a tantalizing array of rewards, but its cost-effectiveness varies depending on individual preferences and in-game priorities. Whether the event is worth pursuing depends on your specific goals. For some, certain rewards may hold little value, while others may covet exclusive items like frames and chatboxes. Ultimately, the Pirate Festival offers an exciting opportunity for players to acquire new items and enhance their gameplay experience.

title: Pirate Festival 2025
description: Pirate Festival 2025 – Full Guide & Skin Breakdown
html:
Pirate Festival 2025 – Full Guide & Skin Breakdown

The Pirate Festival is back, and if you’ve played Harvest Festival before, you’ll feel right at home. It’s basically the same structure, just with pirate flavor on top. The main difference this year is in the rewards: a new Sun Chariot City Skin and, more importantly, Abyssal Throne fragments are now available in the event pass. That’s in my opinion the real big reward for this event, since it means I can slowly build up Abyssal without having to whale on rankings. Very nice!

So yeah, the event itself isn’t anything groundbreaking, but the rewards make it worth paying attention to. Anyways, lets get into the details.

General Event Info

This is one of those seasonal grind events with multiple parts running at the same time: daily quests, challenges, PvE fights, spins, and a final shop. If you’re used to Harvest Festival, it’s the same thing in practice. The only thing that changes from year to year are the skins and which rewards get put into the pool.

Event Content & Mechanics

1. Daily Sign-in

Log in every day, grab Tokens of Light, and toss them into Dazzling Wish. Free spins are always worth it, just don’t expect miracles. If you hit the Chaos Immortal jackpot or the skin fragments, congrats — that’s pure luck.

2. Battle Pass

Same daily quest pass as always.

  • You can skip one quest per day or even miss one full day and still complete it.
  • The $50 premium tier unlocks the Sun Chariot skin.

Sun Chariot, any good?

The march speed here is surprisingly good. Normally defensive skins use troop death rate reduction, but march speed makes this skin more flexible.
I think that Move speed is the best secondary stat (meaning outside of attack or defense) because you are able to hit the enemy and recall before the enemy lands. That means you can fight with a huge advantage as you can recall your main before an enemy hits you).
Could be the best defensive option so far, but it really depends on your setup, for defensive late game setups, this may prove better than Abyssals Attack if upgraded.

More Abyssal Flame!

The fragments you collect while progressing the pass are actually Abyssal Throne, not Sun Chariot. That’s nice, because it means you’re building toward something long-term instead of adding yet another half-finished skin to your list.

3. Glorious Challenge

Exactly the same as always. The only tip is: save your extra gem-attempts until Hard Mode opens. Every event, people burn them early and end up losing value. Once Hard is open, spend freely.

4. Pinnacle Trials

This is the PvE section that ends with the new Pinnacle Trial Ranking mode.

  • Top 10 players on your server show up on a ranking board.
  • Other players can challenge them to gain points and push their own ranking.

It’s more of a competitive race for high-end players, but casuals can still clear the PvE for some rewards. Think of it as a fun distraction if you’re not aiming for the leaderboard. Note that this also rewards Abyssal Throne fragments, thus another avenue to obtain these fragments if you are able to qualify as a top ranking player.

5. Dazzling Wish

This one got worse compared to the old version. It’s no longer cross-server, so you can’t play smart or snipe. The value just isn’t there unless you’re spending heavily.

Odds look like this:

  • Sun Chariot: 0.05%
  • Chaos Immortal Chests (80x): 0.45%
  • Chaos Artifact fragments (60x): 0.6%
  • Chaos Immortal Chests (5x): 2.5%
  • Chaos Artifact fragments (5x): 3%
  • Random Chaos Immortal fragments (1x): 6%
  • Holy/shadow Random Frags: 7.4%

Basically, for most players this is a lottery — not efficient, not worth serious money. If you’re a whale chasing Chaos or skins, you’ll still roll. Everyone else should just treat the free pulls as bonus value.

Personally I think there is a somewhat hidden gem to get the random fragments. Ofc you need a bit of luck with these, but at 6% and 7.4% the drop rate is quite frequent. If you want to rank in this event, you are going to see A LOT of random fragments and a real impact on unlock and maxing immortal progress speeds.

6. Celebration Shop

The priorities here haven’t changed:

  1. Artifacts (x3)
  2. Stardust
  3. Tokens of Light
  4. Speedups or Philosopher Stones depending on your situation

If you’re in Season 2 (or early Season 1), Philosopher Stones are more valuable because the new specialization tree eats up immortal fragments like crazy. If you’re already stacked on immortals, speedups will usually do more for you.

Final Thoughts

Pirate Festival 2025 isn’t a brand-new experience — it’s Harvest Festival with pirate cosmetics. The gameplay loop is the same, so don’t expect surprises. The interesting part is in the rewards:

  • Sun Chariot adds a genuinely solid defensive skin option.
  • Abyssal Throne is still my go-to combat skin, and now it’s more accessible through the pass.

Main advice:

  • Be patient — don’t rush unlocks, you’ll lose Pirate Marks.
  • Don’t over-invest in Dazzling Wish unless you know what you’re doing.
  • Grab Abyssal fragments wherever you can.

The event’s nothing new, but the rewards are worth grinding out if you’re serious about skins.

title: Serpent’s Gaze Awakens (November 2025)
description: A breakdown of rewards, value, and how to make the most out of the event.
html:
A breakdown of rewards, value, and how to make the most out of the event.

Alright, so Serpent’s Gaze Awakens landed today on friday the 14th of november 2025. If you’ve played the last few seasonal events, the structure will feel familiar, but there’s a huge twist this time: the Grail Shop.

The whole thing runs for 10 days, which is long enough that even if you miss a few tasks, you can still walk away with a ton of value. And honestly, this event is pretty friendly to low spenders and free-to-play, because Tokens of Light never expire and Eternal Grails carry over. So nothing feels “wasted” if you can’t push everything.

This guide digs into every part of the event, but also explains why certain pieces are worth doing and what type of player benefits most from each one.

Event Overview

  • Duration: Nov 14 → Nov 23 (10 days total)
  • Main Components:
    • Daily Sign-In
    • Koi Gift Pack system
    • Corridor of Ghostflame Battle Pass
    • Glorious Challenge
    • Pinnacle Trial
    • Dazzling Wish
    • Grail Shop (new)
    • Celebration Shop

Some pieces are quick “grab and go” value, and some are serious time or gem sinks. If you want to stretch your rewards, the trick is knowing which sections your account can realistically handle.

Koi Gift Pack & Daily Sign-In

This is the low-effort, high-reliability part of the event. Even if you do nothing else, at least grab your free Token of Light every day.

Why Tokens of Light matter

They’re used in Dazzling Wish, and here’s the important part:
Tokens do not expire.
So even if this event isn’t your focus, you’re stacking for future cycles where rewards might be better for your account.

About the Koi Gift Pack (Paid Optional)

This pack is honestly one of the best “small spender” packs in the entire game right now. For $4.99 you get:

  • 5 Tokens of Light
  • 520 Gems
  • 500 VIP Points
  • Chance at 4,250 Eternal Grails every two days

If you buy the pack five times and never win the draw, you still get 850 Grails, which equals 80 Chaos immortal shards in the Grail Shop. No other $25 spend in the game gets you Chaos shards this efficiently.

If you’re a light spender, this is the pack that feels like a no-brainer.

Corridor of Ghostflame – Battle Pass

This is your standard monthly-style Battle Pass with 30 levels and the usual daily missions.

But before you swipe the $49.99 premium pass: The skins this month are not meta-defining

  • Corridor of Ghostflame: Honor bonus
  • Mt. Paradise: March speed bonus

Marching speed sounds nice, but in practice the increase is so tiny that it’s hard to feel. And since neither of these skins gives combat stats like HP, ATK, or DEF, they don’t change PvP outcomes.

Note: It says “Peach Blossom Mountain fragments” which for some reason is the misleading name for Mt. Paradise fragments.

Free track gives:

  • 30 Tokens of Light

Premium track ($49.99) gives:

  • 58 extra Tokens
  • 60 Ghostflame Fragments
  • 30 Mt. Paradise Fragments

You need 60 fragments to make a skin, and 11 total skins to fully develop either one. So unless you’re collecting cosmetics, this pass probably isn’t worth the price for most players.

Daily missions

You get 7 missions a day for 100 EXP each, and you’ll end up with around 70 total tasks across the event. You don’t need perfect attendance to finish the pass — you can skip a few each day and still get to level 30.

Tasks include:

  • Training 40k troops (you’ll need to build more than once)
  • Arena
  • Well of Time
  • Market purchases
  • Pinnacle Trial
  • Glorious Challenge
  • Gnome bosses

Veteran tip: The troop-training missions are the only ones you might need to plan around. All the others take only a few minutes.

Glorious Challenge

This section works almost exactly like Well of Time, but with two difficulty modes and different reward currency.

Normal Mode

  • Available from day 1
  • 16 levels
  • Very easy — most players breeze through

Hard Mode

  • Unlocks on day 3
  • Similar to Elite campaigns in difficulty
  • More puzzles, more skill setups needed, more punishing

Attempts

  • 5 free attempts per day
  • Can buy up to 100 more in the shop for 8,000 Gems

Rewards

  • First clear of each stage: 50 gems
  • Raids give Serpent’s Eyes, used in the Celebration Shop

The best way to maximize value here is to save your bought attempts for Hard mode, since the cloud (Serpent’s Eyes) yield is way better there.

If you only do the free attempts, you won’t get every cosmetic, but you’ll easily get all the practical items.

Speed Rankings

This is purely for competitive players. If you’re not pushing top-of-server stats, don’t stress this part. It’s bragging rights and a leaderboard, nothing more.

Pinnacle Trial

Think of Pinnacle as the “elite version” of Glorious Challenge. It has fewer stages but better rewards.

Structure

  • 5 levels total
  • 1 attempt per day
  • No way to buy extra entries

If you clear the levels, you unlock raid for the rest of the event.

Rewards include:

  • 25 Random Immortal Fragments
  • 30 Mt. Paradise Fragments
  • 10 Tokens of Light

The difficulty jumps pretty hard in the last couple of stages because enemy marches use legendary skills. So if you’re mid-game and stuck, don’t feel bad — this mode is meant to be tough.

PvP Ranking Section

This works almost like a mini-Arena:

  • You challenge the top 10 player matches
  • You get 5 PvP attempts per day
  • Wins gain you points
  • Losses do nothing (no penalty)

End-of-event rewards (Mt. Paradise Fragments):

  • 1st — 24
  • 2nd — 18
  • 3rd — 12
  • 4th–10th — 6

If you’re not in a very active or powerful server, you might sneak into top 10 with a strong Chaos or Earth march. But in most servers, whales dominate this board.

Dazzling Wish

Okay, this one got a serious rework for this event.

What changed?

The top prizes (skins, Chaos-exclusive items) were all replaced with Eternal Grails (which can be redeemed for the same Chaos stuff):

  • 1,000
  • 500
  • 100
  • 50
  • 5

Elemental immortal fragments and Dragon Crystal chests are still in the pool.

Token usage

  • 1 token = 1 point on the leaderboard
  • 4,000 tokens guarantees the 1,000-grail pull
  • Daily top 200 get extra grails
  • Overall event top 200 get even more rewards
  • Top player gets the Femme Fatale dynamic frame

Token bundles

Cheapest tokens = best value. The ranking goes like this:

Great value:

  • $2.99
  • $4.99

Worst value:

  • $19.99
  • $49.99 (both of them)

There’s also a one-time $49.99 bundle with 25 tokens and a dynamic frame, but it’s purely for collectors.

You can also get 25 free tokens from the Celebration Shop.

Grail Shop (New System)

This is the game-changer. Eternal Grails are now a reusable currency for buying Chaos immortal shards, artifacts, and other items.

Chaos Shards

Each purchase gives 80 shards, and you can buy each immortal 20 times.

Costs:

  • 850 Grails → Medusa (new)
  • 750 Grails → Athena, Anubis, Fu Fei, Poseidon, Nine Tails, Wukong, Loki

Artifacts

  • Medusa artifact: 1,100
  • All others: 1,000

Other items

  • Forging stone chests
  • Stellar Core Crystals
  • Holy/Shadow Selection Chests
  • Artifact chests
  • Territory decoration fragments

The big thing: Grails carry over

Unlike almost every other event currency, Eternal Grails don’t expire. That means you can save for future seasonal events and release events, as I assume this will be the new default setup (but again, this is an assumption and always subject to being changed).

Celebration Shop

This shop uses Serpent’s Eyes, which come mainly from Glorious Challenge.

Priority Items (what everyone should grab)

  • 25 Tokens of Light
  • Entangle avatar frame
  • Viper chatbox
  • 2 Artifact Selection Chests
  • 600 Stardust

The cosmetics + collectibles cost 1,700 coins total.

Artifact chests are 2,000 each.
Stardust is 1,000 per 100.
Tokens of Light (all 10 sets) = 10,000 coins.

How many coins can you get?

If you do all 32 stages:

  • Normal 1–16: 1,890 coins
  • Hard 1–16: 3,670 coins
    Total: 5,560

If you skip artifact chests, you can clean out all the good items without spending gems.

If you buy the 100-ticket pack (optional gem sink)

  • Costs 8,000 Gems
  • Raiding Hard 16 gives ~28,000 coins

That’s enough to grab literally everything in the shop with room to spare.

Conclusion Summary

Serpent’s Gaze Awakens mostly follows the structure of the usual monthly event, but the introduction of the Grail Shop is a major shift. It gives players a predictable, less-RNG way to farm Chaos immortals, which is something players have needed for a long time.

Everything else in the event is useful, but the real long-term value comes from:

  • Daily Tokens of Light
  • Glorious Challenge farming
  • Eternal Grails → Chaos shards

Bottom line:
Treat this event as a long-term investment. Grab your free tokens, work through the challenges at your own pace, and put every Eternal Grail you get into Chaos immortals. The Grail Shop is the real prize here.

title: Price comparison Chaos Roulette vs Serpent’s Gaze (chaos immortal and artifacts only)
description: Cost of Chaos Immortals and Artifacts in Serpent’s Gaze vs Chaos Roulette
html:
Cost of Chaos Immortals and Artifacts in Serpent’s Gaze vs Chaos Roulette

Introduction

Chaos development is one of the biggest long-term investments in Infinity Kingdom.
Two events allow players to directly acquire Chaos immortal fragments and Chaos artifact materials:

  1. Chaos Roulette – weekly event → Eyes of Chaos → spins → fragments
  2. Serpent’s Gaze – seasonal event → Tokens → Grails → immortal fragments and artifacts

Both events reward Chaos progress, but their cost efficiency is drastically different.
This guide compares the exact value of each system so whales and high spenders can decide where their money is best spent.

Quick Recap: What We Know About Chaos Roulette (For Comparison)

Before comparing Serpent’s Gaze and Chaos Roulette, here are the core numbers from the Chaos Roulette guide — just the essentials you need to understand the value difference.

Expected immortal fragments per spin:

  • ≈ 0.434 fragments per spin
    (This already includes 4% jackpot, 25-spin pity, and the two 3% immortal slots.)

Expected artifact fragments per spin:

  • 0.09 per spin
    (Bonus bar does not add artifact fragments.)

Bonus bar efficiency:

  • Best value at 50, 100, and 200 spins
  • Worst at 350–700
  • 900 spins gives decent value because of the final 60-frag chest
  • If you care about value → stay ≤200
  • If you care about speed → go 900

Cost of a full Chaos immortal (1,640 fragments)

200-spin weekly route (value path):

  • ~14 weeks
  • Costs ≈ $1,400 total
  • ≈ $0.85 per fragment

900-spin weekly route (speed path, corrected):

  • 3 × 900-spin weeks + 1 × 200-spin week
  • Costs ≈ $1,630 total
  • ≈ $0.99 per fragment

This gives us the real comparison baseline:

Chaos Roulette immortal fragments cost between ~$0.85 and ~$0.99 each.

Chaos Roulette artifact cost

  • Requires about 667 spins per artifact
  • Costs $333–$378 depending on whether you follow 200 or 900-spin pacing
  • Much slower overall because you need ~10,000 spins for 15 artifacts
  • Causes heavy immortal-fragment overflow (5,600–6,100 frags gained in the process)

These numbers are what make Roulette excellent for immortals but inefficient for artifacts.

For the full deep-dive math, drop rates, cycle modeling, and bundle analysis, see the full guide here.

Serpent’s Gaze – Detailed Cost Breakdown

Serpent’s Gaze gives Chaos progress through the Grail Shop:

Immortals

  • Medusa: 850 grails → 80 frags
  • Others: 750 grails → 80 frags

Artifacts

  • Medusa artifact: 1100 grails → full artifact (60 frags)
  • Other Chaos artifacts: 1000 grails → full artifact (60 frags)

Grail Wheel Expected Value

Spin probability → expected grails per spin:

Total estimated value (EV): 1+0.75+0.8+0.75+0.5=3.81.

Expected grails per spin = 3.8

Token Cost — Using Only $3, $5, $10 Packs First

  • $3 → 3 tokens → $1/token
  • $5 → 5 tokens → $1/token
  • $10 → 8 tokens → $1.25/token

Let’s begin with only using the most efficient bundles, the 3 and 5 dollar ones at 1 dollar per token. Thus we have: 1 token = 3.8 grails and 1 grail costs = $1÷3.8=0.263$

Serpent’s Gaze – Cost to Buy 1640 Immortal Frags

Non-Medusa Immortals (750 grails → 80 frags)

  • Grails per fragment:
    750 / 80 = 9.375
  • Cost per fragment:
    9.375 × 0.263 = $2.47

That gets us 1,640 fragments * $2.47 = $4,041 for a full 1640 fragments this way.

Medusa (850 grails → 80 frags)

  • Grails per fragment:
    10.625
  • Cost per fragment:
    10.625 × 0.263 = $2.80

1,640×2.80= $4,592 for max star Medusa.

Serpent’s Gaze Immortal Cost Summary

For comparison, we are doing only the cheap bundles so far in the Serpents Gaze event, but we are much much less cost efficient comparing to Chaos Roulette (200–900 spin paths) which was $1,400–$1,630, meaning: Serpent’s Gaze costs 2.5x to 3x more than Chaos Roulette for immortal fragments.

Serpent’s Gaze – Artifact Cost

Artifacts in the Grail Shop:

  • 1,000 grails (most artifacts)
  • 1,100 grails (Medusa)

Cost at $0.263/grail:

  • 1,000 grails → $263
  • 1,100 grails → $289

Comparing to Roulette ($333–$378):

Serpent’s Gaze artifacts are cheaper than Chaos Roulette artifacts.

Final Comparison Table

Conclusion

When you put everything side-by-side, the pattern is actually really clear:
Chaos Roulette is the superior place to buy Chaos immortal fragments, but Serpent’s Gaze quietly becomes the best place in the entire game to buy Chaos artifacts.

Roulette gives you far better value on immortal fragments because of the pity system, the new 1-fragment drops, and the weekly bonus bar. Even the fast 900-spin route, corrected to three full weeks plus one 200-spin week, comes out around $1,630 for a full 1,640-fragment Chaos immortal. That’s miles cheaper than Serpent’s Gaze’s ~$4k price tag for the same number of fragments.

But here’s the interesting twist—for artifacts, the math completely flips.
In Chaos Roulette you need 11–12 full weeks of 900 spins (≈10,000 spins avg. total) to secure the 15 unique artifacts required for a max bonus artifact. That run gives you around 5,600-6,100 immortal fragments, which massively over-caps your Chaos immortals even if you max every talent node (4,750 fragments needed). You basically drown in immortal fragments long before you finish the artifacts.

Serpent’s Gaze doesn’t have that problem at all.
Everything is converted into Grails, and you spend those Grails in a shop where you choose exactly what to buy. That means whales can target only the Chaos artifacts they want, pay less per artifact than in Roulette, and avoid the painful over-capping of immortal fragments entirely. For high spenders optimizing Chaos development, that flexibility is huge.

So the ideal whale strategy looks like this:

  • Do Chaos Roulette for immortal fragments — it’s the best value by far.
  • Do Serpent’s Gaze for artifacts — it’s cheaper, faster, and doesn’t force you into excess immortal fragments you don’t need.

And while Serpent’s Gaze is a limited-time seasonal right now, there’s some indication (IKVIP whispers, not confirmed) that versions of the Grail Shop may return in future seasonals. If that happens, this becomes one of the best recurring artifact paths in the game for whales.

Bottom line:
Whales should build their immortals in Roulette and finish their artifacts in Serpent’s Gaze.
It’s cheaper overall, it’s cleaner, and it avoids the big inefficiencies built into Roulette’s artifact progression.

title: Spring Fiesta 2023
description: Spring is upon us in the world of Infinity Kingdom! In this guide we are going to have a look at the Spring Fiesta event and the rewards. What we need to watch out for and what you should prioritize doing for this years event!
html:
Spring is upon us in the world of Infinity Kingdom! In this guide we are going to have a look at the Spring Fiesta event and the rewards. What we need to watch out for and what you should prioritize doing for this years event!

Rewards

So this year, we are getting a pretty mediocer event for Spring Fiesta. We are not getting the discounts that we are used to from these events (especially compared to the awesome Christmas Winter Festival event) but on the other hand we do get awesome free hidden rewards.

First of all, you are able to get Attila, Saladin, El Cid or Alexander. Spending 35 Silver Lotus’.

Secondly, you can get a unique artifact for your brand new Immortal for 100 Silver Lotus’.

Third, if you are in need of dragon crystals, there are a few in there for not much cost, likewise, there are a few purple crystals to be earned.

Fourth and last, you have the usual cosmetic stuff. Getting the Nameplate, Chatbox and Profile Frame costs you a few Lotus’.

This years Spring Profusion castle skin will cost you 100 Spring Lotus’, but more importantly, it is the same box as the unique which means you are unable to get both unique artifact and event skin this time.

How does it work?

In order to unlock the good rewards for this event, you need some Spring Lotus’!

These are available in the Shop to be purchased spending real fiat currency. In addition to the event currency Spring Lotus’ you get quite awesome rewards from these bundles. Namely, Dragon Essences and a bunch of gems.

The bundles have 1 stock for the entire event, meaning you have to be careful what you spend on.

The bundles offer quite a lot of Dragon Essences at a standard price compared to the monthly bundles. As such, if you are looking to max out some dragon talents quickly then this event is an excellent opportunity to do that. However, you will not get the holy or shadow dragon crystals that we are used to from the monthly bundles.

The full event shop is as follows (one time purchases)

Cost of main rewards

So what does the big juicy rewards cost? On the face of it, it seems you are forced to purchase all bundles to get these rewards. Getting the 100 Lotus’ you need to get all bundles. Buying all other bundles than the last big 99.99$ one only gets you 90 Lotus’ as such, you are unable to get the skin or unique artifact without purchasing the entire event shop. If you do, you have 150 Lotus’ and can get skin/unique artifact + immortal unlock and a single dragon crystal box or some cosmetics.

Alternatively, you can be a bit more efficient about it and spend 3,500 gems AND making sure you complete the entire Spring Color’s side event. This in itself it pretty time consuming and spending the gems does mean you can skip on the last big box but it still costs you 85$ and 3,500 gems to obtain the unique Immortal.

If you are only looking to unlock one of the Immortals, you will need to spend 35 bucks to get the first three bundles and 60 lotus’ meaning you have 25 unspent lotus’s you can use on dragon crystals and/or cosmetics.

Alternatively, you can also complete the Spring Colors Side event thus reducing your spend to only 15$ and 3,500 gems. This is the most value you will get from the standard rewards of this event. 15$ and a few gems is good price for 60x Immortal Fragments for one of the four pay-wall Immortals.

All in all the bundle structure for this event is not very good and makes it hard to purchase anything very efficiently.

Good news! Loki for free

Despite the lackluster event reward costs of this event, there is one hidden treat in here for us. Loki!

Our favorite Chaos Immortal is hiding in the Rainy Spring tab of the event. By unlocking all five will get you a total of 40 Loki Fragments, simply by completing the daily quests that release as the event progresses. This is massive reward as Loki is currently the most expensive Immortal of all Infinity Kingdom. All players should pay careful attention to this and make sure you complete all of the quests this year!

More free rewards

This event offers some pretty good free-to-play rewards, they are very easy to get and you get decent value if you like most players need Purple Crystals and speedups.

title: Spring Fiesta 2024
description: Hey there! The Spring Fiesta 2024 in Infinity Kingdom is upon us, and it’s packed with familiar sub-events that we’ve come to know and love. Let’s dive into what this season has in store for us.
html:
Hey there! The Spring Fiesta 2024 in Infinity Kingdom is upon us, and it’s packed with familiar sub-events that we’ve come to know and love. Let’s dive into what this season has in store for us.

Rewards Tab Highlights

  • Free Tier: You can grab a full 60 fragments of Immortal selection chests for big names like Attila, Saladin, El Cid, or Alexander. Plus, up to 100 Stardust!
  • Spender Tier: For 30 Lotus, grab a full schematic for almost any Immortal’s Unique Artifact. And 60x Shadow or Holy Immortal fragments for just 75 Lotus – that’s a steal!
  • Fate of Chaos Selection Chests: Available for 75 Lotus, meaning 80 Chaos Fragments for just $20 if you play your cards right.

The event in detail

Rainy Spring

There are the usual categories of sub-events that we are used to with these seasonals. They are all very similar. For this one, we have the typical daily quests to be completed. Completing the Rainy Spring quests and getting the final reward chest will get you the main reward from this event: 40 free Chaos Immortal selection chests, here you can choose the chaos immortal you want and get 40x fragments. Very very nice and free! In addition you will get 10 silver lotus’ and some stardust, gems and other stuff from the quests. Make sure to complete this event tab during Spring Fiesta 2024.

Spring Fiesta

The second event tab is the standard ‘send your immortals on expeditions’ mini-game. Here you simply send out your immortal all day and complete the event to earn a 10 more locus and a bit of side rewards. Not bad but also not very impressive. The Lotus are going to be important though!

Gnomes and Farming Resources

For the third event tab, you got the usual: Kill gnomes and farm resources to earn free-to-play currency and buy decent rewards. Just keep playing the game, send out gnome raids and harvest your resources and nodes.

Spring Colors

The fourth event tab is the Spring Colors, again one of the usual suspects in terms of mechanics. You spend the water currency you have earned duing daily quests in the Rainy Spring (tab 1) to complete the 20 levels. The cost will increase continuously, but worry not. Just do your daily quests like you would anyway for chaos fragments and you will complete this event.

The important thing to note here are the Lotus. This is the main source of cheap Lotus currency for this years event. We get 2 in the free tier, 10 in the 2500 gem tier and a whopping 45 from the 20$ tier. Very good value! Comparitively you get only 10 Lotus spending 20$ on the Spring Fiesta bundles. So make sure you complete this event and buy the 20$ tier if you are looking for the main rewards from this years event!

Bundles:

Rewards in more detail

The rewards tab: Here you redeem event currency for big rewards. Let’s look at the highlights here. First up, for FREE you can farm and buy a full 60 fragments of Immortal selection chests for Attila, Saladin, El Cid or Alexander. A free full Immortal unlock (i.e. 60x fragments). Moreover, you can farm your way to a whopping 100 Stardust!

In the spender tier we have the Lotus rewards. For 30 Lotus you can get a full schematic for basically any of your Immortal’s Unique Artifact. They are almost all in there and 30 Lotus, quit cheap! You can get that in the 20$ tier alone! Insane.

Moreover, you can buy 60x Shadow or Holy Immortal fragments for just 75 Lotus. Not too bad and quite cheap! With the 45 from the 20$ event tier, 10 from the 2500 gem tier, 10 from the Spring Fiesta, 10 from the Rainy Spring you are home safe! Just 20$ and you can get a full Holy or Shadow Immortal, insane value!

Lastly, we have 40x Fate of Chaos selection chests also on sale for just 75 Lotus. This means that you can get 40x Chaos fragments on top of the 40 from Rainy Spring netting you 80 Chaos Fragments for just 20$ if you spend Lotus only on this. Incredible for all of us who are done with Holy but still need more Chaos fragments. HUGE value, in fact this is the most value I have ever seen in any event.

Spring Fiesta 2024 is an easy-going, rewarding event with realistic objectives and doesn’t demand overspending. There’s a generous sprinkle of gems and Stardust as rewards. The 75 Silver Lotus mark for buying chaos or holy/shadow immortal is easily achievable with diligence in tasks. It’s a thumbs up from me, a fun and fruitful event, and definitely worth diving into!

description: Ladies and gentlemen! Get your sunglasses on, fill your drinks because it is time! Sun’s out gun’s out and get ready to claim MASSIVE rewards in this years Summer Festival event! html:
Ladies and gentlemen! Get your sunglasses on, fill your drinks because it is time! Sun’s out gun’s out and get ready to claim MASSIVE rewards in this years Summer Festival event! In the 874 days I have played this game I have never seen any event close to this event in terms of awesome rewards. Get ready because the the summer carnival has INSANE rewards in 2023!

Main rewards table:

  1. 60x fragments of Holy or Shadow Immortal fragment, dealers choice
  2. 60x fragments of Alexander, Attila, El Cid or Saladin
  3. 60x fragments of unique artifact for either Yoshitsune, Frederick, YSG or Emperor Qin
  4. 60x fragments of unique artifact for either Herald, William, Arash or King Arthur
  5. 60x fragments of unique artifact for either Alexander, Attila, El Cid or Saladin
  6. 40x fragments of Chaos Immortal Loki

So this year we are not doing cosmetics and skins, no no. Instead they have packed the event with juicy top tier goodies for us. We are getting Loki fragments, we are getting cheap unique artifacts (yes that is plural! Spenders can get 5 unique artifacts for cheap this event), we even got FREE unique artifacts waiting at the end of the Bonfire Festivities and a FULL 60x fragments for your favorite Holy or Shadow Immortal for just 20 bucks!

Unique Artifacts in this event

First up we have a free tier reward of a full unique artifact. This is massive, especially for all of you low spenders / near F2P players. Furthermore, it is some very nice unique artifacts not normally available in events like this. For once we have powerful uniques for water, lightning, wind and earth-wind-hybrid marches.

Free Rewards Tier Uniques include:

  1. Scroll of the Tiger, Unique artifact for Yoshitsune.
  2. Crown of Flame, Unique artifact for Frederick.
  3. The Code of Gyeongguk, Unique artifact for Yi-Seong-gye.
  4. Qin’s Chariot, Unique artifact for Emperor Qin.

This is huge and you want to make sure to complete the Summer Party bonfire challenge by day 5 end.

Artifacts in store bundles

It does not end here! We have more unique artifacts available for the spenders out there in the event bundles. These bundles are available daily with a single stock. Make note that they reset DAILY and as such you cannot buy 5x 5$ bundles on the last day, but you can buy a total of five 5$ bundles by purchasing one each day.

Event shop bundles contain more uniques! You can get a total of 5x uniques for Immortals:

  1. Figurehead of War, Unique artifact for Herald.
  2. Domesday Book, Unique artifact for William.
  3. Champion’s Arrow, Unique artifact for Arash.
  4. Scabbard of Avalon, Unique artifact for King Arthur.

Good news for all you water and fire players!

Pricing of Store Bundles

As such, you can get a full UA every single day of the event for 185 bucks!

But how about efficiency? What is the cheapest UA I can get here? Spending 150 bucks across the five days on 5$ and 10$ bundles will net you the 60 you need for 150$. A reasonable price tag for a unique in this kind of event and cheap comparatively speaking to non-event purchases.

Summer Event 101

The Summer Festival 2023 begins on June 28th and last until July 3rd (available for servers that have been open for more than 7 days; the event will last for the first 5 days, and the sixth day is the settlement day in which you can continue to claim rewards). Let’s check out the event details together!

  1. Summer Carnival: complete daily tasks to obtain firewood and other goodies. More importantly, you earn points towards the juicy star chests with amazing rewards.

Once your task completion progress reaches certain points, you can get a progress chest that contains more firewood as well as Loki fragments! I was personally worries with the last seasonal events introduction of Wukong that we were not getting more free Loki fragments – I am super hyped and excited to see that this is not the case! We are getting a nice 40 more Loki fragments for free this event.

2. Sail Adventure: This is also a complete copy of previous side events, but it is fine since we quite like this one! It is a decent way to earn some free rewards and you can turn gems into speed ups if you have the time and AP to reset and farm camps.

Otherwise, send your Immortals on an adventure at sea and claim rewards that way.

This side event is important because the event chests in this one’s star-bar-meter rewards additional Piles of Firewood which you are going to need quite a few off for the tier-event. More on that.

3. Treasure Hunting: Hunt gnomes, collect resources, etc. As you grind you get more and more chests and eventually you can complete the event and have a nice chunck of speeds on top.

The chests obtain Firewood and a few resources and speed ups as you play the game and grind out resources and gnomes.

4. Summer Party: Now this is where things get really interesting. As mentioned in the beginning of this guide, we have a lot of awesome rewards this time and much of it comes from this side event – the bonfire summer party.

This is where we get our chance at a free full unique artifact for either Yoshitsune, Frederick, YSG or Qin. Furthermore, this is where you can spend 20$ and unlock the second tier with amazing additional rewards. HUGE value for money on this one.

For the price of 20$ (assuming you complete the event) you recieve:

  • 1 full set of 60 fragments for your favorite shadow or holy Immortal. 80-100 bucks value alone.
  • 1 full set of 60 fragments for unique artifact for Alexander, Cid, Attila or Saladin
  • 1 full set of 60 fragments for your choice of Attila, Saladin, Cid or Alexander Immortal
  • Plus a bunch of speeds, philosopher stones and resources.

Completing Summer Party

Completing the Summer Party bonfire event can be quire tricky without spending a lot this event. You gotta complete all other content to get a good chunck of Firewood piles as these count for 40 points in one go. The remaining points you must get from grinding gnomes really hard! Logs drop here and reward you 10 points per log.

Let’s have a look at how long the grind is going to be. Each level requires an increasing amount of points until you reach level 17. Remember to use logs and piles of logs effectively, don’t overcap by spending a pile when there is only 20 points left on the level!

Once you reach level 17, the points required stays the same. All in all the levels and point requirements are as follow:

That is all for this years summer festival event! Happy summer everybody and good thing we can bring Infinity Kingdom with us to the beach!

description: The Star of Popularity is a limited-time, 10-day cross-server celebration event in Infinity Kingdom where players and servers compete in a gifting war to achieve glory, rare cosmetics, and massive server-wide rewards. It’s not just about who can spend the most, but who can organize and strategize mo
html:
The Star of Popularity is a limited-time, 10-day cross-server celebration event in Infinity Kingdom where players and servers compete in a gifting war to achieve glory, rare cosmetics, and massive server-wide rewards. It’s not just about who can spend the most, but who can organize and strategize most effectively.

This guide will walk you through:

  • How the event works
  • How to earn and use gift boxes
  • Individual vs. server rankings
  • Key tips for optimizing rewards
  • Free-to-play participation strategies

📜 Event Overview

  • Duration: 10 days
    • Days 1–9: Active gifting
    • Day 10: Settlement Day – no gifting allowed
  • Type: Cross-server, both individual and server-wide competition
  • Goal: Accumulate Popularity Points by sending or receiving Rose Gift Boxes

🎁 How the Gifting System Works

There are two ways to gain Popularity Points:

  1. Sending Rose Gift Boxes to another player
    • Increases that player’s popularity
    • You earn valuable reward chests for gifting
  2. Sending Rose Gift Boxes without selecting a player
    • Increases your own popularity
    • BUT: You don’t receive rewards for sending to yourself

💡 Tip: Always gift to someone else if you want rewards back—preferably your server’s designated “popularity candidate.”

🏆 Server Strategy – Why It Matters

This event isn’t just about the individual leaderboard—it’s also a server competition. The highest-ranked individual player from each server determines the server’s ranking. Based on that rank, all players level 25+ who participated get server-wide rewards.

🔥 Why Servers Should Focus Their Efforts

  • Choose one main spender as your server’s ranking candidate
  • All other players should gift to this one player only
  • This maximizes the individual’s rank and secures the highest possible reward tier for everyone

💡 If you gift randomly or to yourself, you’ll lose out on both rewards and server rank progression.

🎟️ How to Get Rose Gift Boxes (And What They’re Worth)

You earn gift boxes by spending in-game. The more you spend—and what tier of items you buy—determines what type of box you get and how much popularity you’re contributing.

✔ You can accumulate a lot of points fast by buying higher-tier bundles, but lower-tier bundles still help.
✔ For $50, you’ll usually get 10 Deluxe Gift Boxes, equaling 30 popularity points if sent to another player.

💡 Efficient Spending Tip: Mixing in $5 and $10 bundles gives you more total gift boxes, which means more reward chests back when gifting to the designated player.

📦 Daily Gift Box Claims – Freebies You Shouldn’t Miss

Even if you’re not spending, you can claim 10x Deluxe Gift Boxes daily during the event!

🎁 Claim these every day! They include:

  • AP bottles
  • SP bottles
  • Random Immortal Fragments
  • Dazzling Summons
  • And more

💡 These are NOT tied to spending, so free-to-play players can still actively contribute and benefit.

🥇 Individual Rewards – What You Get for Ranking

The top 100 players in Popularity Points receive exclusive cosmetic rewards and buffs.

🎁 Server-Wide Rewards – Shared With All Active Players

Every player level 25+ who sends or receives a gift during the event gets rewards based on the server’s top ranked player.

💡 This means your whole server benefits if you coordinate gifting to the right person. Don’t just chase personal popularity if you aren’t competing for rank—help your server instead.

⭐ Quick Tips for Maximizing This Event

✅ DO gift to your server’s main candidate – don’t split points randomly
✅ DON’T gift to yourself unless you’re chasing top 100 (you won’t get gift rewards)
✅ DO claim your 10x Deluxe Gift Boxes every day – they’re free and valuable
✅ DO buy lower-tier bundles if you want max rewards-per-dollar
✅ DON’T forget that day 10 is settlement only – no more gifting!

Summary

The Star of Popularity is more than just a vanity contest—it’s a strategic, server-wide opportunity to earn amazing cosmetics, fragments, and gems. With the right coordination, even non-spenders can walk away with great rewards.

Whether you’re a spender pushing for rank or a free-to-play player contributing support, your participation helps your entire server succeed.

🎯 Pick your representative, gift daily, and claim your free boxes—and let your server shine across the realms!

title: Stallar Compass, how does it work and what are the chances of artifact rewards?
html:
The Stellar Compass event is a relatively new Event to grace the Lords of Norheim. It is a very important event for all players because some of the core-unique artifacts of the game can be found here. If you main earth you need Alexander’s if you main water you need Attila’s and so on. These unique artifacts can be extreemly expensive to get and you need 15 uniques to max a single one.

This is a rare opportunity to both get cheap unique artifacts via bundles and also getting FREE unique artifacts if you grind and bank right!

This means that free to play players are able to grind and bank Crystal Balls to ensure Unique Artifact rewards.

Redeem event for F2P crystal balls

This event is a solid way to obtain rewards, much cheaper for spender than Triss and is also available for Free-To-Play players since the side-event “Redeem Event” offers you Crystal Balls rewards by spending event currency farmed killing gnomes, gathering resources, etc.

Wonderful Journey, more F2P crystal balls

Futhermore, you can obtain a lot of Crystal Balls by completing the Wonderful Journey event that will also be happening at the same time. Here you spend Dice obtained by spending gems and/or purchasing in the shop. Also a F2P method for obtaining Unique Artifact Fragments.

I spent a total of 80 dice to complete the bonus wheel. Your experiance may vary, seen as any hits on the jackpot tile make a huge difference. Theoretically, you are 100% sure to max out points by lapping the board 13 times. With 29 tiles to land on and a 6-sided dice, your absolute maximum required number of rolls (without EVER hitting any of the jackpots small of large) is 377.

AV = ( (M + 1 )/ 2 ) * N

  • Where AV is the average dice value
  • M is the max value of all dice
  • N is the total number of die

( 6 + 1 )/ 2 ) * 106 = 377

However, there is a 3.4% chance to hit the big jackpot and a 10.32% chance to hit one of the small ones on every lap. I got a little lucky and spent 80 dice. You could do with fewer or a few more averaging around 80-100 dice to complete event with resonable certainty.

Stellar Rewards

In addition to the unique artifact fragments, you are going to be getting a lot of speedups and other very nice resources from farming this event. All in all this is a VERY high value event for most all players in Infinity Kingdom and one you should pay careful attention to. Make sure you grind out the entire free to play Redeem Event every time it comes around, you will be able to get F2P artifacts and speedups very quickly.

Moreover, try to make sure you spend your gems while Spending Rewards and Wonderful Journey events are live. For instance, growing and developing players are going to be spending gems on summoning for Purple Crystals. When you do that you spend a ton of gems and thus you should always do that during a spender-event. That way you get a lot of Dice to be used later in many events. Take note, that Dice are an inventory ressource and as such carry over for the next event.

title: Stellar Compass event in season 2
description: The Stellar Compass event is where you can earn artifact fragments, either for elemental selection chests or seasonal unique artifacts. It looks simple at first, but a lot of players get confused about why they see different drops — that’s because there are actually two separate reward sets in this
html:
The Stellar Compass event is where you can earn artifact fragments, either for elemental selection chests or seasonal unique artifacts. It looks simple at first, but a lot of players get confused about why they see different drops — that’s because there are actually two separate reward sets in this event, and you control which one you get.

This guide explains exactly how it works, how the pity mechanic functions, where to get crystal balls, and how the bundle values compare.

Event Mechanics

There are two separate drop sets in Stellar Compass:

  • Elemental Selection Fragments: Fire, Water, Lightning, Earth, and Wind Immortals
  • Seasonal Selection Chests: Unique artifacts for Margret, YSS, Louis, Seondeok, Artemisia, Pakal, Tokugawa, Matilda, Trajan, Cao Cao, Toyotomi, Darius, Mehmed, and Ragnar

You can’t get both at once — it’s one or the other depending on your reward pool. Which is nice, because having it mixed would get you just half the rewards you actually are out for! Very good.

If your board shows the wrong set (for example, you want Elemental but see Seasonal), tap “Reward Refresh.”

  • First refresh: free
  • After that: 10 gems per refresh
  • Refreshing resets your board and any progress, so only do it before spinning.

Each board always includes:

  • 4 fields that can drop 15 artifact fragments each
  • 0.8% chance per field (so 4 × 0.8% = 3.2% total per spin)

That means every crystal ball gives you about a 3.2% chance to land on one of those artifact fields.

Pity System

There’s a pity mechanic in Stellar Compass:

  • After 100 spins without any artifact drop, you’re guaranteed one.
  • The description says your “chance increases” after several misses, but no percentage change is visible.

So practically speaking, expect one artifact drop roughly every 30–35 spins on average, or 100 spins at worst (pity hit).

Bundle Pricing

Here’s a full comparison between the in-game shop and GTarcade bundles.

In-Game Shop Bundles

GTarcade Bundles

Value Comparison

If you only care about crystal balls, GTarcade gives you better value across every price point.
But if you’re also chasing gems for fast progression, the in-game bundles are still good because of the gem bonus.

Realistically, most players won’t hit the daily stock limits since both stores reset each day. However, if you’re trying to push artifact progress quickly, mixing GTarcade’s cheaper bundles with in-game gem bundles is the best approach — that way, you stretch your money without running out of stock early.

Summary:

  • Best raw value → GTarcade $1 bundle (5 balls per $1)
  • Best mixed value (balls + gems) → In-game $1 bundle (4 balls + 100 gems)
  • Mix both if you’re pushing hard and want both balls + gems daily

Artifact Cost Estimate

Each artifact requires 60 fragments.

Each drop gives 15 fragments, so you need 4 successful drops to complete one artifact.

With a 3.2% total drop rate, you’ll average ~31 spins per artifact.
At pity (100 spins), that’s the guaranteed upper limit.

Now let’s translate that into money based on the best bundles:

In-Game (Best Low Tiers)

GTarcade (Best Low Tiers)

So generally, GTarcade saves you around 15–25% per artifact, depending on luck and bundle mix.

Free Crystal Ball Sources

For free-to-play or light spenders, there are a few ways to earn crystal balls outside bundles:

Redeem Event

Use Ancient Silvers from standard gameplay (gnomes, gathering, etc.).

  • 25 balls for 40 gems + 40 silvers each
  • 25 balls for 80 silvers each

That’s up to 50 balls total if you do both.

Wonderful Journey

Earn Dice from spending gems or completing Golden Path levels during the event.

  • Completing all stages = 100 crystal balls

If you line this up with the Redeem Event, you can collect around 150 balls per event cycle totally free.

In Wonderful Journey, your progress comes from rolling Dice, which move you around the board for rewards — and finishing all stages can net you up to 100 Crystal Balls.

You can’t buy Dice directly; instead, you earn them through two main actions:

  • Recharge 400 gems (by buying any in-game bundles) → 1 Dice
  • Spend 800 gems (for example, on Golden Path levels, Market refreshes, or building speedups) → 1 Dice

So if you recharge and spend normally during events, you’ll pick up Dice naturally in the background.

The key is timing — try to line up your regular spending with Wonderful Journey’s duration. You’ll earn Dice on both recharges and spending gems, for maximum efficiency.

Player Perspective

So, the main thing is to check your reward pool before you start. If you’re after seasonal artifacts, make sure the board says so — otherwise, you’re wasting spins.
The Reward Refresh button is the switch between the two pools, but any progress on the pity-bar will reset with it.

For spending strategy:

  • GTarcade is just better value per ball, no question.
  • But if you’re also climbing Golden Path or chasing gem-based progress, mixing in-game bundles helps if you struggle with gems.
  • Most players won’t hit daily stock caps, but for heavy spinners, running both stores in parallel ensures smooth progress.

I’d personally use GTarcade for the core rolls, and throw in the in-game $1 packs for the gems if you’re already active in events like Path of Gold or Dragon Treasure.

Conclusion

  • There are two separate drop sets — Elemental Selection and Seasonal Selection.
  • Switch between them using Reward Refresh (resets progress).
  • Artifact drop chance = 3.2% per spin, with pity at 100 spins.
  • GTarcade bundles give the best ball-per-dollar ratio, while in-game bundles give gem value.
  • F2P can earn ~150 crystal balls per event through Redeem + Wonderful Journey.
  • If you want fast progression, mix bundle types to expand daily stock — otherwise, GTarcade alone is the best deal.

html:
Stellar Compass Event Guide – Infinity Kingdom

The Stellar Compass event is a seasonal, high-value event in Infinity Kingdom that provides players with artifact crafting materials, speed-ups, purple crystals, and, most importantly, unique artifact fragments.

The first iteration of the event, introduced in Season 1, allows players to choose their artifact fragments through universal elemental selection boxes, making it a fantastic opportunity to upgrade your Immortals.

In this guide, we’ll cover:
✔ How the event works
✔ How to participate (both free-to-play & spending players)
✔ Crystal Ball pricing & drop rates
✔ Comparing Stellar Compass vs. Standard Artifact Bundles

If you’re looking to efficiently upgrade your unique artifacts, this guide will help you make the most cost-effective choices.

How Stellar Compass Works

1. Participation & Currency – Crystal Balls

To participate in Stellar Compass, players need Crystal Balls, which can be obtained in several ways:

✔ Through the spender-dice event (a rolling event where purchases give dice rolls & rewards).
✔ Through the redeem event (kill Gnomes and farm resources to earn a currency that can be exchanged for Crystal Balls).
✔ Direct purchase in the in-game shop.

💡 Tip for Free-to-Play Players:

  • Do NOT spend Crystal Balls until you have collected 100.
  • There is a guaranteed artifact jackpot at 100 draws if you miss it 99 times.

Understanding the Pricing of Unique Artifacts in Stellar Compass

While Stellar Compass offers more than just artifact fragments, artifacts are the main draw of the event. Let’s break down the costs and compare them to the traditional artifact bundles in the in-game shop.

1. Crystal Ball Pricing in Stellar Compass

Purchasing Crystal Balls comes at different price points:

Comparing Stellar Compass vs. Standard Artifact Bundles

1. Standard In-Game Shop Pricing

💡 Observations:

Conclusion: Should You Participate in Stellar Compass?

✔ Yes! Stellar Compass is worth participating in because of bonus materials and speed-ups, but don’t expect massive savings on artifact fragments.
✔ Use a mix of daily bundles and cheaper Stellar bundles for optimal artifact progression.
✔ If you’re free-to-play, save 100 Crystal Balls before pulling to guarantee at least one jackpot.

💡 Final Thought:
While Stellar Compass isn’t the absolute cheapest way to get artifacts, it offers valuable side rewards that make it worth participating in—as long as you’re strategic with your spending. 🚀

Throne of the Supreme is a cross-server PvP tournament in Infinity Kingdom that showcases the top players from many servers battling it out in a grand arena. It typically opens around the same time as a server’s first Season 1 of KvK (Conquest Season) and is one of the most exciting competitive events in the game.

What Is the Betting System in Throne of the Supreme?

During the Throne of the Supreme (ToS) cross-server tournament, players can earn massive rewards without even fighting by participating in the Lucky Guess side event — the betting system. Here, you place bets on the outcomes of PvP battles and win Lucky Amulets if your predictions are correct. These are later exchanged for high-value items in the Supreme Trove.

How Betting Works

  • Three Betting Slots per Day: During the group stages, there are three separate times each day when you can place bets.
  • Multiple Bets per Slot: In each slot, you can bet on 8 matches. Later in the tournament (knockouts), this reduces to 4, then 2, then 1 (the finals).
  • Odds Multiply: The more matches you bet on correctly in a single slot, the higher the total payout due to compounding odds. Even if the individual match odds are low, combining 8 correct predictions can lead to multipliers of 4x to 10x or more.

Betting Schedule and Timing

  • Two Combat Rounds per Day: Battles happen twice a day during the group stage, and betting rounds open around those.
  • Odds Start Neutral: When betting opens, all players have equal odds (e.g., 1.00 vs 1.00). The odds adjust based on how many players bet on each side.
  • Frequent Odds Refreshes: Odds refresh multiple times per hour, especially in the first couple of hours after bets open.

How to Maximize Value – Step-by-Step Strategy

Here’s the optimal strategy to make thousands of Lucky Amulets per day with minimal risk:

1. Save Up Betting Currency

  • Earn basic Lucky Guess Coins during the first stage (group battles).
  • Don’t spend recklessly — save up to go hard when odds are favorable. Always have atleast 3x 90 coins.

2. Use Alts to Manipulate Odds (Allowed!)

  • It is not against the Terms of Service to use alt accounts to bet.
  • Right after betting opens, use alts to place bets on players you know will lose.
  • This will skew the odds and raise the return rate for the actual winners.

3. Place Bets on Your Main After Odds Adjust

  • Wait for the first odds refresh (usually within 15–30 minutes).
  • Now place bets on the likely winners on your main account.
  • With just one betting slot, you can easily get 4x to 5x returns on safe bets.

4. Repeat 3x a Day

  • Do this in all three betting windows per day.
  • If you hit 8 safe bets with 5x odds each round, you’re earning around 4,000–5,000 amulets per slot, or up to 15,000 per day.

Tips for Winning Bets

  • Scout the Tournament: Watch battles or use ranking lists to know who the top players are.
  • Stick to Favorites: Bet on reliable players with strong records — the odds manipulation will still make these profitable.
  • Don’t Overthink It: Stick to the strategy. You’re not gambling, you’re farming.

Final Thoughts

The Lucky Guess system in Throne of the Supreme isn’t just for fun — it’s one of the best value farming mechanics in Infinity Kingdom. With a little planning and some clever odds manipulation, you can walk away with tens of thousands of Lucky Amulets, which translate directly into powerful rewards.

Use the system smartly, and the Supreme Trove is yours to loot.

html:
What is Throne of the Supreme?

Throne of the Supreme is a cross-server PvP tournament in Infinity Kingdom that showcases the top players from many servers battling it out in a grand arena. It typically opens around the same time as a server’s first Season 1 of KvK (Conquest Season) and is one of the most exciting competitive events in the game.

This event lets you test your strength against the best – without risking any troop losses.

How Does It Work?

No Troop Losses – Just Glory

In this event, your own Immortals and troops are used, but the battles are simulated – no troops are lost, and healing isn’t required. This means you can go all out with your best builds and strategies without worry.

Stage 1: Ranking Battles (Arena Style)

The first stage plays like the regular Arena, but it’s part of the Supreme competition. All participants are placed in a large ranking system and fight each other to climb the leaderboard.

  • Fight other players to earn points and improve your rank.
  • Only the Top 64 players will qualify to move on to the next stage.
  • This part of the event is very competitive, so make sure to use your strongest Immortals, best troop synergies, and optimal relics.

Stage 2: Knockout Bracket

After the top 64 are determined, the event switches to a bracket-style knockout tournament.

  • Players are divided into fixed brackets.
  • Each round eliminates half the field.
  • The format goes from 64 → 32 → 16 → 8 → 4 → 2 → Champion.

This stage tests your consistency and ability to win against top opponents in best-of matches.

Cross-Server Competition

Unlike regular Arena, Throne of the Supreme is cross-server, so you’ll face top players from many different servers. This increases the challenge and prestige of the event.

Side Event: Betting System

Alongside the tournament is a betting mini-game, where you can place bets on which players you think will win their matchups.

  • Use your predictions to earn valuable rewards like gems, speedups, and rare items.
  • Smart betting can make this side event just as profitable as participating directly!

Tips for Success

  • Optimize your lineups with strong synergy and well-upgraded Immortals.
  • Scout the leaderboard early to understand the competition.
  • Participate in the betting system even if you didn’t qualify – it’s worth it!
  • Save your strongest teams and relics for the knockout rounds.

Conclusion

Throne of the Supreme is a true test of PvP strength and strategy in Infinity Kingdom. Whether you’re fighting to be crowned the Supreme Champion or making smart bets on your favorite competitors, it’s an event no player should miss!

title: Chaos Roulette (updated for patch 2.8.9)
description: Chaos Roulette is the weekly “push your luck” event that lets players convert Eyes of Chaos into Chaos immortal fragments and Chaos unique artifact fragments. It’s one of the core long-term progression systems for Chaos accounts, after the recent patch we now also have an added extra 1× immortal fra
html:
Chaos Roulette is the weekly “push your luck” event that lets players convert Eyes of Chaos into Chaos immortal fragments and Chaos unique artifact fragments. It’s one of the core long-term progression systems for Chaos accounts, after the recent patch we now also have an added extra 1× immortal fragment drops to the wheel.

If you’ve played the event before the update, the new version feels noticeably smoother. You still get the guaranteed jackpot every 25 spins, but now you’re also collecting drips of 1-frag drops along the way.

This guide breaks down exactly how the event works, the real drop math, which bundles provide the best value, and then two full cost-analysis paths for immortal fragments and unique artifact fragments using the Chaos Roulette event:

  • 200 spins per week (best value, slow but efficient), and
  • 900 spins per week (fast, expensive, max bonus bar).

How Chaos Roulette Works

1. You buy Eyes of Chaos

These come from either:

  • GTarcade bundles (best value)
  • In-game bundles

2. You spin the wheel

Each spin can land on:

  • 6× immortal fragment jackpot
  • 1× immortal fragment
  • 1× artifact fragment
  • … or other minor rewards (ignored for cost analysis).

The important part is the actual drop rates:

So:

  • Total immortal 1-frag chance: 6% per spin
  • Total artifact 1-frag chance: 9% per spin

Note that the in-game tooltip still has a typo saying 30%, but every artifact slot is actually 3% — all equal.

3. Jackpot pity system

If you don’t hit the 6-frag jackpot after 24 spins, the 25th spin is guaranteed jackpot.

This matters a LOT for the math because the jackpot effectively becomes more common than the raw 4%.

4. Weekly Bonus Bar (resets every event)

You get extra immortal fragments for hitting total-spin milestones:

Important:
The most efficient bonus-bar fragments are at 50 and 100 spins.
The worst efficiency is 350 to 700, so you either:

  • stay low (50/100/200) for value, or
  • go all the way to 900 if you’re speed-pushing.

Note that by cumulative I refer to the fact that on e.g. 200 spins you get the bonus of the 50, 100 and 200 spin bonus reward = 30 fragments divided by 200 spins = 0.15 fragments per spin value.

Drop Rate Math – Real Expected Fragments per Spin

This is the exact math including both the 4% jackpot chance and the forced pity jackpot at spin 25.

1. Jackpot fragments per spin

Expected spins per jackpot (with pity): ≈ 15.99 spins
So jackpots per spin: ≈ 1 / 15.99 ≈ 0.06254

Each jackpot = 6 fragments, so:

Fragments from jackpots per spin ≈ 0.06254 × 6 ≈ 0.375

This includes both:

  • every natural 4% jackpot, and
  • every forced pity jackpot.

2. 1-fragment immortal drops per spin

Two 3% immortal slots → 6% chance per spin
Adjusted for the pity cycle, these average:

≈ 0.0586 immortal fragments per spin

Total immortal fragments per spin

Add both sources:

0.3752 + 0.0586 ≈ 0.4338

So the real expected value is:

≈ 0.434 Chaos immortal fragments per spin all in all as you do the event (not including bonuses).
(about 43 per 100 spins, not incl. bonuses)

This is the number used in all cost calculations below.

Bundle Options & Efficiency

Here’s the clean version of the bundle efficiency table you provided, focusing only on $ per Eye (D/E).

GTarcade Bundles

Best value:

  • $5, $10, $20 GTarcade packs → $0.50/eye

In-game Bundles

Verdict:
Use in-game bundles only after exhausting GTarcade $5/$10/$20/$50.

Cost Analysis – Path 1: 200 Spins per Event

Slow, efficient, best value from the bonus bar. Note that to keep it somewhat simple, I am not including the 3 free spins below.

Fragments per spin at 200 spins/week

  • Base expected value: 0.4338 frags/spin
  • Bonus bar at 200 spins gives 30 frags → 0.15 frags/spin

Total:

≈ 0.4338 + 0.15 ≈ 0.5838 immortal fragments per spin

Fragments gained per 200-spin event

200 × 0.5838 ≈ 116.8 fragments/week

How many weeks to hit 1640 fragments?

1640 ÷ 116.8 ≈ 14.0 weeks

Cost per week (200 eyes/week)

All cheap GTarcade eyes:
200 × $0.50 = $100/week

Total cost

That means, that through buying the Gtarcade bundles and doing 200 spins per week we need a total of 14 weeks × $100 spend = for an average estimated cost of $1,400 to reach 1640 immortal fragments and it takes 14 weeks if you do it ONLY through Chaos Roulette.

Cost Analysis – Path 2: 900 Spins per Event

Fast, expensive, pushes full bonus bar every week.

Fragments per spin at 900 spins/week

  • Base expected value: 0.4338 frags/spin
  • Bonus bar gives 120 frags → 0.1333 frags/spin

Total:

≈ 0.5671 immortal fragments per spin

Fragments gained per 900-spin event

900 × 0.5671 ≈ 510.4 fragments/week

How many weeks to reach 1640 fragments?

1640 ÷ 510.4 ≈ 3.21 weeks

So realistically 4 weeks.

Cost per week for 900 spins

You need 900 eyes:

  • First 620 eyes = $0.50 → $310
  • Remaining 280 eyes = GTarcade $50 packs ($0.71) → $200
    (Four $50 packs = 280 eyes)

Total weekly cost: $510 per event

Total cost

This means, that going fast you are going to be able to get 1640 fragments in 3.21 weeks, so reality during your 4th week at a total cost of 3 full weeks of $510 plus a fourth week where we on average need 108.8 fragments. To get these last fragments we can do one week of 200 spins for the 116.8 fragments and slightly overcap. Given that these are averages that is fair. Also note that doing more than 200 becomes quite inefficient given the bonus bar but doing less will statistically not get you the 108.8 you need.

Total cost thus becomes 3 weeks × $510 + 1 week × $100 = $1,630.

Comparatively, we pay on average $230 premium going fast with 900 spins over slow with 200 spins, but we also cut down the time to 1640 fragments from 14 weeks to just 4 (3.21).

Artifact Fragment Cost Analysis (Bonus-Bar Doesn’t Help Here)

Artifact fragments are simpler:

  • Artifact drop rate = 9%
  • Expected value = 0.09 fragments per spin
  • Need 60 fragments →
    60 ÷ 0.09 ≈ 666.7 spins

Cost via 200 spins/week

  • 200 spins/week → 18 artifact frags/week
  • ~3.3 weeks
  • Cost: ~667 × $0.50 = $333

Cost via 900 spins/week

  • 900 spins/week → 81 artifact frags/week
  • Typically finished in one event
  • Effective cost per eye ≈ $0.567
  • Total: 667 × $0.567 ≈ $378

Player Perspective (What I’d Actually Do)

If I’m honest about how Chaos Roulette feels after doing this event for years:

  • 50-100 spins/week is the sweet spot for value.
    You stay in the good bonus-bar tiers, your cost stays as low as possible but the speed is rediculessly slow. At 200 spins we bring speed to 14 weeks which is still a long time, but costs are less than the fast 900 spin path.
  • 900 spins/week is the “I want my Chaos march NOW” mode.
    You’ll grind through the terrible 350–700 bonus-bar range, you’re forced into the $50 GTarcade packs, and it gets a bit more pricy… but you finish MUCH more quickly.
  • For artifacts, they accumulate naturally during immortal farming. If you force them, expect variance — some weeks you’ll get a bunch early, some weeks it’ll be cold.
  • Artifacts are the hardest if you seek to max: At a 3% drop chance for 1 artifact with 3 slots available to land on, you need precisely 10,000 spins on average to get the 15 unique artifacts you need to fully upgrade one with a bonus. That means 11.11 events of full 900 spins. Given that players realistically need the full 4750 immortal fragments to max out stars and talents you do need more than the 1640 immortal fragments in the long run. But even maxing at 4750 fragments (stars plus immortal talents) takes you less time than maxing one artifact.
  • No matter what, never sit at 350–700 spins. That zone is pure bonus-bar pain.

Conclusion

Chaos Roulette is one of the most important long-term Chaos progression systems, and the recent update made it noticeably smoother thanks to the added 1-fragment immortal slots. And on a closing note, make sure you collect artifacts from other events when possible if you need one that is maxed for your Chaos Immortal!

Player Guide: Lucky Spin Event in Infinity Kingdom

The Lucky Spin event in Infinity Kingdom is a fantastic opportunity for players to bolster their immortal roster. Whether you’re a free-to-play player or a spender, this event provides a chance to obtain key immortals and valuable rewards. This guide will walk you through the mechanics of the event, the rewards, and some strategic tips to make the most out of it.

Event Overview

The Lucky Spin event allows players to use gems to purchase spins on the roulette wheel. Each spin has a chance to reward various prizes, with a 2.5% chance to win the grand prize of 60 epic immortal fragments. Spinning 40 times guarantees the grand prize, ensuring that players will eventually obtain the top reward.

Key Details:

  • Maximum Spins per Day: 50
  • Free Spins per Day: 1
  • Spins to Clear the Wheel: 40
  • Max Daily Purple Crystal Gain: 2x 7000 = 14,000
  • Daily Gem Spend: 14,700 (for max purple crystal gain)

How to Participate

  1. Collect Gems: Gems can be earned through gameplay, events, or by spending real money. Ensure you have enough gems to participate effectively.
  2. Select Your Reward: Choose the immortal you want as the main reward from the available list. This includes high-tier immortals like Ragnar, Mehmet, Seondeok, Darius, Atalanta, and many others.
  3. Spin the Wheel: Use your gems to spin the wheel. Each spin has a chance to win various rewards, with a 2.5% chance for the grand prize.

Available Immortals

The Lucky Spin event offers a variety of top-tier immortals, many of which are otherwise paywalled. These include:

  • Ragnar
  • Mehmet
  • Seondeok
  • Darius
  • Atalanta
  • Margaret
  • Yi Sun-Shin
  • Trajan
  • Louis

  • Tokugawa
  • Toyotomi
  • Dido
  • Arash
  • Cyrus
  • Hammurabi
  • Emperor Qin

This selection covers a wide range of classic elements, making it possible for all players to build competitive teams.

Rewards

In addition to immortal fragments, the wheel offers:

These rewards can significantly boost your progress in the game, especially for building out your original element teams.

Strategy and Tips

Maximizing Value

  1. Daily Free Spin: Always use your daily free spin to maximize your chances without spending gems.
  2. Save Gems: Accumulate gems in preparation for the event. This allows you to make the most of the guaranteed grand prize after 40 spins.
  3. Focus on Key Immortals: Select an immortal that fits your current team needs or one that will complete your setup.

Calculating Costs

  • Average Gem Cost per Immortal Fragment: Assuming you need to spin 40 times to get the grand prize, you will spend 12,000 gems per 60 fragments, which equals 200 gems per fragment.
  • Total Cost to Max an Immortal: To max out an immortal (1020 fragments), you will need approximately 204,000 gems. This is a feasible target if you save up over time and complement your fragments from other sources.

Purple Crystal Grinding

While some guides suggest using the Lucky Spin for grinding purple crystals, it’s not the most efficient method. You can convert gems to purple crystals at a roughly 1:1 ratio, but there are better ways to earn crystals. Check out dedicated guides for more efficient crystal farming methods.

Conclusion

The Lucky Spin event is a valuable opportunity to obtain powerful immortals and other rewards in Infinity Kingdom. By understanding the mechanics, planning your gem usage, and selecting the right immortals, you can make significant progress in your game. Happy spinning, and may the odds be in your favor!
