html:
Player Guide: Crafting Artifacts with Bonus Rolls in Infinity Kingdom

In Infinity Kingdom, artifacts play a crucial role in bolstering your immortals’ capabilities, with bonus rolls on these artifacts often making a significant difference in battle performance. However, the likelihood of crafting an artifact with a bonus is relatively low, with many players reporting success rates around one in four or five attempts. This guide explores a strategy to potentially increase your chances of obtaining artifacts with desired bonus rolls, focusing on efficiency and resource management.

Understanding Bonus Rolls

Bonus rolls on artifacts can grant additional stats such as bonus damage or energy regeneration, which can substantially enhance an immortal’s effectiveness. The randomness associated with obtaining these bonuses makes crafting a game of patience and strategy.

Strategy for Increasing Bonus Roll Chances

While there’s no guaranteed method to secure bonus rolls, certain practices seem to improve odds based on player experiences. Here’s a strategic approach to try:

Step 1: Building a “No-Bonus Streak”

Begin by crafting lower-tier artifacts, such as green or blue ones, until you accumulate a streak of 4-5 crafts without receiving any bonus rolls. This step is based on the observation that a series of unsuccessful attempts might increase the likelihood of success in subsequent crafts.

Step 2: Crafting Desired Artifacts

Once you’ve established a “no-bonus streak,” proceed to craft the artifact(s) for your targeted immortal(s). This approach hypothesizes that the chances of obtaining a bonus roll are somewhat higher following a series of non-bonus crafts.

Step 3: Bulk Crafting for Key Artifacts

To further optimize your chances, consider saving up resources to craft multiple instances of a desired artifact in one go. For example, if aiming for a bonus on an Alexander artifact, gather enough materials to craft four unique artifacts consecutively. This bulk crafting, combined with the preceding “no-bonus streak,” may improve your odds of landing a bonus roll.

Tips for Efficient Artifact Crafting

  • Resource Management: Efficiently manage your crafting materials, focusing on accumulating enough resources to implement the bulk crafting strategy for artifacts you highly prioritize.
  • Patience and Persistence: Recognize that crafting with the aim of obtaining bonus rolls requires patience. Be prepared for a process of trial and error, and don’t get discouraged by initial failures.
  • Prioritize Key Immortals: Focus your efforts on crafting artifacts with bonus rolls for immortals who will benefit most significantly from the additional stats, thereby maximizing the impact on your overall strategy.
  • Document Your Attempts: Keeping track of your crafting attempts and outcomes can provide insights into the effectiveness of this strategy and help refine your approach over time.

Conclusion

Crafting artifacts with bonus rolls in Infinity Kingdom is a challenge that combines luck with strategic planning. By employing a methodical approach, such as creating a “no-bonus streak” and engaging in bulk crafting for high-priority artifacts, you can potentially increase your chances of acquiring artifacts with beneficial bonus rolls. While this strategy does not guarantee success, it offers a structured way to pursue those game-changing artifact bonuses, making your immortals more formidable on the battlefield.

title: Athena Aigis Unique Artifact
description: Player Guide: Athena’s Unique Artifact – Aigis
html:
Player Guide: Athena’s Unique Artifact – Aigis

Athena is a powerhouse among the Chaos Immortals in Infinity Kingdom, consistently ranking as one of the top three Immortals in the game. Her strength is further amplified by her unique artifact, Aigis, which, although it may seem simple at first glance, provides an immense boost to her and her team’s survivability. In this guide, we will delve into what makes Athena so formidable and why her unique artifact, Aigis, is incredibly powerful.

Athena: A Top-Tier Immortal

Athena’s role as a Chaos Immortal is vital in any high-level team composition. Her abilities and stats make her a key player in both offensive and defensive strategies. Athena’s primary strength lies in her ability to sustain and protect her team, which is further enhanced by her unique artifact. Moreover, her unique ability to consistenly remove all negative effects makes her sustain power unrivaled. Many players are not very impressed with her, simply because she show quite low healing compared to being an expensive Chaos Immortal. However, it is important to note that the main strength from Athena comes from who mechanics which are not shown anywhere in your battle report!

  1. She consistently removes all wounding and all negative effects from your team, making her one of very few things in the entire game to be able to counter the strongest ultimate abilities and tower of knowledge skills in the game.
  2. Her Unique Artifact is the second mechanic that people are not seeing in reports and therefore underestimating. The power here comes from her ability to bolster the entire teams physical defense attribute.

While the first effect is something I may explore further in it’s own guide (check under the hard-counter sections, I hope to get it out soon). The unique artifact mechanis is something we are going to talk about here today.

Athena’s Unique Artifact: Aigis

Description and Effect

Aigis provides a substantial physical defense boost to Athena and her allies. The artifact’s effect is described as:

“Increases physical defense for 12 seconds equal to 20% of Athena’s physical defense.”

Why is Aigis So Powerful?

At first glance, giving 20% of Athena’s physical defense to allies might not seem like a game-changer. However, when you consider the high attribute levels that Athena can achieve in the end-game, this becomes a massive boost.

Insane Physical Defense Boost

Athena can easily reach 9,000 to 10,000 physical defense. This means that Aigis provides an additional 1,800 to 2,000 physical defense to her allies for 12 seconds. To put this into perspective, this boost is equivalent to 22-24 fully upgraded physical defense nodes in the dragon talent tree, which is considered one of the best defensive nodes available.

Such a significant increase in physical defense cannot be underestimated. It dramatically reduces the damage taken by your team, allowing them to survive longer and sustain their attacks. This defensive boost is crucial in high-stakes battles where every bit of defense counts.

End-Game Attribute Levels

At the end-game, attributes play a crucial role in determining the outcome of battles. The boost provided by Aigis scales exceptionally well with the high attribute levels that players achieve. This scaling makes Aigis one of the best artifacts in the game, providing both immediate and sustained value in combat situations.

Synergy with Other Skills and Artifacts

Athena’s Aigis works exceptionally well in conjunction with other defensive skills. Consider pairing Aigis with skills that further enhance defense or provide additional healing and shielding to maximize the survivability of your team.

How to obtain Aigis?

It is quite streight forward actually. You obtain Athena fragments via the Chaos Roulette event, and as you progress through the 25 spins each time you clear the wheel, you are getting unique artifact fragments as the second most rare drop – usually coming around just before you get the Athena Immortal fragments. On average, maxing out your Athena Immortal in the Chaos Roulette will also net you 720 unique artifact fragments (avg. drop) meaning a solid 8 artifacts crafted when you max her. While this is far from the 15 it takes to max out an artifact, it is plenty to make a good chance at a decent roll and a good bonus upgrade for your Athena.

Conclusion

Athena’s unique artifact, Aigis, is a deceptively simple yet incredibly powerful tool in Infinity Kingdom. By providing a massive boost to physical defense, it ensures that Athena and her team can withstand even the most formidable opponents. Understanding and leveraging Aigis’s power can significantly enhance your team’s performance, making Athena an invaluable asset in your lineup.

As you progress in the game and face tougher challenges, remember to prioritize the acquisition and upgrading of Aigis. Its impact on your team’s survivability and overall effectiveness in battle cannot be overstated. Equip Athena with Aigis and watch as your team becomes a nearly unstoppable force on the battlefield.

title: Attila’s Unique Artifact Effect
description: Attila is one of the many powerful Immortals in Infinity Kingdom. His unique artifact effect reduces the physical and magical defense of silenced opponents in a fan-shaped area. While this effect can be useful in certain situations, it’s important for players to understand its limitations and how to
html:
Attila is one of the many powerful Immortals in Infinity Kingdom. His unique artifact effect reduces the physical and magical defense of silenced opponents in a fan-shaped area. While this effect can be useful in certain situations, it’s important for players to understand its limitations and how to use it effectively.

First, let’s take a closer look at Attila’s unique effect. When Attila uses his ultimate ability, his artifact effect kicks in, reducing the physical and magical defense of silenced opponents in a fan-shaped area. The reduced defense lasts for a short time and is indicated by a red icon on the affected Immortal’s character.

Only applies to silence-procs!

Special thank you to KinCaid for providing information for this article. You most likely already know KinCaid who is doing very good work as an Infinity Kingdom Press Officer!

It’s important to note that Attila’s unique effect only applies to enemies who are currently silenced. If an opponent is not silenced, they will not receive the debuff, and the red icon indicating the debuff will not appear on their character. This means that players using Attila need to time their attacks carefully to take advantage of the debuff when it does proc on their opponents.

One of the key factors that can affect the effectiveness of Attila’s unique effect is the duration of the silence effect. As the silence effect is short-lived, players will need to act quickly to take advantage of the debuff before it wears off. On the other hand, if you are able to hit in this window the player will be able to deal significant damage to their opponents.

Another important factor to consider is the range of Attila’s unique effect. While the effect covers a fan-shaped area in front of Attila, it has limited range and will only affect opponents within a certain distance. Players need to position Attila strategically to ensure that his unique effect covers as many opponents as possible.

How to see when Attila’s silence and debuff is applied?

In-game, the reduced physical and magical defense debuff from Attila’s unique artifact effect will appear as a red icon on the enemy Immortals that are silenced and affected. When the silence duration ends, the debuff will disappear from the affected Immortal.

For example, in the first image provided, you can see that the debuff is not applied to Qin or Barca because they are not currently silenced.

In contrast, in the second image, the debuff applied by Ragnar means that he is receiving increased magical damage, and the debuff appears as a red icon on his character.

So, how can players use Attila’s unique effect effectively in battle? One strategy is to pair Attila with Immortals that have strong damage abilities, such as Merlin. Merlin is able to do very high and overwhelming damage to your opponents, especially if the window lines up with Attila’s unique effect to kick in and reduce their physical and magical defense.

Furthermore, you want to try and time Attila’s attacks to coincide with other Immortal abilities. For example, players can use Attila’s unique effect in combination with Ragnar’s ability to deal increased magical damage to opponents with reduced magical defense and trying to line it up with Merlin’s Ultimate hit. This can result in massive burst damage to opponents, allowing players to quickly take out key targets and turn the tide of battle in their favor.

It’s also important for players to be aware of the limitations of Attila’s unique effect. As mentioned earlier, the effect only applies to opponents who are currently silenced. This means that Attila’s unique effect is not as powerful as some players may think, as the window for which Merlin needs to hit his skill for the added damage is limited. If players are lucky and their opponents are silenced, they will receive a big boost in damage. However, if the silence effect does not proc on the opponent, Attila’s debuff is not as potent as the unique effects of other Immortals such as Ragnar or Herald, which have longer durations and provide more time for Merlin to strike with a massive burst hit.

In conclusion, Attila’s unique artifact effect can be a powerful tool in the right situations. However, players need to be aware of its limitations and use it strategically to maximize its effectiveness in battle. By pairing Attila with Immortals that have strong crowd control abilities, timing attacks to coincide with other Immortal abilities, and positioning Attila strategically, players can take advantage of Attila’s unique effect and deal significant damage to their opponents.

description: Player Guide: Mastering Manco’s Unique Artifact – Barricade of Light
html:
Player Guide: Mastering Manco’s Unique Artifact – Barricade of Light

Manco’s unique artifact, “Barricade of Light,” is a game-changer for players who are strategizing around dodge mechanics in Infinity Kingdom. This artifact boosts Manco’s dodge rate by 25% during the casting of his ultimate ability, Sun Flare. When synergized with the “Misleading” skill and another dodge-enhancing skill, “After-Image,” this artifact can make your Manco incredibly elusive, significantly reducing the incoming damage from enemy attacks.

Deep Dive into Barricade of Light

Barricade of Light not only increases the survivability of Manco but also turns him into a critical asset for your army’s defense. The key benefit of this artifact comes into play when Manco casts Sun Flare, his ultimate ability. During this casting time, the 25% increase in dodge rate makes him substantially more difficult for enemies to hit. This temporary boost is crucial during intense moments of battle where sustaining high dodge rates can be the difference between victory and defeat.

Strategic Implementation

Implementing Barricade of Light effectively requires a build that capitalizes on dodge mechanics. Combining Manco’s unique artifact with the “Misleading” Tower of Knowledge skill, which reduces enemy accuracy, and “After-Image,” which further boosts dodge rates, creates a formidable setup. This combination ensures that not only Manco but potentially your entire lineup benefits from increased evasion, as Misleading affects all enemy units on the battlefield.

The true strength of this setup lies in its ability to mitigate the effectiveness of high-accuracy opponents. While opponents may build their immortals to counteract dodge through increased accuracy, the stacked evasion from Barricade of Light, Misleading, and After-Image can tip the scales back in your favor, making your units frustratingly difficult to hit.

This strategy is particularly effective in PvP scenarios where precision in striking is crucial for overcoming enemy defenses.

Considerations for Use

While the synergy between Barricade of Light and dodge-enhancing skills is powerful, it is important to remember that this strategy may not always be optimal. Opponents who anticipate a high-dodge build might equip skills or pursue strategies that negate dodge benefits, such as using immortals with enhanced accuracy or skills that guarantee hits. Therefore, it’s vital to analyze your opponent’s typical setups and adjust your strategy accordingly. If the meta shifts towards high accuracy builds, the effectiveness of a dodge-centric strategy may decrease, prompting a reassessment of your tactical approach.

Conclusion

Manco’s unique artifact, Barricade of Light, when used in conjunction with skills like Misleading and After-Image, offers a robust defensive mechanism that can turn the tide of battles in Infinity Kingdom. This setup excels in environments where dodging enemy attacks provides a significant strategic advantage. However, its success largely depends on the prevailing battle conditions and opponent strategies. Players should remain flexible and ready to adapt their approach based on the evolving meta and the specific challenges posed by their adversaries. By doing so, they can maximize the impact of Manco and his unique artifact, securing crucial victories in both PvP and PvE engagements.

description: The Enigmatic Power of the Code of Yuan in Infinity Kingdom
html:
The Enigmatic Power of the Code of Yuan in Infinity Kingdom

In the heart of the immersive realms of Infinity Kingdom, a new artifact has emerged to captivate the attention of commanders and strategists alike: the Code of Yuan. This distinctive artifact, exclusively crafted for the revered holy immortal Khubilai Khan, has sparked fervent discussions and ignited curiosity within the kingdom’s ever-evolving landscape. This article delves into the intricacies of the Code of Yuan, dissecting its unique attributes and potential impact on the battlefield.

Unveiling the Artifact: Skill Mechanics

At the core of the Code of Yuan lies a skill mechanic that promises to redefine Khubilai Khan’s prowess in combat. Distinctive to this artifact and unique to Khubilai Khan himself, the skill activates each time his ultimate ability, Total Conquest, inflicts damage. With a remarkable 75% chance, the Code of Yuan empowers the target to endure additional damage.

This mechanic introduces a new layer of strategic possibilities, allowing Khubilai Khan to inflict multiple instances of damage on a single target. The genius of the Code of Yuan lies in its enhancement of Khubilai Khan’s Total Conquest ability. This ultimate ability, already a formidable force, now carries the potential to unleash an even more devastating blow. The additional damage mechanic, triggered by the skill’s activation, amplifies the precision and impact of Khubilai Khan’s attacks, providing him with a newfound advantage in battles. Because the ultimate ability Total Conquest as a default deals damage a total of 5 times, the damage increase is an almost sure proc.

Probability of UA trigger occuring = 1 – (1 – 0.75)5 = 0.9990234375 = 99.9%

Theoretical Potential and the Quest for Precision

On the theoretical front, the Code of Yuan hints at a significant boost to Khubilai Khan’s damage output. This enhancement, in theory, makes a compelling case for a more potent presence on the battlefield. However, the quantifiable extent of this augmentation remains a subject of exploration, necessitating empirical tests to truly ascertain its tangible effects.

Putting Theory to the Test

In the pursuit of understanding the Code of Yuan’s practical implications, rigorous testing has been undertaken. The tests were designed to unravel the artifact’s impact within a controlled environment, minimizing extraneous variables that could skew results.

Boss battles emerged as the litmus test for the Code of Yuan’s potency. As such I engaged in a series of level 18 boss encounters.

(1) Using a Normal Epic artifact with strong physical attack roll and Surge bonus

This artifact is a very powerful one, having rolled near perfect attributes and the Surge bonus. Both of these stat values are amongst the absolute best and most critical for the damage output of Khubilai Khan.

(2) Using a “Code of Yuan” unique artifact with TERRIBLE rolls, no physical attributes and no bonus

This unique artifact contrary to the above, has terrible rolls with no damage impact at all besides the unique effect itself. As such the test we are going to be conducting here will determine if the unique artifact effect all by itself can carry it’s own and make up for the massive damage attribute loss.

Firtly, our Khubilai Khan will be equiped with our powerful normal artifact gaining huge attack and damage-boosting attributes.

Subsequent trials saw Khubilai Khan wielding the Code of Yuan—a unique artifact devoid of attack-boosting attributes and bonuses. The anticipation was a drop in damage output due to the stark disparity in attributes.

Results: Surprising Outcomes and Future Prospects

Counter to expectations, the test results unveiled a fascinating trend. Despite the massive reduction in attributes like physical attack and energy regeneration with the Code of Yuan, the damage output and overall DPS of Khubilai Khan surprisingly increased during boss encounters. Despite having 25% lower physical attack and 17% less energy regen, our UA-Khubilai Khan wielding Code of Yuan was able to deal 11% more damage! Very surprising and a huge find to me.

Counter to expectations, the test results have revealed a compelling narrative that sheds light on the formidable prowess of the Code of Yuan. Our UA-Khubilai Khan, brandishing the Code of Yuan, demonstrated an astonishing 11% increase in damage output during boss encounters. This discovery stands as a resounding testament to the potency of this unique artifact, compellingly underscoring its ability to amplify Khubilai Khan’s impact on the battlefield. This revelation ignites anticipation, kindling eagerness to craft more Codes of Yuan and to envision the potential of a physical main role and a surge bonus on a Unique Artifact. The Code of Yuan’s transformative effect on damage output signifies a significant stride forward in strategic evolution, setting the stage for an exciting era of calculated experimentation and optimized combat mastery.

I look forward to many more Codes of Yuan – best of luck to you on your crafting rolls!

title: Yi Sun-Shin and the Spear Ship
description: Yi Sun-Shin’s unique artifact is one of those upgrades that quietly flips a march from “hard to kill” to “why won’t this team die?”. Base YSS is already a frontline tank with Guard of Devotion, a team-wide 6-second 30% damage taken reduction window. But with the artifact equipped, that same window a
html:
Yi Sun-Shin’s unique artifact is one of those upgrades that quietly flips a march from “hard to kill” to “why won’t this team die?”. Base YSS is already a frontline tank with Guard of Devotion, a team-wide 6-second 30% damage taken reduction window. But with the artifact equipped, that same window also boosts healing received by 30%, which is exactly what sustain cores want — you mitigate the spike and then slurp the HP right back while the enemy alts cycle.

In practice, that means your defensive swing turns into a full reset if your heals land inside YSS’s uptime.

So the artifact isn’t about making YSS hit harder; it’s about turning his ult into a bigger sustain moment for the whole squad. That’s why you see him stapled into modern Earth/Himiko builds with Theodora or Fu Fei — the mitigation buys time, and the +healing pushes those bars up fast enough to shrug off much of the enemy’s damage pressure. If you’re building around layered damage reduction (DR effects like Earth dragon, Oaken, Resist, etc.), this artifact is the glue that lets the comp outlast opponents instead of trading blows.

  • Read more about YSS here.
  • And more about top meta YSS builds here.

What does the Artifact do then?

Yi Sun-Shin’s ultimate ability Guard of Devotion gives you a buff which reduces damage taken by all allied immortals by 30% for 6s.

Through his Unique Artifact we can get another layer of defensive on top of the already very powerful damage reducion, because we will gain his Unique Artifact effect which adds +30% healing received to all allies under Guard of Devotion (same 6s).

Main stat priority (frontline tank): When it comes to optimizing this artifact, the primary attribute you should aim for is: Physical Defense (Preferably as a Percentage): This enhances YSS’ ability to absorb physical attacks, crucial for his role as a frontline shield.

Secondary attributes that are beneficial include: Resilience: Adds an extra layer of survivability and can be good especially in season 1 and 2 where you can resiliance stack (and use Malice) to counter critical damage far better than in Conquest where crit-rates scale beyond resiliance being very useful.

TL;DR: Physical Defense % as the top main attribute is the safest and most consistent pick — he’s frontline and eats a ton of physical poke/auto damage.

Bonus roll preference:

  • If you’re lucky enough to land Physical Defense % and a bonus: Guard > Growth in most lobbies. The extra physical defense you get from Guard generally outperforms Growth.
  • Edge case: if your shard is stacked with mage‑solo‑carry teams (e.g., Himiko, Fu Fei, Bjorn, YSS type mirrors where the big hits are magic‑weighted), Growth can catch up a bit — but marginal.

Crafting reality check: the unique effect unlock is the main power spike. If you’re tight on coins, get one copy to turn on the healing buff first; perfecting sub rolls can come later.

How to obtain

Yi Sun-Shin is a ‘GP-Immortal’ also sometimes referred to as a ‘seasonal immortal’, in essence that refers to him being available through the Golden Path season pass. This is also the main method I recommend to obtain and farm his artifact. As a ‘seasonal immortal’ his artifact is NOT part of the regular elemental selection chests.

You can however obtain his artifact in the Golden Path shop and the Mysterious Pearl shop (daily store).

Obtaining via Golden Path Shop

In the Golden Path, you get a max of 1 in stock per season, 600 coins. If you’re gem‑rich you can keep buying every season to star it up; if not, buy one to unlock the effect ASAP — that single unlock is huge.

Obtaining via Daily Pearl Shop

The Mysterious Pearl Shop has 1 in stock per day, but at a price of 240 Pearls. If you have been banking a lot of pearls prior to the recent update where the unique artifacts from GP immortals was released into Pearl Shop, you may want to use a few here. Or if you are looking for that one crucial unlock this can be good value.

The price however is quite steep and it will be a long grind to obtain the 15 artifacts you need to max one unique artifact (bonus maxing in forge) using Pearls alone. The daily max you can gain through the daily bundles is 20 Pearls.

Conclusion

YSS’s artifact isn’t flashy, but it’s a win-condition for sustain comps. You’re taking his already solid 6-second, 30% teamwide DR and layering +30% healing received on top—so your “don’t die” window turns into a mini-reset if heals land inside it.

Build it like a real frontline, best crafted attribute stats are: Physical Defense % most consistent main stat. For bonuses, Guard > Growth in most battles; the extra phys-def soaks auto attacks and physical damage. Strickly mage-battles: if your Battlegroup or main rivals are relying on solo-carry-mage setups, then Growth can provide a bit more value than Guard.

Acquisition-wise, the power spike is the first unlock. Grab one copy from Golden Path (600 coins, 1 per season) or the Mysterious Pearl Shop (240 pearls, 1/day) to turn the effect on, then min-max rolls later when your wallet/pearls recover.

Bottom line: if your plan is to outlast and/or relies on healing sustain, YSS’s artifact is basically mandatory to unlock and nice to upgrade if possible—turn on the healing buff first, then worry about perfect stats after.

There are many different attributes and stats in Infinity Kingdom. Some of them are selfexplanatory and some of them are very difficult to figure out. In this short page I will try not to over-explain these attributes and instead just give short accurate description of what effects each one has.

Please read my guide on debuffs and buffs for info on these mechanics, and read the guide on how damage calculations and mitigations work on its’ seperate page.

Every Immortal has its’ own base-value for each of the main stats and sub attributes.

UNCONFIRMED
It appears that Magic Penetration and Magical Protection on the surface is quite similar to the Intelligence stats Magic Attack and Magic Defense – they behave in a similar facion, yet first look at how the stats interact with damage taken leads me to believe these stats are more intertwined then the old Int stats. So Magic Penetration may provide baseline increased Magic Damage across the board, but it’s stat value seem positively related to Magical Protection, i.e. it’s effect is enhanced against enemies with higher Magical Protection.

How to improve an Immortals Main Stats?

title: Detailed guide on Attributes and their relevance for immortal types
description: Understanding Immortal Stats and Their Roles
html:
Understanding Immortal Stats and Their Roles

Introduction

Immortals are the beating heart of every army in Infinity Kingdom, and understanding their individual stats is essential to maximizing your team’s performance in both PvE and PvP. While skill builds and elemental synergies are important, the raw stats of each Immortal directly affect their combat effectiveness. This guide will break down what each stat means, how it impacts battle performance, and what types of Immortals benefit most from each stat category.

Core Immortal Stats Explained

1. Physical Attack (PATK)

  • What it is: This stat determines the base damage dealt by skills or basic attacks that scale with physical attack.
  • Relevance: Crucial for melee and ranged physical damage dealers (e.g., Alexander, Hannibal Barca).
  • Synergies: Works well with skills like Cleave, Duel Master, and Anger.

2. Magical Attack (MATK)

  • What it is: This stat affects the potency of magic-based damage skills.
  • Relevance: Key for mages and casters such as Himiko, Merlin, and Baldwin.
  • Synergies: Boosts effectiveness of skills like Annihilation, Fireball, and Death Breath.

3. Physical Defense (PDEF)

  • What it is: Reduces incoming physical damage.
  • Relevance: Important for frontline Immortals, because they are likely to face an enemy physical damage based immortal and also because normal attacks / Auto attacks are physical, even when made by a mage or a support!
  • Synergies: Combines well with Oaken Guard, Physical Shield, Life-Link, Toxin Barrier and Blessing of Defense.

4. Magical Defense (MDEF)

  • What it is: Reduces incoming magical damage.
  • Relevance: Vital for units regularly exposed to AoE magic attacks.
  • Synergies: Reinforced by skills like Resist, Magic Shield, Absolute Defense, Blessing of Defense, Jade Barrier, etc.

5. Dodge

  • What it is: Huge defense against physical damage. All physical damage can be dodged. If you dodge you take 0 damage from the ability or skill you are dodging. Therefore very good value if you can get the enemy to miss attacks!
  • Relevance: Universally important. But ultimately only relevant if you can stack enough to make your enemy miss / your immortals dodge enemy attacks. See Battle Reports!
  • Synergies: Strong synergy with other effects like Misleading and After-Image because dodge basically is based on your dodge value versus the enemies Accuracy value. If your dodge is greater = you dodge enemy attacks.

6. Accuracy

  • What it is: All physical damage can be dodged. If you dodge you take 0 damage from the ability or skill you are dodging. Accuracy makes sure your attacks dont miss or get dodged!
  • Relevance: Important to physical damage dealers, high priority to get enough of. But once you get enough the value drops to nothing. But ultimately only relevant if you can stack enough to make your enemy miss / your immortals dodge enemy attacks. See Battle Reports! Therefore, you get huge value out of all accuracy attributes as long as you are “behind” against an enemies dodge. Once you hit 100% hit rate, the value of accuracy drops to nothing at all. But getting it to 100% is extreemly important! This can be a triggy balance if you wield a physical damage centered setup.
  • Note that magical attacks cannot be dodged and thus mages require 0 accuracy to hit everything.
  • Synergies: Strong synergy with other effects like Coercion.

7. Resilience

  • What it is: The higher your resilience the less chance there is to get hit by a critical strike.
  • Relevance: Relevant to all Immortals and especially relevant fighting against Chase-based mage setups.
  • Synergies: Malice boosts your resilience rate significantly and is an expert defense against enemy crit-based setups.

8. Crit Hit / Crit Damage

  • What it is: Determines the chance and effectiveness of critical hits.
  • Relevance: Crucial for burst-damage dealers and builds centered around Chase or Rage Blessing.
  • Synergies: Works exceptionally with Chase setups but generally Critical Hits are a huge factor in burst setups. You can reach over 3x crit damage if you stack and getting a single crit can literally wipe the battlefield if you are playing a high crit-damage-based setup.

9. Energy Regen.

  • What it is: Determines the speed at which your immortal regains energy. Upon reaching 1000 energy your immortal will cast his or her ultimate ability. Side note, Attack Speed is directly attributed to regen speed.
  • Relevance: Crucial for burst-damage dealers and builds but the higher the better for all..
  • Synergies: Works exceptionally with Blessing of Rage builds and building using No Escape, and Energy Suppression and even Fountain of Life.

10. Aptitute

  • What it is: Determines your immortals ability to govern. Higher values give boosts when appointed in Castle Government. Also factor for Shield Values and for Magical Protection and Penetration.
  • Relevance: Crucial for Charles and Tokugawa as shield values depend on Apt.

11. Magical Penetration / Protection

  • What it is: Determines the effectiveness of magical damage hits.
  • Relevance: Magical Penetration basically works as exposure percentages. If you have high Penetration your magical damage will be amplified. Enemies with high Protection means the magical damage they recieve is reduced. Think of Elemental protection in other games.

12. HP (Health Points) – Unofficial attribute

  • What it is: Determines how much damage an Immortal can take before being eliminated.
  • Health Points are directly linked to troop tier attributes and your immortals “health pool” is thus a direct factor of the troop count deployed by the immortal. Increased troop count = bigger health pool.
  • Relevance: Universally important, especially important for DPS units. Damage Dealt by skills and healing done my skills are based directly on the amount of troops alive at the time of the cast – thus the remaining HP which equated to troop count.
  • Synergies: Strong synergy with healing skills and leech mechanics like Spring of Life and Duel Master.

Stat Priorities by Immortal Type

1. Tanks

  • Good stats: HP, Physical Defense, Magical Defense

2. Physical DPS

  • Good stats: Accuracy (first prio until hit-cap), Physical Attack, Crit Rate, Regen Speed (attack speed), Physical Defense for frontliners.

3. Magical DPS

  • Good stats: Magical Attack, Regen speed, Crit Rate, magical penetration

4. Support / Healers

  • Focus on: Regen Speed, HP, Magical Defense, Physical Defense

Advanced Tip: Balancing Base Stats with Skills

An Immortal’s base stats should influence how you build their skill sets. For instance, a high MATK mage should not be given physical scaling skills. Conversely, a physical damage dealer like Alexander should be built for PATK scaling skills. Understanding base stats also helps prioritize artifacts and passive bonuses from specialization trees.

Conclusion

Immortal stats are the foundation upon which all powerful teams are built. Mastering how each stat functions and contributes to different Immortal roles gives you an edge in both PvE events and competitive PvP. Use this knowledge to better assign skills, choose gear, and build cohesive and lethal team compositions.

title: Difference between Troop attributes and Immortal attributes – prioritize troops!
description: Exploring the difference between Troop and Immortal attributes in Infinity Kingdom — their mechanics, their relevance, and which to prioritize as a player seeking to maximize combat performance.
html:
Exploring the difference between Troop and Immortal attributes in Infinity Kingdom — their mechanics, their relevance, and which to prioritize as a player seeking to maximize combat performance.

⚔️ Infinity Kingdom Guide: Understanding Troop vs Immortal Attributes

In Infinity Kingdom, every march consists of two essential components: the Immortal who leads the army, and the troops who make up the body of that army. Both Immortals and troops have their own attribute stats, and understanding how these two interact is critical for mastering combat — whether you’re pushing in PvP, dominating in PvE, or gearing up for events like IBL or KvK.

This guide unpacks how troop and Immortal attributes work, why they matter, and how to optimize your build by prioritizing what counts most.

🧠 The Basics: What Are Attributes?

Let’s start with the fundamentals.

Every Immortal in Infinity Kingdom has a set of personal attributes — stats like Physical Attack, Magic Attack, Defense, HP, Energy Regen, Crit, and so on. These values directly influence that Immortal’s ability to cast skills, trigger ultimate abilities, and survive in combat.

Meanwhile, the Immortal also commands a group of troops, whose strength is determined by a combination of troop count (how many soldiers are in the unit) and troop attributes (Attack, Defense, etc.). These stats come from the troop tier, castle level, buffs from city bonuses, technologies, and other global modifiers such as castle skins or Honor rank.

So when your Immortal casts a skill or deals basic attack damage, the resulting output is a blend of:

  • The Immortal’s base stats
  • The strength and number of troops
  • Any external modifiers (like buffs, skills, and artifacts)

But here’s the critical part: while Immortal stats might be large in value, they apply to one unit. Troop stats, on the other hand, are multiplied by how many troops are in that army — and that changes everything.

📈 Scaling: Why Troop Stats Multiply Harder

Let’s consider a real combat example.

If your Immortal has 10,000 Magic Attack and commands 15,000 troops with a certain base attack stat, the actual damage output for an ability is not just based on that 10K Magic Attack. The troop attributes — even if modest — are amplified by the total troop count, and that massive scaling creates an exponential increase in damage.

This is why players with high troop counts deal significantly more damage than players with similar Immortal stats but fewer troops. Even a relatively small buff to troop attack becomes a huge boost once multiplied by tens of thousands of units. A 5% troop attack bonus from a castle skin, for example, is more powerful than it appears — especially in late game when marches push 60,000+ troops.

And this is also why empty marches deal almost no damage. If your Immortal is standing alone with no troops left, their skill casts feel like gentle taps — because the troop multiplier is gone.

🎯 Strategic Takeaway: Troops First, Immortals Next

This leads to an important realization: if you’re deciding between boosting troop stats or Immortal stats, troop stats almost always offer the greater overall benefit.

Yes, Immortal attributes are crucial — they differentiate builds, influence skill synergy, and power up PvP matchups. But they don’t scale in the same way that troop stats do.

So your first priority should always be to increase troop count and improve troop attributes. This means investing in:

  • Castle upgrades (which increase troop cap)
  • Research and tech
  • Troop tier advancements
  • City bonuses and ownership
  • Castle skins that add troop stat buffs (e.g. Troop ATK, Troop HP)
  • Honor rank, which boosts troop stats globally

Once you’ve maximized those factors, then it’s time to turn your attention toward building Immortal attributes via gear, artifact bonuses, skill synergies, and portrait levels.

🛡️ So Are Immortal Stats Still Important?

Absolutely — just in a different way.

While troop stats carry your base power, Immortal stats allow you to tailor your setup. You can emphasize Crit for burst builds like Wu-Zhao or Cyrus. You can build high Defense and Resilience on supports like Hippo or Charles. You can boost Energy Regen on key utility Immortals like Trajan, Dido, or Matilda to enable faster ability rotations.

In this way, Immortal stats shape your identity on the battlefield. Everyone is pulling from a similar pool of troops, but Immortal builds create the variation that defines matchups.

So no — you shouldn’t ignore Immortal stats. But in terms of raw power, troop attributes win out, especially when it comes to endgame performance.

🧮 But What’s the Actual Damage Formula?

Here’s the truth: we don’t know the full damage formula. The developers have never shared it publicly, and despite the efforts of dedicated testers and theorycrafters in the community, we’ve only been able to approximate the impact of different variables.

What we do know, through testing and observation, is that:

  1. Troop count massively amplifies skill damage
  2. Troop stats are multiplied by troop count in the damage equation
  3. Immortal stats have fixed scaling based on attributes and skill coefficients
  4. Missing troops = major damage drop-off, especially for ultimates
  5. Execution timer meaning as the clock ticks the damage equation amplifies itself relative to troops and eventually even would be medium damage hits can one-shot. This is the executioner mechanic being introduced to the damage equation during the time-out meta where people made unkillable setups that would time-out any battle and thus always win a defense.

The takeaway? Build for troop sustainability and troop stat scaling, and let your Immortals guide the flavor and focus of your build.

🏁 Final Thoughts

In Infinity Kingdom, understanding the difference between troop and Immortal attributes can be the key to building a dominant march.

Troop stats give you the brute force you need to scale your damage and carry fights. Immortal stats fine-tune that power and allow you to specialize, control, and outmaneuver opponents.

So next time you’re thinking about where to invest your resources — gear upgrades, research, buffs, skins — think first about what affects troop performance at scale. Maximize that, and your Immortals will deliver truly game-changing results.

title: How to increase Physical and Magical attack – And how attributes impact damage
description: One of the most common questions new players ask in Infinity Kingdom is: “How do I raise my physical or magical attack from 3,000 to 5,000 or even 10,000+?” It’s a great question—and one that deserves a deep dive.
html:
Introduction: What Does “Attack” Really Mean?

One of the most common questions new players ask in Infinity Kingdom is: “How do I raise my physical or magical attack from 3,000 to 5,000 or even 10,000+?” It’s a great question—and one that deserves a deep dive.

First, we need to clear up a common misconception: high attack stats do not directly equal high damage output. Think of attack as a foundation. The higher your base attack, the more potential damage you can do. But actual damage depends on many other factors like skills, debuffs, enemy defenses, criticals, and damage bonuses.

The Difference Between Attack and Damage

Let’s clarify with an example:

  • A skill like Anger directly increases physical damage by 30%. This affects your actual damage output.
  • A skill like Onslaught increases physical attack by 60%. This boosts your base attack stat but doesn’t guarantee more damage—it increases the possibility of doing higher damage.Basically, attributes are all part of the damage equation, whereas Anger and other damage modifiers apply as aplification after standard damage equation is calculated. Thus much stronger.

Anyway back to attributes… So if you have 5,000 physical attack and apply a 60% bonus:

  • 5,000 x 1.6 = 8,000 physical attack
  • This will not guarantee higher damage per hit, but it will increase the ceiling of what you can hit for.

How to Increase Physical or Magical Attack

There are several core areas to focus on if you want to increase your attack stats:

1. Gears and Equipment

Max out your Immortal’s gear to max level and socket appropriate attack gems (physical or magical depending on the Immortal).

  • Gem upgrades make a big difference, especially at higher levels.

2. Artifacts

Artifacts are massive contributors to both physical and magical attack.

  • Example: A maxed-out artifact with physical attack bonuses of 42% or more can raise your total by thousands.
  • Look for artifacts with both % attack boosts and flat attack values (+350 or more).

3. Specialization Tree

Your Immortal Specialization Talents provides major boosts to attack stats.

  • Example: Each node may provide +250 magical or physical attack.
  • Fully unlocked trees can give 1,750–2,000 attack.

4. Mayor Bonuses

If you have a city mayor position that boosts attack, make use of it.

  • Not always active, but very helpful when you’re building a high stat profile.

5. Immortal Portrait Leveling

Portrait bonuses (especially at level 20) can give additional % damage or attack boosts.

  • These are especially powerful when combined with artifacts and gear.

Real Example: High-End Stats

Let’s take a look at a player like Lord Mora who has:

  • 18,776 physical attack on a fully built Chaos Wukong
  • This is thanks to:
    • Maxed artifact: 49% + 16% suffix = 65% physical attack bonus 
    • Flat bonus of +1028 from gems
    • Immortal Talent Tree maxed
    • level 50 portrait

Note: Had he rolled a flat bonus on one of the remaining suffixes on the artifact he would have even hit well above 19,000+

Now compare that to a player with 12,000 attack?

  • The 18,000 Wukong will deal higher average damage over time, but not necessarily 50% more damage every hit since the physical attack attribute is…. yes you remember from earlier: it’s part of the damage equation as one amongst multiple variables!
  • Important side note: Damage also greatly depend on critical hits, skill multipliers, and enemy resistances.

Why It Matters: Attack vs. Consistent Output

Attack boosts are important, but they serve as part of a larger equation.

  • Physical/Magical Attack increases potential output
  • Physical/Magical Damage% skills like Anger or Fire Blessing increase actual output

You want to build both.

  • Don’t just chase numbers—pair your high attack with proper damage-enhancing skills.

Final Tips for New Players

  • Start with gear and gems. Easy to upgrade and impactful early.
  • Prioritize artifacts. They scale hard with star level.
  • Invest in Dragon Specializations. They add thousands of stats.
  • Balance attack with damage%. One without the other limits your output.
  • Don’t neglect portraits. They’re slow to build but give major long-term power.

Conclusion

Raising your physical or magical attack takes time and planning. Gear, gems, artifacts, portraits, and specialization trees all work together to increase your attack stats. And remember—attack increases your damage potential, but it’s your build and skills that turn that potential into consistent, high-performance output.

Keep building, and over time you’ll hit those crazy high attribute numbers and feel the difference every battle.

Happy upgrading!

title: How to understand and use the Energy Regen attribute
description: Introduction – Why Energy Matters So Much
html:
Introduction – Why Energy Matters So Much

Energy is the heartbeat of every immortal. It’s what fuels their ultimate abilities – the big, flashy, game-defining moves that usually decide who wins the fight. Without energy, your immortals are basically swinging wet noodles – with a few exceptions.

Each immortal automatically gains energy over time, plus extra from certain buffs or abilities. Once they hit 1000 energy, they cast their ultimate.

A lot of players underestimate how much energy regen speed defines an immortal’s tempo. Whether your team cycles ultimates fast and keeps pressure up, or fires off slow, heavy-hitting bursts depends almost entirely on this stat.

How Energy Regeneration Works

All immortals regenerate energy passively every second. You can see their specific regen speed in their info window:
Open your immortal → tap Power Info → look to the bottom → for “Energy Regen”.

That number shows how much energy per second your immortal naturally gains.

For example:

  • Hippolyta: 142 energy per second → ~7 seconds to reach 1000 energy.
  • Genghis Khan: 83.1 energy per second → ~12 seconds to reach 1000 energy.

So Hippo can cast almost twice as often as Khan without any buffs. But that doesn’t mean Hippo is stronger — just that she plays faster. Khan hits harder but slower, meaning any regen buff has a bigger relative effect on him.

Why Regen Speed Changes Everything

The faster an immortal regens energy, the more ultimates they can cast in a fight. But the important nuance is how that interacts with other effects:

  • Flat energy gain (like Adrenaline Rush or Energy Burst) adds fixed energy each trigger.
  • Percentage-based buffs (like Blessing of Rage or Matilda’s ultimate) multiply your base regen rate.

So, if you’ve got a low-regen immortal like Khan, flat energy skills are more impactful. If you’re running someone with naturally high regen, percent buffs scale harder. Note that there are also other factors to consider, with Adrenaline Rush you need attack speed whereas Energy Burst needs many damage instances and high critical hit rates. However the principle remain.

Here’s an example:

  • Hippolyta gains 142 per second.
    Add Blessing of Rage (20% bonus): +28 energy per second.
  • Khan gains 83.1 per second.
    Same Blessing: +16.6 per second.

Both benefit, but Hippo gains nearly double the extra energy — that’s why Matilda and Blessing of Rage feel insane on immortals who already regen quickly. That being said, this does not mean you should never run e.g. Blessing of Rage in lightning Khan builds, the gain is still hugely valueable, but you need to understand what it actually does and how it impacts your immortals.

Examples & Synergy in Action

Here’s where this gets fun. Energy regen isn’t just about speed — it’s about timing synergy.

Take Theodora + Yi Sun-sin (YSS) as an example:

  • Theodora regen: 93.7/s
  • YSS regen: 97.6/s
    That means both hit their first ultimates around the same time — YSS at about 10.24 seconds, Theo at 10.67 seconds.

When timed right, YSS’s artifact buff (which increases healing by 30%) is active when Theo’s heal goes off. That’s free extra sustain purely from energy syncing.

Exceptions & Special Cases

A few immortals ignore or bend the energy system:

  • Alexander and Hannibal: Once you unlock their unique artifacts, their ultimates become passive — energy doesn’t matter.
  • Manco Capac: Only needs 1000 energy once; his ultimate stays active after that.
  • Control effects (like stuns, silences, and water dragon strikes) can interrupt ultimates or remove energy regen for a time (silences). If you’re unlucky, your immortal might lose energy mid-cast and never fire off.

So even with perfect regen, battlefield chaos can still ruin your timing. Always account for those disruptions in real fights.

What Affects Energy Regen

Several things modify your regen stat directly:

  • Technology:
    • Energy Surge → +5% energy regen speed.
  • Talent Trees:
    • Owl Guardian (in the Military talent tree) → +5% energy regen speed.
  • Immortal Boost Levels:
    • Total +14% at Boost 30. (5% at level 9, 5% at 19, 2% at 24, 2% at 29), read more here.
  • Artifacts (Surge Bonus Roll):
    • Available for Attack and Support types.
    • +5% base bonus, increasing with star level and quality.
    • Max caps by season:
      • S1 Bronze: 15% cap (5★)
      • S2 Silver: 20% cap (5★)
      • Conquest & Legendary (Gold): 25% cap (5★)

Stacking all these together can make a huge difference — especially for immortals who rely on frequent ultimates like Hippo, Merlin, or Himiko.

Conclusion – The Bottom Line

Energy regen isn’t just another stat — it’s the tempo of your march. It defines how often your immortals cast, how their combos line up, and how much value you get from skills and other boons.

Knowing how Energy Regen works will help you understand how to setup immortal synergies, skills and to understand combat performance as well as how to optimize your choice of setups and builds.

title: 1.Triggered skills
description: There are a lot of skills and passives which are “triggered”. Being triggered means that a certain condition has to occur in order for the skills effect to be triggered.
html:
There are a lot of skills and passives which are “triggered”. Being triggered means that a certain condition has to occur in order for the skills effect to be triggered.

Infinity Kingdom marks some skills as “Passive” and other as “Triggered” despite the fact that they are in fact both Trigger skills (for instance combo). So disregard that in the in-game text, it will only confuse you. Think of all skills that has a trigger as trigger skills!

There are many skills and passives which are “triggered”. Being triggered means that a certain condition has to occur in order for the skills effect to be triggered. For instance, using a skill like Combo, it reads that when triggered your Immortal inflicts a x% physical damage instance on the enemy Immortal being attacked. Moreover, it is indicated that the trigger condition is normal attacks. As such, when your Immortal has Combo on, there is a x% chance to trigger x% physical damage every time your Immortal performs one normal attack.

There are a few different triggered skills in Infinity Kingdom. The fundamentals are all the same:

  1. Trigger condition
  2. Once triggered inflicts skill effect

Whereas we saw a skill like Cleave or Combo being triggered from normal attacks and cause a single damage instance, another trigger skill like Chase has the trigger condition of critical hits. This means, that ANY instances of damage performed by this Immortal (ultimate ability, normal attacks or other passive skills) can all trigger the skill effect but ONLY when a critical hit is rolled.

A third trigger condition is time. Skills like Annihilation or Garrote has a timer as the trigger condition. Meaning that every x seconds the passive skills rolls and activates. With Annihilation,  every 6 seconds the a dice is rolled and you have 45% chance to activate the skill effect causing x% magical damage to all four enemy Immortals.

The same trigger condition applies for a skill like Garrote, Chaotic Blade, Toxic Nova and Fire Nova, however while the trigger condition is the same (after x seconds you have x chance to proc) the skill effects are very different from what we saw from e.g. Cleave, Combo and Annihilation.

Instead of dealing a single instance of damage when the trigger condition is true, skills like Garrote, Chaotic Blade, Toxic Nova and Fire Nova instead deal both a single instance of AOE damage + applied a DoT on your enemy. A DoT means a damage-over-time effect, which once applied ticks for additional damage over x time.

Synergies for trigger skills

It is very important that you think about especially the trigger conditions for a skill when deciding to use it in your setup. For instance, if you are running an earth march with Alexander, Charles, Zenobia and Cleopatra. You have four very different Immortals and you must play to each of their strengths. A skill such as Cleave or Combo we know is triggered through normal attack hits. This means, you want to use it on an Immortal that has a high attack speed and thus has a high hit-per-second value. Alexander is a perfect example of such an Immortal.

Moreover, because we are dealing physical damage with Combo and Cleave, you want them on an Immortal that has high physical attack. Think what would happen if you used both of these on Zenobia? She is attacking slowly and does not have particularly high physical attack attributes. As such, you would get very few triggers and low effect once triggered.

Likewise, a trigger skill such as Chase has the trigger condition of critical hits, meaning for greater effect you can synergize its use with other passives and ultimate abilities. For instance, combining Chase with Death Breath and Annihilation which provide a high amount of damage instances increases the total number of hits that can cause a critical proc. Additionally, equipping weakness on another Immortal adding to the critical hit chance further boosts the potential of chase. If you have a e.g. a fire team with William and Trajan providing crit buffs you greatly increase the effectiveness of Chase because you increase the number of crits across the damage instances of your other skills.

The same can be said about a skill like Energy Burst, which also required critical hits as its trigger condition. However, this skill provides energy regen as its skill effect and can thus be used in synergy with both magical passives like annihilation but also physical damage triggers like chaotic or cleave.

Another important thing to be aware of when creating skill synergies are your elemental dragon bonuses. They are all different in the way they interact with mechanics of your immortals and skills.

Using the lightning dragon for instance, you want to have debuffs and DoT effects on your enemies, making Chaotic Blade and Garrote particularly strong.

On fire, you want buff effects hence the following section of Blessings and Graces have inherently greater effect on a fire team.

I hope that these examples of how to think about synergies makes sense to you as the reader. I don’t like tier-lists for the simple reason that skills can never be valued at a static amount of value. The effectiveness of each and every single Immortal and ToK skill/passive you equip is 100% dependent on it’s synergy with the rest of your setup. Moreover, what is “best” to use depends on your enemy as well!

As such, you need to think about each and every decision in Infinity Kingdom, which is why I love this game!

title: 2.Blessings and Grace effects
description: Blessings and Graces are skills which function by providing a combat buff to x amount of Immortals in your march. This buff is not permanent (like with Auras) but instead temporal. They last for varying amounts of time but provide powerful buffs to your Immortals while active. Once the buff timer ru
html:
1. Blessings and Grace effects

Blessings and Graces are skills which function by providing a combat buff to x amount of Immortals in your march. This buff is not permanent (like with Auras) but instead temporal. They last for varying amounts of time but provide powerful buffs to your Immortals while active. Once the buff timer runs out, these skills will no longer provide value for the remainder of the fight.

Blessings and Graces are always applied at the beginning of a fight. Meaning that for the first x seconds of a fight your Immortals will have the buff active. Once it runs out or is dispelled it no longer provides value.

Examples of these skills are Blessing of Defense, War, Rage and other skills of the Epic tier like Oaken Guard and Resist. They provide powerful combat buffs for the beginning of the fight and are valuable in a front-loaded setup.

For instance, Blessing of Defense provides a defensive buff to all of your Immortals for the first 12 seconds of the fight, reducing the damage taken on each Immortal by 25% (at max rank). After the 12 seconds, the buff has run out, you take full damage from incoming hits and crits.

How do you know if a Blessing effect will work well in your setup then?

They provide the same buffs regardless of setup. The key to Blessings and Graces are in the purpose of the setup you are trying to build. For instance, if we are using a pure-earth setup with Charles and Zenobia in it, we are providing a lot of defensive capability to our team which over the course of a long battle will provide very high value. As such, the first 12 seconds of our fight is NOT where we are winning the battle. With this type of setup we win the battle by sustaining high troop counts throughout a prolonged battle instead. Contrary to this we could take a fire setup.

With fire, we have squishy Immortals that provide high damage and no sustain power. Our fire dragon likewise provide massive up-front damage, with very little effect in a longer battle. As such, Blessings and Graces work particularly well here. The entire purpose of the setup we want to create for our fire march is one that needs to win the battle in the beginning of the fight.

We want to deal overwhelming damage to our enemy’s troop count early on and in order to do that we want to maximize our fighting strengths in the first 12-20 seconds of the battle. Hence Graces and Blessings work excellent towards the overall purpose of our setup.

The same goes for a more tricky setup like the earth-wind hybrid, despite having strong sustain power with Zenobia, we win the fight by having Hannibal Barca and Alexander pumped up to deal massive front-loaded damage early on – sometimes almost killing the entire troop count of both enemy frontline immortals before they even get a chance to cast their ultimate’s.

All in all, Blessings and Graces are very powerful skills because of the way troop-count advantages interact in Infinity Kingdom damage calculations, but they are not for every setup.

title: All Auras synergies explained
description: In this article we are going to go over all of the auras of Infinity Kingdom and make some suggestions as to when they are useful and when they are not. You need to determine yourself what the purpose of your particular build is to figure out which auras are right for you!
html:
In this article we are going to go over all of the auras of Infinity Kingdom and make some suggestions as to when they are useful and when they are not. You need to determine yourself what the purpose of your particular build is to figure out which auras are right for you!

1. Berserk

Berserk is useful for attack-speed setups like Hannibal Barca and Alexander builds because of the attack speed buff provided and the fact that you only get value from its trigger if you have high attack speed in general. Works well in combination with things like Blessing of Speed.

2. Shelter

Shelter is a defensive trigger aura that works well against enemy teams where the total damage dealt to you is spread across many damage instances. For example, if I am fighting against a holy team which relies on a high amount of damage instances in AOE then an aura such as Shelter has very high value because it triggers from incoming attacks.  Does NOT work well against e.g. Fire where you will take large amounts of single attack damage.

3. Paralysis

Paralysis is a debuff aura which reduces the attack speed of your enemy. This should be considered a counter-skill. Meaning that it only finds value if you use to specifically counter the enemy you are facing. A prime example is when fighting against an earth-wind hybrid that relies on high attack speed Immortals in Hannibal Barca and Alexander, paralysis has very high value. However, it is next to useless against setups that relies on time-based triggers and spell casting.

4. Missleading

Missleading reduces the accuracy of your enemy’s immortals. As such, it works very well against physical damage setups. Physical attacks can be dodged providing 100% damage mitigation. However, Missleading can be countered by coercion and should only be used in synergy with other skills that provide enhanced dodge chance. For instance, it works well in a wind setup together with the wind dragon’s accuracy debuff and the After-Image blessing. It has no value at all when fighting against magic damage, since magic attacks cannot be dodged.

5. Malice

Malice reduces the critical hit chance of your enemy’s immortals. This makes the passive very useful in almost all setups, however the value from Malice is greater the more reliant your enemy is on critical hits. If you are fighting someone who use crit-trigger skills like Chase or Energy Burst then Malice has greater than normal value. Likewise, it works very well against fire setups which rely on fast burst critical damage hits. As a side note, it is in general always a good passive especially for sustain setups, because reducing the chance to take critical hits means you are smoothening incoming damage, getting more value from shields and healing. Even if you are incurring the same amount of total damage taken, having it come in smoothly across e.g. 12 seconds instead of in critical bursts means you have greater absorb rate on Charles’ shields and leaves time for healers to top off troops continuously.

6. Weakness

Weakness is a buff type aura that increases the critical strike rate of your Immortals. This is pretty simple, your chance for an attack to roll a critical hit increase the more critical strike rating you have. Since critical hits is always good value, you will always get solid output by using weakness. However, if you are running multiple marches I recommend you use weakness in a setup that scales well with critical hits. Personally, I use it in my fire second team because my fire team is highly crit-dependent and built for massive burst damage. Pairs particularly well with Chase and Energy Burst since we are boosting the trigger-rate of these skills.

7. Sacrifice

Sacrifice is an aura that has a chance to increase your Immortals energy by x amount. However, this is not the significant part of this passive. What you are looking for in this passive is its buff that provides an x% increase to damage dealt by two of your other three Immortals. It should therefore always be equipped on a support Immortal and is best used when at least two of the remaining Immortals deal significant damage. Can work well in a water march on dido or in Fire if you are running Cyrus. I have also seen it used on Charles in earth setups where Zenobia is swapped out for Bathory or Genghis Khan.

8. Coercion

Coercion is a debuff type aura, that provides increased accuracy to all of your Immortals. As such, you get very high value from this aura in a physical heavy setup. If you e.g. have Bathory and Alexander, Barca and Atalanta, or Manco and Gilgamesh as your primary damage dealers, then coercion is a must have passive to make sure you get as close to hit-cap as possible (and do not miss attacks). On the complete opposite side, if you are running a dual-mage setup, coercion is almost useless since magic attacks cannot miss to begin with and therefore require no accuracy stat.

9. Fear of Domination

Fear of Domination is the newest aura of the bunch. It was added with the new Tower of Knowledge skills and require Triss event skill stones to unlock. Not a lot of players have this avilable to them, but when you do you will find that it works quite well for most setups to be honest. You will however find far superior value from using this passive in big nuke burst setups. Fire setups for instance, where the dragon itself get’s you a nice troop reduction on the enemy right off the bat. Likewise, it is very powerful on shadow marches.

title: 3.Auras
description: These skills are tower of knowledge passive which provide a combat buffs and debuffs passively to Immortals. Auras are in general all powerful skills and as such they are also limited in use.
html:
These skills are tower of knowledge passive which provide a combat buffs and debuffs passively to Immortals. Auras are in general all powerful skills and as such they are also limited in use.

You can only equip one aura on each Immortal, simply because being able to load up three auras on a support Immortal would make hard support Immortals too powerful.

As a class of skills there is not much to know about auras besides the fact that:

  1. You can only equip one aura per Immortal
  2. Auras passively provide their unique effect throughout the entire battle

Synergies

As for synergies with Auras it is very important that you have a clear read on the purpose of your setup as well as that of your enemy.

For instance, if I am fighting against a holy team which relies on a high amount of damage instances in AOE then an aura such as Shelter has very high value because it triggers from incoming attacks.

Some buff-auras like Shelter here and Berserk has a trigger condition just like what we talked about in the guide on Trigger skills. Shelter triggers from taking incoming damage and Berserk from successfully landing an attack, as such Berserk finds it value in attack-speed centric setups where it’s attack speed buff and sustain-trigger effects have greater value.

Another Aura Weakness provide its buff passively like a Blessing or Grace but without an expiry timer and they are not despellable.

Lastly, the debuff type auras such as Coercion, Paralysis, Misleading and Malice should be used based on your enemy in combat. These also work just like a Grace effect, but without an expiration timer and they are not despellable.

Think about what your setup is weak against and use an aura to bolster your defense against those setups.

  • Berserk and Shelter are Trigger-based auras
  • Berserk, Coercion, Paralysis, Missleading and Malice are debuff auras
  • Weakness and Sacrifice are buff auras

Auras are in general very powerful, but because they are also very limited in how you can use them, you must think long and hard about which aura’s play to the advantages of your own setup as well as what your main rivals you most often fight are using. So when you are using a fire burst team you want to run auras like Sacrifice and Weakness and when you face magic damage teams run malice to defend.

Likewise, you want to avoid coercion and berserk if you rely yourself on magic damage, but you must run them both if you are running an Alex + Barca setup. If you are faced with hard holy or earth enemies shelter can be very helpful but against Merlin waters it’s effect is a lot less.

If you want to read more about each of the aura passive skills of Infinity Kingdom, checkout my guide on Aura synergies here

title: Different skill mechanics (Triggered, Passives, Graces, Blessings, Aura)
description: Infinity Kingdom has a variety of different skills and passives. These in turn all have unique effects and have different mechanics in the way they interact in combat scenarios. For instance, an Aura type passive work very different to a proc-chance trigger ability/passive and entirely different too
html:
Infinity Kingdom has a variety of different skills and passives. These in turn all have unique effects and have different mechanics in the way they interact in combat scenarios. For instance, an Aura type passive work very different to a proc-chance trigger ability/passive and entirely different too from how graces and blessings function. Moreover, damage proc’s can both occur and trigger in different ways, some are DoT (damage over time) functions where others are bursty procs. Some trigger from hits, some time, some crits.

The large variation to how skills and passives works in Infinity Kingdom is what makes this game such an awesome experience. You can synergize skills to great effect if you understand a few fundamentals of how the mechanic’s work. This, however, also leads to confusion, since there is a decent degree of complexity in Infinity Kingdom and has given rise to a bunch of player questions regarding how skills and passives functions and interact.

As such, I have promised to make a guide in which I will attempt to explain the fundamental types of skills and passives and how their mechanics should be understood. I will not be going into great detail with every single passive in the game, if you want more information on a particular passive let me know and I will do a thorough Passive Review guide for that. Instead, what we are going to do today is outline classes of passives and explain how each work and how you can think about them in terms of synergizing with passives and other Immortals.

Tower of Knowledge Passives & Immortal Skill classes

  • Triggered skills
  • Blessings & Grace effects
  • Auras
  • Passives

Brief overview of each class of skills

For a more in-depth explanation of each and recommended synergies click on the class of skills you want to know more about to read a full review.

Triggered skills

There are a lot of skills and passives which are “triggered”. Being triggered means that a certain condition has to occur in order for the skills effect to be triggered.

Infinity Kingdom marks some skills as “Passive” and other as “Triggered” despite the fact that they are in fact both Trigger skills (for instance combo). So disregard that in the in-game text, it will only confuse you. Think of all skills that has a trigger as trigger skills!

Take this example: Using a skill like Combo, it reads that when triggered your Immortal inflicts a x% physical damage instance on the enemy Immortal being attacked. Moreover, it is indicated that the trigger condition is normal attacks. As such, when your Immortal has Combo on, there is a x% chance to trigger x% physical damage every time your Immortal performs one normal attack.

On another skill like the Chaotic Blade or one of the magic DoT effects, we have a timer as the trigger.

There are a few different triggered skills in Infinity Kingdom. The fundamentals are all the same:

  1. Trigger condition
  2. Once triggered inflicts skill effect

They do however differ greatly in terms of both trigger condition and skill effects. Read more about the different trigger skills, their conditions and differences in trigger effects here.

Blessings and Grace effects

Blessings and Graces are skills which function by providing a combat buff to x amount of Immortals in your march. This buff is not permanent (like with Auras) but instead temporal. They last for varying amounts of time but provide powerful buffs to your Immortals while active.

Once the buff timer runs out, these skills will no longer provide value for the remainder of the fight. Blessings and Graces are always applied at the beginning of a fight. Meaning that for the first x seconds of a fight your Immortals will have the buff active. Once it runs out or is dispelled it no longer provides value.

Read more about the different Blessings & Graces here

Auras

This leads nicely into Aura skills. These skills are tower of knowledge passive which provide a combat buffs and debuffs passively to Immortals.

Auras are in general all powerful skills and as such they are also limited in use. You can only equip one aura on each Immortal, simply because being able to load up three auras on a support Immortal would make hard support Immortals too powerful. As a class of skills there is not much to know about auras besides the fact that:

  1. You can only equip one aura per Immortal
  2. Auras passively provide their unique effect throughout the entire battle

Read more about all the auras and their syngeries here

Passives

Lastly, we have the passive type of Tower of Knowledge and Immortal skills. Passives are quite simple. It means that their effects are permanent and applied at all times when equipped. They need no trigger, have no duration timer, cannot be despelled. They simply provide their boon and that’s it!

Examples of Passive skills are Rage, Concentration, Anger, Duel Master, Fighting Master. Some of them are very very powerful. Read more about passives here

title: Passive Skills
description: Passive Tower of Knowledge skills are skills which provide their effects permanently when equipped. They only work on the single Immortal they are equipped but they need no trigger, have no duration timer, cannot be despelled. They simply provide their boon and that’s it!
html:
Passive Tower of Knowledge skills are skills which provide their effects permanently when equipped. They only work on the single Immortal they are equipped but they need no trigger, have no duration timer, cannot be despelled. They simply provide their boon and that’s it!

There are a few different types of Passive Skills. They have three purposes:

  1. Offensive
  2. Defensive
  3. Utility

1. Offensive Passives

For offensive passives you have skills such as Concentration, Anger, Duel Master, Rage. These provide a flat bonus to your Immortal which increase the damage dealt by your Immortal.

For instance, Concentration boosts a mage’s magical damage dealt by 30% (MASSIVE) and likewise ít’s counterpart Anger provides 30% more physical damage dealt (also MASSIVE).

2. Defensive Passives

Defensive Passives such as Physical Shield and Magical Shield, provides a flat boost to your defenses. As their names suggest, Physical Shield gives you enhanced protection against physical damage and makes your single Immortal take 30% less physical damage. Likewise, Magical Shield provides 30% less magical damage taken.

3. Utility Passives

These are some of the most interesting skills in all of Infinity Kingdom. They are extreemly powerful to use as hard counters against certain enemy setups. They provide highly specific and niche buffs / Immunities to your Immortals.

For example, Duel Master can be used for extreem value against an enemy wounds-setup. If you have a healer, then you will die hard to wounds. But with Duel Master, you can ensure that one of your core damage dealing Immortals keeps being healed.

Same concept for another skill like Fighting Master. This one provides immunity to Control Effects (does not work on Himiko). This is likewise extreemly powerful against certain setups. For instance if you fight against an earth team, being Immune to dragon stun provides a huge advantage!
