title: 🗡️ Knife Through Butter: The Energy-Shredder That Could Make the Next Version of Hybrid-builds
description: Infinity Kingdom’s next patch introduces one of the most disruptive Tower of Knowledge skills we’ve seen in years: Knife Through Butter. At first glance, its raw damage looks unremarkable — but its energy drain mechanic makes it potentially meta-breaking.
html:
Infinity Kingdom’s next patch introduces one of the most disruptive Tower of Knowledge skills we’ve seen in years: Knife Through Butter. At first glance, its raw damage looks unremarkable — but its energy drain mechanic makes it potentially meta-breaking.

This skill doesn’t just punish the current hyper-regen meta — it may also bring back the long-forgotten Earth–Wind hybrid archetype, putting physical carries like Alexander the Great back in the spotlight.

🔎 What Knife Through Butter Does

Skill Details:

  • Type: Physical, Attack-triggered
  • Effect: Normal attacks have a 60% chance to remove 300 Energy from all enemy Immortals
  • Proc Chance: 60% per 6 normal attack, thus scaling with attack speed.
  • Target: All enemies simultaneously

🚩 Why It’s a Big Deal

1. Hard Counter to Hyper-Regen Meta

Right now, many Conquest battles revolve around regen-based comps — teams that chain ultimates endlessly through energy boosts. These teams thrive on casting before you can react.

Knife Through Butter flips that on its head:

  • Every proc robs the entire enemy team of 300 energy.
  • With high attack speed, enemies may never reach ultimate thresholds.
  • Result: Heals, shields, and CC chains collapse.

2. Revival and evolution of Hybrid Teams

For several seasons, hybrids (earth wind) have struggled in the regen backline-centered meta. With Knife Through Butter, hybrids finally have a disruptive tool that rewards their natural strengths:

  • High attack speed carries like Alexander, Hannibal when boosted by Zeno and Qin for attack speed can proc this constantly.
  • By draining energy, they prevent enemy from cycling their devastating ultimates.
  • The freed-up space lets hybrids’ sustained DPS shine again.

The next evolution of Hybrid will be Alex-Ares frontline!?

In short: Hybrids get relevance back — not by brute force, but by shutting down the opponent’s key win condition. Perhaps even as a new version with Ares? I personally think so.

📊 Numbers That Matter

Let’s put the impact of Knife Through Butter into context, using a common hybrid setup:

  • Attack Speed Setup: With standard hybrid builds (e.g., Alexander running Wind Rage and Berserker), achieving 3-4 attacks per second is common in prolonged battles.
  • Proc Mechanics: With a 60% chance per 6 attacks attack, at 3 attacks per second, you average 1.8 procs per second (60% × 3 = .9 procs).
  • Energy Drain Impact: At each proc, you drain 300 Energy from each enemy Immortal. Averaging .9 procs per second gives us approximately 270 Energy drained per second from each enemy Immortal—an absolutely staggering number.

The idea is simple yet effective:

  • DPS #1 shuts down enemy ultimates by continuous energy drain.
  • DPS #2 quickly bursts down priority targets who become vulnerable due to interrupted heals, controls and shields.

🎯 How It Fits Into Conquest Meta

Hybrid Resurgence

  • Earth–Wind hybrids with Alexander and Hannibal suddenly look dangerous again.
  • With Knife Through Butter, they can suppress backline enery regen based builds that otherwise ramping up damage.

More Attack-Speed Builds

  • Expect Wind Rage, Berserker, and other speed-enhancers to become mandatory.

Whale Must-Have

  • For spenders, this skill will likely be required for top Conquest matches.
  • Any team without energy control will risk being steamrolled by Knife Through Butter comps.

Implications

  • Skills like Energy Suppression may see renewed relevance as synergies to constant energy drain.
  • Teams that rely less on ultimate cycles (like raw crit Khan comps) will adapt faster.

🏆 Final Thoughts

Knife Through Butter isn’t just another skill — it’s a meta-shifter. By introducing large-scale energy disruption, it dismantles regen-based setups and opens the door for hybrid physical builds to thrive again.

  • For Whales: It’s almost mandatory. If you want to compete at the very top, you’ll need it.
  • For Mid-Spenders: It’s a ticket to punch above your weight, especially in Conquest battlegroups dominated by regen comps.
  • For the Meta: Expect hybrid marches (Alex-Hannibal earth wind) to climb back to the top.

⚡ Verdict: This is a very interesting skill and one that in the right build may be the most broken energy skill so far? Right now it looks strong but not broken, but I think that once whales figure out how to setup Alexander-Ares hybrids, we are going to see some new top builds and a new hybrid era… time will tell!

title: Last Stand
description: Skill News: Introducing the new Chaos skill the “Last Stand” Skill in Infinity Kingdom
html:
Skill News: Introducing the new Chaos skill the “Last Stand” Skill in Infinity Kingdom

“Last Stand” is the latest addition to the arsenal of Tower of Knowledge skills in Infinity Kingdom, specifically within the chaos category. This guide will delve into the mechanics of this formidable skill, its implications in the game’s meta, particularly for high-level play, and what makes it a significant investment for the biggest spenders in the game.

Skill Overview

Availability and Cost

“Last Stand” is a chaos-tier skill, which is the highest rarity for skills in Infinity Kingdom. It requires a substantial investment to unlock and maximize:

  • Skill Stones Needed: To fully upgrade “Last Stand,” players need 290 skill stones.
  • Acquisition: Available exclusively through wishes during the Triss event.
  • Expected Cost: With an average drop chance of 4%, acquiring enough skill stones for “Last Stand” could necessitate around 7,000 wishes, making it one of the most expensive items in the game.

Skill Mechanics

  • Activation Condition: “Last Stand” activates when your troops are below 70% of their total count.
  • Effects:
    • Damage Reduction: Reduces damage taken by 60%.
    • Damage Increase: Boosts damage dealt by 60%.

Strategic Implications

Comparisons to Existing Skills

“Last Stand” offers the combined benefits of multiple top-tier defensive and offensive skills, but in a single slot: Comparatively, Physical shield and Anger has been used for three years now as some of the strongest skills to respectively reducing incoming damage and increase your damage dealt.

These are a great comparison for this skill as using two skill slots on physical and magical shield gives you a solid 30% damage taken reduction – half of what this skill does! Albeit you gain the effect only under 70% troop count, but still incredble! Combine that with 2x anger (anger = 30% damage buff) and this single skill has the inherent value of 2x physical shield, 2x magical shield and 2x anger/concentration. But it takes up one slot!

  • Physical and Magical Shield: Normally, occupying two skill slots to achieve a 30% damage reduction, “Last Stand” provides double that reduction under its activation condition.
  • Anger/Concentration: Similarly, while each of these skills provides a 30% damage boost, “Last Stand” doubles this effect as well.

Looking at a chaos setup with Last Stand available it is going to be very difficult to deal real impactful damage to their key damage dealer, and at the same time you will take massive amounts of incoming damage if you are able to even break the 70% barrier and reach activation! Scary skill for sure!

Meta Impact

The introduction of “Last Stand” is poised to significantly influence the strategic choices at the highest levels of play, particularly among players who can afford the heavy investment (whales):

  • Breakthrough Capability: In a meta dominated by dual healer backlines, “Last Stand” offers a potential counter by significantly enhancing both the survivability and damage output of chaos immortals.
  • Shift from Defense to Offense: Its powerful effects may encourage top players to rethink strategies that heavily favor sustain and defense, potentially reducing the prevalence of immortals like Theodora in favor of more offensive or balanced setups.

Considerations for Use

Build Synergy

  • Critical Thresholds: Players will need to manage their troop health strategically to ensure “Last Stand” activates when most needed.
  • Complementary Skills: Pairing “Last Stand” with skills that enhance energy recovery, critical hits, or further damage mitigation can amplify its effectiveness.

Whale Territory

  • Given its cost and the rarity of required resources, “Last Stand” is realistically only accessible to the game’s biggest spenders. This exclusivity ensures that its impact, while potentially meta-defining, will be confined to the upper echelons of player rankings.

Conclusion

“Last Stand” embodies a significant evolution in the strategic dynamics of Infinity Kingdom. Its potent combination of defensive and offensive enhancements in a single skill slot sets it apart as a potential game-changer for those who can afford to integrate it into their builds. As more top-tier players begin to unlock and deploy this skill, its true effect on the game’s competitive meta will become clearer. For now, it remains a symbol of high-stake investments yielding potentially unmatched battlefield supremacy.

title: Life Link – How does it actually work?
description: The Life Link Tower of Knowledge Passive is a powerful ability featured in various fantasy role-playing games and is notably known for its defensive and offensive capabilities. This passive ability allows the user to establish a Life Link with two enemy units every six seconds after the battle begin
html:
The Life Link Tower of Knowledge Passive is a powerful ability featured in various fantasy role-playing games and is notably known for its defensive and offensive capabilities. This passive ability allows the user to establish a Life Link with two enemy units every six seconds after the battle begins, providing a unique and strategic advantage during combat. In this article we explore precisely how this works. Is damage shared? Or do we reduce the damage we take when we run Life Link? I asked the development team to make sure.

Official Description: The official description of the Life Link Tower of Knowledge Passive states that, once activated, there is a 50% chance of creating a Life Link with two enemy units. This Life Link enables the sharing of received damage, specifically 50%, between the user and the linked enemies. The Life Link remains active for a duration of 6 seconds.

Defensive and Offensive Mechanisms

The Life Link Tower of Knowledge Passive skill serves a dual purpose, both as a defensive mechanism and as an offensive tool. Many players often question whether it functions as damage mitigation or a thorns mechanic. However, the true nature of this ability lies in its unique damage transfer mechanism.

When an Immortal character possesses the Life Link Tower of Knowledge Passive, they are able to mitigate incoming damage, resulting in a reduced overall impact. The portion of damage mitigated by Life Link on our own Immortal is then transferred to the linked enemies, transforming it into offensive damage against them. This innovative mechanic allows the user to capitalize on the damage they would have otherwise sustained, turning it into an opportunity to harm their adversaries.

Strength and Importance

Undoubtedly, the Life Link Tower of Knowledge Passive skill is considered exceptionally powerful due to its versatile nature and the strategic advantages it provides during combat. With the ability to significantly reduce the damage taken while simultaneously retaliating against enemies, it offers a distinct edge in battles, making the Immortal wielding this skill a formidable force on the battlefield.

Especially in situations where you are faced with a prolongued fight with consistent damage. Life Link has a pretty high uptime making for an amazing mitigation and offensive capacity against e.g. holy setups or on a tank facing an enemy Alexander.

The strength of the Life Link Tower of Knowledge Passive lies in its ability to turn defense into offense, creating a symbiotic relationship between damage reduction and counterattacks. This makes it a highly sought-after skill among players and a crucial asset for those seeking to excel in combat scenarios.

In conclusion, the Life Link Tower of Knowledge Passive is a remarkable ability that enhances the defensive and offensive capabilities of Immortal characters in fantasy role-playing games. With its unique damage transfer mechanism, it provides a means to mitigate incoming damage while simultaneously dealing a blow to adversaries. Its strength and versatility make it an invaluable asset, cementing its reputation as a potent and highly sought-after skill in the gaming world.

Lightning Strike Skill Guide – Tower of Knowledge Passive

In this guide, we take a deep dive into one of the newer legendary skills in Infinity Kingdom: Lightning Strike. Whether you’re testing it out on your mid-tier marches or considering it for one of your top squads, this skill introduces a unique dynamic to physical damage teams—especially those built around seriously wound synergies.

We’ll walk through what the skill does, how it works, best Immortal pairings, purchasing info, and some practical insights from player testing.

Lightning Strike – What It Does

You’ll find Lightning Strike in the Tower of Knowledge, right near Soul Synergy. As of now, it’s a legendary skill with position restrictions and a damage + debuff mechanic.

Skill Description:

  • Trigger: Every 12 seconds (70% chance)
  • Effect: Deals physical damage (Damage Rate: 90% + 30%/level) to all enemies and increases their damage taken by (3% + 1%/level) for 6 seconds
  • Bonus: If the target is seriously wounded, the damage is increased by 50%

Damage benchmark

Overall the damage from Lightning Strike averages out at 70% physical damage per second placing it above older skills such as Chaotic Blade etc., and generally quite high compared to other physical damage skills. What is more interesting however, is looking at the damage while condition is met. With an activation from Wounds (which you can have constant uptime on quite easily) you are getting 105% damage per second, which places is very high on the list of skills behind only skills like Blade Vortex and Drastic Action. In essence, this is a must have for Wounds-based setups and not the best in others.

💡 Quick Tip: The skill is reportedly being buffed in a future patch, reducing the cooldown from 12s → 9s, which will increase uptime and DPS significantly.

Brining it down to just 9s cooldown will further increase its usefulness taking the damage average to 93.33% DPS and a whopping 140% while wounds is active. Very impressive!

How to Get Lightning Strike

Lightning Strike is a pay-to-acquire skill (currently exclusive):

  • Cost: $140 total through the Recharge event
  • You’ll receive the required skill stones across the tiers in the event

At the time of writing, free-to-play access is not available, so this skill is only for players who are willing to spend.

Ideal Immortals for Lightning Strike

Due to its physical damage type and position restrictions, Lightning Strike works best on high-attack melee Immortals, especially those in physical-heavy or lightning-focused teams.

Top Picks:

🗡️ Alexander the Great

  • High physical attack (~10k+ with gear)
  • Excellent synergy in frontline burst setups
  • Compatible with Time to Shine, Fighting Master, and Chase

🗡️ Genghis Khan

  • Works great in backline physical builds
  • If running dual seriously wound Immortals (like Khan + Qin), Lightning Strike gets its 50% bonus damage consistently

🛡️ Hannibal Barca

  • Another powerful physical option
  • Less commonly used in current meta but still viable in tanky, retaliate-style teams

💡 Note: Lightning Strike is not available to Chaos Immortals or Magic/Support units, and is best left to main damage dealers in the front or backline.

Theorycrafting: Seriously Wounded Synergy

The real power of Lightning Strike comes from the bonus 50% damage if the target is seriously wounded. This makes it ideal in setups where:

  • You run two wound-inflicting Immortals
  • You have high uptime on wound effects from fast energy regeneration

One test setup:

  • Frontline: Alexander + Khan
  • Backline: Qin + Tokugawa
  • Result: Lightning Strike dealt 7M damage in a 38s battle, thanks to high uptime on wounds

While performance varies by matchup and timing, the synergy potential is very real when wound uptime is consistent.

Practical Testing & Performance

  • In tests, Lightning Strike performed reliably with 1.5x damage multipliers
  • Performance depends heavily on:
    • Wound uptime
    • Immortal attack stat (Khan with low attack didn’t benefit as much)
    • Fight duration (short fights = fewer triggers)
  • Optimal when paired with fast energy regen units and frontline sustain

It won’t always shine in short skirmishes but scales well in drawn-out battles or PvE boss fights where uptime is king.

Should You Buy It? Final Thoughts

🔥 Pros:

  • Unique AoE + debuff combination
  • Strong synergy with meta wound-based builds
  • Getting buffed soon (cooldown from 12s to 9s)
  • Great on staple Immortals like Alex and Khan

🧊 Cons:

  • Paywalled behind $140 recharge event.
  • Limited to physical attackers with positioning constraints
  • Dependent on synergy to hit full potential

✅ Recommendation:

If you’re a spender building physical DPS teams, Lightning Strike is a worthy addition—especially once the cooldown buff goes live. It’s not a must-have, but it’s a high-ceiling skill when used with the right team setup.

Summary – Lightning Strike at a Glance

Player Guide: Harnessing the Power of “Misleading” in Infinity Kingdom

“Misleading” is a Tower of Knowledge skill in Infinity Kingdom that offers significant defensive potential but requires careful consideration and strategic deployment to be effective. It’s a skill that either defines a battle or becomes a wasted slot, depending on the context and enemy builds. This guide explores how to maximize the effectiveness of “Misleading” and integrate it into your battle strategy.

Skill Mechanics

Core Functionality

  • Effect: “Misleading” is an aura skill that reduces the Accuracy Rate of all enemy units by 20% for the duration of the fight.
  • Impact: A reduced accuracy rate increases the likelihood that enemy attacks will miss your units, effectively making “Misleading” one of the strongest defensive measures available—when it works.

Strategic Application

Understanding Accuracy and Dodge

  • Dodge vs. Accuracy: Battles in Infinity Kingdom are influenced by two opposing attributes—Dodge rate and Accuracy. While Dodge increases your chances of evading an attack, Accuracy is designed to counteract this and ensure hits land.
  • Balancing Act: The effectiveness of “Misleading” hinges on having a higher Dodge rate than the enemy’s Accuracy. If successful, it forces the enemy to miss attacks, which means zero damage dealt during those instances.

Ideal Use Cases

  • High Dodge Builds: “Misleading” excels in builds that naturally have high Dodge rates or are enhanced through other skills and artifacts that boost evasion, such as “After-Image” or Manco’s unique artifact.
  • Enemy Build Analysis: Before deploying “Misleading,” it’s crucial to analyze the likely builds of your opponents. If they invest heavily in Accuracy through their immortals’ attributes, dragon talents, or skills like “Coercion,” the effectiveness of “Misleading” diminishes.

Tactical Considerations

When to Use Misleading

  • Effective Scenarios: Use “Misleading” when you know your opponents have lower Accuracy investments. This is often more feasible in controlled environments or where you have good intelligence on enemy setups.
  • Risky Deployments: Avoid using “Misleading” in high-stakes battles without prior knowledge of the enemy’s build, as it could potentially waste a valuable skill slot if the enemy has high Accuracy.

Building Around Misleading

  • Complementary Skills and Gear: Enhance the effectiveness of “Misleading” by equipping your immortals with gear and skills that increase Dodge rates. This synergistic approach maximizes the chances of enemy attacks missing, leveraging the full defensive potential of “Misleading.”
  • Strategic Immortal Placement: Consider placing immortals with “Misleading” in positions where they can affect the maximum number of enemies, especially against high-damage dealers whose impact you want to mitigate.

Conclusion

“Misleading” offers a powerful defensive capability in Infinity Kingdom, potentially turning the tide of battle by causing enemy attacks to miss. However, its effectiveness is highly contingent on the relative Dodge and Accuracy attributes of engaged forces. Properly utilized, it can render your army nearly untouchable, but it requires careful preparation and a deep understanding of both your and your enemy’s builds. As with any strategy, the key to success with “Misleading” lies in adaptability and informed decision-making, ensuring that each slot in your Tower of Knowledge is optimized for maximum impact on the battlefield.

Mastering the “No Escape” Skill in the Tower of Knowledge

Welcome to the thrilling world of Infinity Kingdom! The “No Escape” skill, a recent addition to the Tower of Knowledge, is a game-changing Pay to Play (P2P) skill. Introduced in the “Blessings of Triss” event, it’s a high-impact control skill that can radically alter the course of battle.

Basics

Type: P2P Skill Investment: Approx. $700 on average to unlock efficiently.
Availability: “Blessings of Triss” event Power Level: High-impact, game-changer control skill

While the skill’s damage is low, its silence and stun controls are incredibly potent, effectively countering most setups, especially those relying on holy elements.

Comprehensive Player’s Guide to “Oaken Guard” in Infinity Kingdom

Hey fellow Infinity Kingdom gamer! Let’s talk about one of the coolest skills in the game – “Oaken Guard.” It’s not just another skill; it’s a game-changer in the current physical-centric meta. Ready to learn why? Here we go!

Understanding the Power of “Oaken Guard”

The Ideal Defense Against Physical Attacks

“Oaken Guard” is essentially your virtual shield in the game. What makes it so awesome? This skill reduces all physical damage taken for the first 18 seconds of a fight. Considering how common physical attacks are in the game, this skill is incredibly powerful. Imagine if my enemy has oaken guard active in the above fight. Dealing 48 million physical damage in 34 seconds, for simplicity say we deal the same DPS throughout the fight (we deal a bit more with graces early, but then more later with execute, so let’s call it even). That is around 24 million damage dealt in the first 18 seconds meaning my enemy could have “shielded” themselves for 12 million damage with Oaken Guard. That is insane value for a single ToK skill and very well explains the core value proposition of this skill: Physical defense against quick burst front-loaded physical damage.

A Versatile Shield Against Various Setups

The skill is obviously amazing versus Hybrids, but it is very strong against all of the physical damage setups, e.g.:

  1. Seon Fire Teams: It shines against Seon’s fiery assaults, turning their intense attacks into mere sparks.

  5. General Physical Setups: Overall, “Oaken Guard” is your go-to defense against almost every physical attack setup in the game.

Since “Oaken Guard” impacts your entire team, placing it on a non-primary damage dealer (like a support or tank) is a smart move. This allows you to maximize your team’s overall performance without sacrificing offensive capabilities.

Wrapping It Up

“Oaken Guard” is a stellar skill in Infinity Kingdom, especially valuable in the current physical attack-dominated meta. It’s your shield against a variety of physical attacks, making it a must-have in most battles. However, remember to switch strategies against magic-centric teams or chaos Loki builds.

Use this guide to harness the full potential of “Oaken Guard” in your battles. Equip it wisely, and let it be your shield against the fiercest of enemies!

n the realm of Infinity Kingdom, where strategy and skill intertwine, the “Purification” ability emerges as a unique and nuanced skill that can significantly influence the tide of battles. You can despell control effects as well as wounds using this skill making it highly effective and sought after for many builds.
  • Healing Aspect: The healing part of Purification is based on the HP of the source and has a recovery rate of 160%. This rate, though modest, ensures consistent healing with each activation.
  • Synergy: Beyond all the valuable aspects of the skill itself, it has further value for you as a result of its synergy with the skill Wine and Dine. As one of the most frequent healing skills you can get high uptime on Wine and Dine buffs by pairing it with Purification. Very powerful and worth consideration.

Mastering Siren’s Gaze: A Strategic Guide for Infinity Kingdom Players

Welcome to the deep dive into one of the most intriguing and tactical skills available in the Tower of Knowledge: Siren’s Gaze. Unlike the straightforward damage-dealing or damage-mitigating skills, Siren’s Gaze brings a layer of cunning strategy and battlefield control that can significantly sway the tide of battle in your favor. Let’s unravel the mechanics of this skill, its benefits, and how to synergize it for maximum effect in your lineup.

Understanding Siren’s Gaze

At its core, Siren’s Gaze is a skill that manipulates the battlefield dynamics in a subtle yet impactful way. With a 75% chance every 12 seconds, it taunts a random enemy backline immortal for 6 seconds, forcing them to target the immortal wielding Siren’s Gaze. This redirection of focus is not just about drawing fire; it’s about strategic manipulation of enemy actions.

The Power of Siren’s Shell

Activation of Siren’s Gaze automatically triggers the Siren’s Shell effect. During the taunt, any enemy that attacks the targeted immortal is silenced for 1 second. This silence is a potent control effect, preventing enemies from casting ultimate abilities and halting their energy regeneration. Considering that backline enemies often rely on their ultimates for significant impact, silencing them can severely cripple the enemy’s offensive capabilities.

Strategic Implementation of Siren’s Gaze

Choosing the Right Immortal: Siren’s Gaze shines brightest when equipped on an immortal that can withstand the increased attention, such as those with high durability or evasion rates. However, its unique synergy with damage output makes it especially appealing for damage-dealing immortals who can benefit from the taunt mechanic, like Khubilai Khan, William, or Ragnar.

Synergy with Toxin Barrier: Pairing Siren’s Gaze with Toxin Barrier creates a formidable combo. The taunt ensures that your immortal takes a significant number of hits, activating Toxin Barrier’s damage mechanism frequently. This setup is particularly effective on damage-dealing immortals, turning them into both a beacon for enemy attention and a source of relentless damage.

Tactical Tips for Siren’s Gaze

  • Positioning is Key: Place your Siren’s Gaze-equipped immortal strategically to maximize the number of enemies affected by the silence. Ideally, you want them positioned in such a way that they draw fire from both the taunted backline and the enemy frontline.
  • Timing Matters: Given its 12-second cycle, timing Siren’s Gaze with enemy ultimate abilities can disrupt their rhythm and reduce their effectiveness in battle.
  • Complementary Skills: Beyond Toxin Barrier, look for skills that either benefit from the increased attention your immortal will receive or that offer additional control and damage as enemies are drawn in and silenced.

Conclusion

Siren’s Gaze offers a unique approach to battlefield control, emphasizing strategic manipulation over brute force. By taunting enemy backline immortals and silencing attackers, this skill can disrupt enemy formations and ultimate ability usage, providing a significant advantage. When paired with the right skills and strategies, Siren’s Gaze can turn your immortal into a pivotal control piece in your lineup, capable of swinging battles in your favor with its cunning influence. Harness the power of Siren’s Gaze, and watch as your enemies fall silent before your strategic might.

Becoming a sniper

Sniper is distinguished by its capacity to inflict significant damage on key enemy combatants, particularly those stationed in the rear echelons of the opposing formation. The skill’s design allows players to tactically eliminate or weaken pivotal backline adversaries, such as a primary damage dealer, thereby disrupting the enemy’s strategic framework and diminishing their overall combat efficacy.

Strategic Deployment

Aligning with Battle Formations

Understanding the enemy formation is crucial. By positioning your Sniper-equipped Immortal appropriately, you can ensure the skill targets the enemy’s key backline unit. This requires careful observation of opponent setups and predicting their strategic placements.

Synergistic Pairings

The synergy between Sniper and control skills, such as those possessed by Himiko, amplifies its strategic value. For instance, pairing Sniper with Himiko’s ability to target the backliner with the highest troop count allows for tailored control and damage focus. Tactical Examples

Player Guide: The most important bad skill in Infinity Kingdom

Stormeye, a Tower of Knowledge skill in Infinity Kingdom, often finds itself overshadowed by more potent damaging and debuff skills. This guide aims to shed light on its effectiveness, strategic use, and an often overlooked benefit of strategically not completing its acquisition.

Overview of Stormeye

Stormeye is designed primarily as a damage-dealing skill with the following mechanics:

  • Official Skill Description: “Every 6 seconds after the battle starts, has a 55% chance of causing Magical Damage (250%) to 3 random enemy units. If the target is under Root effects, Stormeye’s damage increased by 50%.”

Despite its potential for higher damage under specific conditions, Stormeye generally offers lower damage output compared to other skills available in the game.

Comparing DPS Efficiency

When evaluated against other magical damage-dealing skills, Stormeye falls short:

  • DPS without Root: Stormeye averages 68.75% DPS, significantly lower than Toxin Nova and Fire Nova, both of which average around 81.25% DPS.
  • DPS with Root: Potential DPS can rise to 103% if the target is rooted, but achieving this consistently is challenging due to the sporadic nature of Root effects in most battle setups.

Strategic Limitations

The key limitation of Stormeye lies in its reliance on Root effects to maximize its damage output. The narrow window for exploiting this feature, coupled with the lack of additional debuff effects (which skills like Spell Disintegration and Poison Thorn offer), severely limits its utility:

  • Root Dependency: Effective only when used in conjunction with immortals or skills that can reliably apply Root, such as Fighting Will.
  • Inconsistent Performance: Without consistent Root effects, Stormeye’s damage output is often outperformed by other skills that also bring valuable debuffs or higher base damage.

An Unconventional Strategic Advantage

So why is Stormeye the most important bad skill in Infinity Kingdom? We see that it dosen’t deal great damage, but it isn’t useless. It’s just not as good as the other skills in the same category. What makes this skill extreemly valuable is actually not owning it.

Stormeye’s relative underperformance can be turned into a strategic advantage. As one of the weaker skills in terms of battle impact, it becomes an ideal candidate for a strategic non-completion in the Legion of Frostborne rewards:

  • Continuous Skill Stone Acquisition: By intentionally not completing Stormeye, players can continue to purchase its skill stones, convert them into Cinders, and use those to acquire more impactful skills or other valuable items in the Triss shop.
  • Resource Management: This approach allows players to optimize their use of Cold Coins or Gems by continually accessing a resource exchange pathway, thus maximizing the efficiency of their in-game spending.
  • OBS: If you complete all skills available as KvK rewards, you WILL NOT BE ABLE TO EARN ANY REWARDS.

Conclusion

While Stormeye does not stand out for its combat effectiveness, its strategic value in resource management strategies should not be overlooked. Players are encouraged to evaluate their current roster and battle strategies to decide if investing beyond the minimal necessary level in Stormeye is beneficial. For many, keeping Stormeye as an open channel for resource conversion might prove more valuable than any damage it could potentially contribute on the battlefield.

description: Player Guide: Mastering Toxin Nova and Fire Nova in Infinity Kingdom
html:
Player Guide: Mastering Toxin Nova and Fire Nova in Infinity Kingdom

In the sprawling battlefield of Infinity Kingdom, the Tower of Knowledge skills Toxin Nova and Fire Nova often go unnoticed among the array of flashy and high-profile skills. However, these magic damage dealer skills are not only accessible to all players but also provide a surprisingly robust damage output that can enhance your strategic gameplay significantly.

Skill Overview

Toxin Nova and Fire Nova share the same fundamental mechanics, with the only distinction being the type of damage over time (DoT) effect they apply—Toxin Nova inflicts Poison, and Fire Nova inflicts Burn. These skills are described as follows:

  • Official Skill Description: “Every 6 seconds after battle starts, has a 50% chance of causing Magical Damage (175%) to 3 random enemy units and also inflicting a damage over time effect for 6 seconds dealing Magical Damage to the targets for 75% once every 3 seconds.”

Analyzing the Damage Output

Despite their simplicity, the damage efficiency of Toxin Nova and Fire Nova is quite notable. Here’s a breakdown:

  • Probability of Activation: Each skill has a 50% chance to trigger every 6 seconds.
  • Damage Calculation: Upon activation, these skills not only deal an immediate 175% magical damage but also add a DoT that totals 150% over 6 seconds (75% every 3 seconds).
  • Comparative DPS: This sums up to a whopping 325% damage per activation. Given the 50% trigger chance, the average DPS (Damage Per Second) contribution from these skills is approximately 81.25%.

This DPS is competitive, even surpassing several higher-tier skills like Stormeye (68.75% DPS), Spell Disintegration (62.5%), and Poison Thorn (55%). This demonstrates that both Toxin Nova and Fire Nova are not just filler skills; they are potent tools in their own right.

Strategic Deployment

Toxin Nova and Fire Nova are best utilized in teams that can capitalize on sustained damage throughout a fight. They are particularly effective in:

  • Magic-focused Teams: Complementing immortals with high magical output.
  • Control Teams: Pairing with control effects to maximize damage during enemy disable periods.
  • Synergy with Chase: Given that there are a lot of damage instances from both triggering effects and the damage over time effects, these skills pair well with Chase as the high number of damage instance will give you a good chance to land a critical hit quite frequently.

Note on Usage with Fire Dragon: Players using the Fire Dragon should opt for Toxin Nova to avoid overlapping Burn effects, which do not stack and might result in significantly reduced efficiency.

Acquisition and Utilization

Both skills are freely available and can be acquired without the need for special events or premium currency, making them accessible options for building out your fourth march or reinforcing your existing teams.

Conclusion

While Toxin Nova and Fire Nova might not carry the prestige of some higher-profile skills, their effectiveness in the right strategic setup cannot be understated. Their high potential DPS, coupled with the versatility in application, makes them worthy of consideration for any player looking to enhance their magical damage capabilities in Infinity Kingdom. Remember, the best arsenal is one that’s fully utilized—don’t overlook these gems hidden in plain sight.

Player Guide: Mastering the “Unyielding” Skill in Infinity Kingdom

“Unyielding” is a powerful Tower of Knowledge skill that has become available in Infinity Kingdom through the Triss event and the Triss shop (in exchange for Cinders). As a skill that enhances critical hit capabilities under specific conditions, it can be a game-changer in the right setups, particularly those centered around critical hits. This guide will delve into the mechanics of “Unyielding” and how to effectively integrate it into your battle strategies.

Skill Mechanics

Core Functionality

  • Critical Rate Boost: When your troops drop below 70% health, “Unyielding” increases your critical hit rate by 50%. This significant boost can dramatically increase your damage output in critical phases of a battle.
  • HP Recovery on Hit: Alongside the increase in critical rate, “Unyielding” also allows you to recover HP equivalent to 30% of the physical damage dealt whenever a critical hit lands.

This combination of enhanced critical hits and self-sustain makes “Unyielding” particularly effective in aggressive, damage-focused builds.

Strategic Implementation

Ideal Scenarios

  • Crit-Based Builds: “Unyielding” shines in builds that are heavily reliant on critical hits for damage. The skill’s activation at lower troop health thresholds synergizes well with strategies that engage in high-risk, high-reward combat scenarios.
  • Energy Burst Synergy: Pairing “Unyielding” with “Energy Burst” enhances the consistency of critical hits, further leveraging the burst damage potential of your immortals.

Optimal Use Case: Seondeok in a Fire Team

  • The Perfect Match: Seondeok, known for her potent burst damage capabilities, is the ideal candidate for “Unyielding”. Positioned in a fire-based team, which often eschews sustain for outright offensive power, Seondeok benefits immensely from the critical boosts provided by “Unyielding”.
  • Tactical Deployment: As fire teams generally experience a rapid decrease in troop health, Seondeok can activate “Unyielding” relatively early in combat, allowing her to unleash devastating critical hits that capitalize on her ultimate ability.
  • Maximizing Damage: Although Seondeok’s ultimate no longer triggers off itself, the enhanced critical rate from “Unyielding” ensures that each hit she delivers is maximally effective, potentially turning the tide of battle with swift, powerful strikes.

Building Around Unyielding

To maximize the effectiveness of “Unyielding”, consider the following tips:

  • Equip Critical Enhancing Artifacts: Supplement “Unyielding” with gear and other skills that boost critical damage or rate, ensuring that once “Unyielding” activates, every hit counts.
  • Complementary Skills: Pair “Unyielding” with other skills that either provide damage mitigation or further enhance damage output to make the most of the critical phase.

Conclusion

“Unyielding” is a potent skill that, when strategically deployed, can significantly alter the dynamics of your combat encounters in Infinity Kingdom. Ideal for critical hit-based builds and particularly effective with immortals like Seondeok in fire setups, it promises to deliver thrilling combat performances. Player Guide: Mastering the “Vitality Touch” Skill in Infinity Kingdom

“Vitality Touch” is a top-tier skill in Infinity Kingdom, renowned for its significant boost to healing and defensive capabilities in your immortal lineups. Perfect for sustain-focused strategies, this skill can be a game-changer in how you manage your troops during intense battles.

Overview of Vitality Touch

Skill Mechanics:

  • Activation: Automatically activates every 6 seconds after the battle begins.
  • Healing: Heals the allied unit that has lost the most troops by 120% of the Recovery Rate.
  • Defense Buff: Increases physical and magical defense of the healed unit by 10% for 18 seconds.

This potent combination not only helps in maintaining your troop’s health but also provides a rolling defensive buff that can cover multiple immortals over the duration of the battle, enhancing their survivability against both physical and magical attacks.

Strategic Implementation

Optimal Use Cases:

  • Sustain Setups: Vitality Touch shines in builds where prolonged combat is expected, such as Earth or Holy setups, where maintaining high troop health is crucial.
  • Shadow Sustain: Although traditionally less common, integrating Vitality Touch in shadow setups focused on sustain can provide unexpected durability, especially when combined with other defensive skills.
  • Hybrid Synergy: In hybrid teams, particularly those including Zenobia, pairing Vitality Touch with skills like “Purify” and “Wine and Dine” can create a resilient core that supports both offensive and defensive maneuvers effectively.

Choosing the Right Immortal: Since the skill’s healing effect is based on the Recovery Rate, which in turn depends on the immortal’s Aptitude Attribute, it’s important to select an immortal with a high Recovery Rate to maximize the healing effect. Healers or support immortals generally make the best carriers for this skill.

Acquisition Guide

How to Obtain Vitality Touch:

  • Triss Event: Vitality Touch can be purchased through the Triss shop using Cinders. Cinders can be accumulated by participating in various events like Legion of Frostborne or by selling unused skill stones.
  • Accessibility for Free Players: Free-to-play players have a pathway to this skill by accumulating rewards from events like Legion of Frostborne and converting other resources into Cinders, making it accessible without direct payment.

Tactical Considerations

  • Timing and Placement: Given the skill activates every 6 seconds, placement in your lineup is crucial. It should ideally be placed on immortals who are likely to sustain significant damage early in the battle to maximize its defensive utility.
  • Buff Stacking: Managing the defensive buffs to overlap efficiently can create windows of high resilience against incoming damage, pivotal in turning the tides during critical moments of a fight.

Conclusion

Mastering the “Weakening Curse” Skill in Infinity Kingdom

The “Weakening Curse” is a formidable premium skill in the Tower of Knowledge (ToK) for the game Infinity Kingdom, specifically tailored for Defense immortals. Unlockable at ToK level 51, this skill can be acquired during the Triss Blessing Event, offering a strategic advantage on the battlefield by significantly reducing the damage output of your adversaries.

Concept and Mechanism

The essence of “Weakening Curse” lies in its ability to diminish the damage dealt by enemy forces by a staggering 70%. This effect is instant from the commencement of battle and persists on every opponent until they either cast their ultimate skill or 45 seconds elapse. Intriguingly, the skill is engineered to counter dominant figures like Alexander and Hannibal. Due to their Exclusive Artifact converting their ultimate skill into a passive ability, they’re perpetually affected by the curse, making them less threatening over the duration.

It’s noteworthy that the damage reduction specifically targets trigger and auto-attack damage, leaving the first use of the ultimate skill unaffected. This nuance makes “Weakening Curse” particularly effective against builds focusing on burst damage, providing a tactical edge in sustaining your forces.

Strategic Combinations

Enhancing the efficacy of “Weakening Curse” involves tactics to delay the enemy’s first ultimate skill activation. Skills such as “No Escape” and “Energy Suppression” (not to be used simultaneously) are excellent companions to “Weakening Curse,” extending the duration of damage mitigation and compounding your defensive strategy.

Counter Tactics

Despite its potency, the “Weakening Curse” is not without its vulnerabilities. Its effects can be neutralized by skills like “Purification” or by immortals such as Athena and Fu Fei, who possess dispelling capabilities. When strategizing, it’s crucial to consider these counters and, if possible, select opponents whose compositions are susceptible to your march that incorporates “Weakening Curse” to maximize its benefits.

Conclusion

“Weakening Curse” stands out as a skill of strategic depth, thoughtfully restricted to Defense immortals to maintain balance within Infinity Kingdom. Its introduction into your arsenal can significantly deter the offensive capabilities of your adversaries, making it a cornerstone for defense-oriented strategies. With careful planning and execution, “Weakening Curse” can be the linchpin in turning the tides of battle in your favor, underscoring the importance of tactical skill deployment and synergy in Infinity Kingdom’s dynamic combat system.

Player Guide: Mastering Weakness Protection in Infinity Kingdom

Weakness Protection is a unique Tower of Knowledge skill in Infinity Kingdom, specifically designed to bolster the defenses of your immortals at the onset of battle. This guide will delve into the nuances of utilizing Weakness Protection effectively, ensuring your frontline can withstand initial bursts of enemy attacks.

Skill Mechanics

Weakness Protection dramatically reduces both physical and magical damage received by the allied units with the lowest defenses:

  • Effect: Reduces physical and magical damage received by 60%.
  • Duration: Effective for the first 12 seconds of battle.
  • Target: Applied to the allied unit with the lowest physical defense and the one with the lowest magical defense.

The grace period of 12 seconds is pivotal; this skill is designed to provide a significant, albeit temporary, defensive boost against early heavy hitters, such as burst fire setups or hybrid attacks. This makes it an excellent choice for countering teams that aim to overwhelm their opponents right from the start.

Strategic Implementation

Choosing the Right Immortal: Weakness Protection is most beneficial on support immortals who aren’t primarily healers. This includes:

  • Supporters: Immortals like Mathilda, Tomyris, or Cyrus benefit from this skill as it enhances their survivability without compromising the effectiveness of their support abilities.
  • Non-Healer Supports: The skill is particularly effective on supports that do not rely heavily on healing, as they can spare the skill slot without sacrificing essential healing or damage capabilities.

When to Use:

  • Against Burst Damage: Ideal in battles against teams known for their strong initial attacks. It provides your team a crucial window to withstand the initial onslaught and stabilize.
  • Complementary Strategies: This skill pairs well with defensive setups but should be used cautiously with control-heavy strategies like No Escape or Weakening Curse, as its benefits might overlap or be underutilized if the enemy is already significantly debilitated early on.

Acquisition of Weakness Protection

Originally available through the Triss event, Weakness Protection had been out of reach for many players due to event rotations and updates. However, it has recently been reintroduced through the 5-day bundles:

  • Availability: Can now be obtained from 5-day bundles in the game.
  • Investment Required: Players need to participate in at least two rounds of these bundles to collect the 60 skill stones required for maximizing the skill.

Practical Tips

  • Build Synergy: Integrate this skill into a balanced team setup where its protective benefits can be maximized without redundancy. Avoid stacking too many defensive or control skills that might diminish its value. For instance, No Escape and Weakening Curse will render the enemy unable to do.. well anything.. so you would get very little value from the massive defense for 12 seconds.
  • Event Participation: Keep an eye on bundle events to complete your skill stone collection, ensuring you can fully upgrade Weakness Protection for optimal effectiveness.

Conclusion

Weakness Protection offers a powerful defensive tool for the critical opening moments of combat in Infinity Kingdom. When used judiciously, it can turn the tide of battle by protecting your most vulnerable immortals from early elimination. By understanding the strategic contexts in which this skill excels, you can enhance your team’s resilience and maintain a competitive edge in your battlefield encounters.

Mastering the “Wind Rage” Skill in Infinity Kingdom

“Wind Rage” stands as one of the most dynamic and potentially game-changing skills within the Infinity Kingdom, obtainable exclusively via the Legion of Frostborne event. This skill’s official description states: “Every normal attack will have a 55% chance to immediately trigger an additional normal attack.” The essence of “Wind Rage” lies in its ability to significantly amplify the offensive capabilities of your immortals, making it a pivotal skill in crafting a dominating force on the battlefield.

The Power of “Wind Rage”

The skill’s potency is not to be underestimated. It essentially offers a 55% chance for immortals to double their attack output on every normal attack. This creates a cascade of additional benefits, especially when combined with other Tower of Knowledge skills that activate on normal attacks, such as Combo, Cleave, and Heavenly Thunder. The skill is especially valuable in physical damage dealer setups but is versatile enough to augment the capabilities of mages and support immortals through increased energy regeneration.

Strategic Synergy

“Wind Rage” requires thoughtful pairing with other skills to unlock its full potential. Its ability to increase the frequency of normal attacks makes it a cornerstone for combinations that rely on triggering effects from normal attacks.

For instance use it in synergy with:

  • Coupled with Combo and Cleave, it escalates physical damage output by ensuring more frequent triggers of these damage-enhancing skills.
  • When used alongside Heavenly Thunder, it increases the chance of applying this skill’s effects, further augmenting your army’s damage potential.
  • Adrenaline Rush gains substantial value from “Wind Rage” in magic-focused or control setups, where rapid energy regeneration is crucial.

Recommended Immortals for “Wind Rage”

Physical Damage Dealers

  • Alexander and Hannibal Barca emerge as top contenders for “Wind Rage,” thanks to their high attack speed and physical damage output. Their ability to benefit from additional normal attacks makes them even more formidable in combat.

Mages and Supports

  • Himiko and Loki are prime candidates among mages and control immortals. Their powerful control abilities, when activated more frequently due to increased energy regeneration from “Wind Rage,” can decisively tilt battles in your favor.
  • Theodora and Charles can leverage “Wind Rage” in specialized support setups that require rapid energy regeneration for shield deployment or debuff cleansing.

Obtaining “Wind Rage”

Currently exclusive to the Legion of Frostborne event, there’s anticipation that “Wind Rage” may become available through a 5-day bundle in the near future. This would offer players an accelerated path to acquiring and leveraging this potent skill.

Utilizing “Wind Rage” to Its Full Potential

To maximize the effectiveness of “Wind Rage,” consider the following:

  • Skill Synergy: Plan your Immortal’s skill set to ensure “Wind Rage” complements the overall strategy, focusing on maximizing normal attack triggers.
  • Team Composition: Align your team composition to support the enhanced capabilities “Wind Rage” offers, ensuring you have immortals that can capitalize on increased attack frequency and energy regeneration.
  • Battle Strategy: Adjust your battle strategies to exploit the rapid attack and skill activation rates “Wind Rage” facilitates, targeting enemy weaknesses with precision and efficiency.

Conclusion

“Wind Rage” is an incredibly powerful skill in Infinity Kingdom, offering the potential to significantly enhance your combat effectiveness through increased attack frequency. Its value is amplified when strategically paired with other skills and immortals, making it a must-have for players looking to dominate both PvP and PvE battles. Keep an eye on events like Legion of Frostborne (and potentially future bundles) to secure this game-changing skill for your arsenal.

title: Wine and Dine – a truely delicious passive
description: 🍷🍖 Wine and Dine – The Support Skill That Turns Healing Into Damage
html:
🍷🍖 Wine and Dine – The Support Skill That Turns Healing Into Damage

The ever-evolving world of Infinity Kingdom introduces a new and formidable passive skill within the Tower of Knowledge called “Wine and Dine.” With the recent 2.6 update, this skill has swiftly captured the attention of seasoned players and promises to become an essential addition to many prevailing meta setups. In this article, we delve into the mechanics, significance, and strategic applications of the powerful new passive known as “Wine and Dine.”

The Tower of Knowledge is full of hidden gems, but few skills have made as much noise as Wine and Dine. Originally introduced in patch 2.6, this passive skill quickly became a favorite for support-focused lineups. On paper, it’s simple: every time an Immortal heals an ally, there’s a chance to grant them a powerful damage buff. But in practice, Wine and Dine offers much more depth — and its mechanics have caused plenty of confusion among players.

In this guide, we’ll break down exactly how it works, clear up misconceptions, and explain how to maximize its power in your teams.

🛡️ What Does Wine and Dine Do?

  • Effect: When an Immortal restores HP, there’s a 50% chance to grant the healed target a +30% Damage Dealt buff.
  • Trigger Condition: Each instance of healing counts separately.
  • Duration: Short buff duration (varies slightly based on skill level).

This means that every single tick of healing (not just the cast) has a 50% chance to activate the buff.

💡 Example:

  • Zenobia’s HoT (heal over time) ticks multiple times. Each tick gives every healed ally an independent 50% chance to receive Wine and Dine.
  • In practice, Zenobia spreads the buff reliably because of her constant HoTs.

Synergy with Holy, Earth, and Hybrid Compositions: Holy, earth, and hybrid compositions often rely on healers to sustain their Immortals on the battlefield. With Wine and Dine in play, healers gain an additional layer of significance as they become instrumental in not only restoring health but also enhancing the damage potential of their allies. This skill synergizes exceptionally well with these compositions, elevating their effectiveness and granting them a competitive edge in battles.

⚔️ Why It’s a Game-Changer

1. Healing = Damage Boost

Normally, healers exist just to keep allies alive. With Wine and Dine, they also become offensive enablers, making your carries hit harder whenever they get topped up.

2. Synergy With HoT Healers

  • Zenobia is the perfect example: her ultimate heals everyone over time, giving each ally multiple rolls to proc Wine and Dine.
  • Other healers with healing (Theodora’s, Fu Fei etc.) also gain huge value.
  • Activates off of healing skills such as Purification, Vitality Touch. Especially Purification is very powerful with Wine and Dine because of the high frequency of healing instances (in cases where no debuffs can be removed ofc).

3. Great for Sustained Fights

Unlike burst buffs (like Battle Stance), Wine and Dine keeps re-triggering throughout prolonged battles, making it ideal for stall or ramp setups.

Recommendation: Incredible skill for Hybrid, where you almost always have HoTs running on Alexander and Hannibal, getting them a 30% damage buff is amazing!

❌ Clearing Up Misconceptions

Because of its vague description, players often misunderstand Wine and Dine. Let’s set the record straight:

  • Does it buff the healer or the allies?
    → The buff applies to the healed target, not just the healer.
  • Does one heal-cast buff everyone?
    → No. Each target healed gets their own 50% chance to gain the buff.
  • Do healing auras like Shelter or Berserk trigger it?
    → Technically yes, they can trigger Wine and Dine.
    → However, the buff only applies to the healer themselves (e.g. Zenobia), not to the allies healed by those auras. This limits their usefulness for Wine and Dine synergy.

🌍 Best Setups for Wine and Dine

  • Holy Teams: Already healer-heavy; turns sustain into burst damage.
  • Earth Comps: Zenobia + tanks + DPS becomes even harder to crack.
  • Hybrid Teams: Works wonders in comps where healing uptime is high, letting both magical and physical carries benefit.

🏆 Final Thoughts

Wine and Dine is one of the most impactful support skills in Infinity Kingdom because it turns sustain into offense. With healers like Zenobia, every HoT tick becomes a chance to unleash 30% more damage, making her not just a lifesaver but also a damage amplifier.

It’s not perfect — aura-based heals like Shelter and Berserk don’t spread the buff as widely as players hope — but in the right hands, Wine and Dine is a must-have passive for late-game Conquest and beyond.

👉 If you’re building around healers, especially HoT-based ones, this is a skill you must pick up.

description: Welcome, fellow Infinity Kingdom players! This guide focuses on Tower of Knowledge (ToK) skills from levels 0 to 20. html:
Welcome, fellow Infinity Kingdom players! This guide focuses on Tower of Knowledge (ToK) skills from levels 0 to 20. During the early preparation stage, it’s easy to overspend purple crystals on skills that you’ll later need to replace. Rebirthing skills costs you 20% of the original crystal investment, so it’s crucial to choose wisely and avoid wasting precious resources. I’ll share which skills I recommend upgrading, which to skip, and how to keep your builds efficient while still enjoying a power boost in these early levels.

Why Skill Selection Matters at Levels 0–20

In the very first stages of the game, you need to strike a balance between grabbing skills that offer immediate benefits versus saving your purple crystals for high-tier skills you’ll unlock later.

Many of the skills available at these lower levels either:

  1. Remain decently strong throughout the early game (and can later be moved to a secondary team).
  2. Provide short-term power but will eventually require rebirthing (and thus waste crystals).

You want to avoid the second scenario whenever possible. Let’s take a closer look at the major skill unlocks at levels 1, 5, 10, 15, and 20.

Level 1: Onslaught and Wisdom

Right from the start, you gain access to Onslaught (green) and Wisdom (green). Both are extremely cheap to acquire and upgrade:

  • Onslaught boosts your physical damage output, making it ideal for early-game physical attackers such as Alexander.
  • Wisdom boosts magic damage, benefiting your magic-based Immortals. If you use Medb (powerful early immortal) Wisdom is quite strong.

They’re not as strong as higher-level skills like Anger (lvl 27) or Concentration (lvl 24), but they still pack enough punch to remain useful well into mid-game. Once you outgrow them on your main march, you can always move them to your second or third team, ensuring you haven’t wasted your crystals.

Level 5: Hold Fast, Fortify, and Thump

At level 5, three more skills appear: Hold Fast (green), Fortify (green), and Thump (green).

  • Hold Fast provides a physical defense buff, which can help your frontline survive longer, especially early on. Normal attack damage is significant in the first stages of the game, so a cheap defensive buff can go a long way. You can move it to a backup team or rebirth it later if you no longer need it.
  • Fortify and Thump are generally less appealing. They don’t offer enough impact to justify spending purple crystals, so it’s best to skip these if you can.

Level 10: Meteor and Instigation

Upon reaching level 10, you unlock Meteor (blue) and Instigation (blue).

  • Meteor can be useful for dealing extra magic damage against bosses if you’re using a magic-based Immortal. Outside of that niche, it’s not particularly impressive, so most players can skip it.
  • Instigation was once considered powerful for control-focused teams, but the pace of the game has accelerated, reducing its effectiveness. It’s not a terrible choice if you really want extra control, but it’s generally not worth investing a lot of crystals.

Level 15: Support, Grace, and Silence

Level 15 adds Support (blue), Grace (blue), and Silence (blue) to your options.

  • Support and Grace offer healing or regen capabilities, often popular in Earth-based teams. However, with Wounds becoming more common in the current meta, these skills lose much of their effectiveness. They can still be useful for PvE, but unless you have a specific plan, it’s safer to save your crystals for better skills.
  • Silence stands out as a powerful option because it prevents enemies from regaining energy, effectively shutting down their ultimates. It also deals decent damage. This is one of the best early mid-tier control skills you can pick up, and it can remain relevant on your secondary teams even after you unlock higher-level skills.

Level 20: Stray Arrow and Combo

Finally, at level 20, you gain Stray Arrow (blue) and Combo (blue).

  • Stray Arrow focuses on single-target physical damage at a 55% trigger chance. It can be handy if you need more boss damage, but it’s still on the weaker side in most PvP scenarios. If your purple crystals are in short supply, this skill is usually best skipped.
  • Combo is an excellent pick for any frontline fighter who relies on normal attacks (like Alexander or Hannibal Barca in Earth, Wind, or hybrid lineups). It scales well and remains competitive for a long time. Even after you move your main march to stronger ToK skills, Combo can find a new home on a secondary lineup.

Personal Recommendations and Opinions

You’ll unlock higher-level (and generally more potent) skills pretty quickly in today’s fast-paced environment. Therefore, investing heavily in weaker or situational early skills can cost you crystals later. Here’s a general tier list for levels 0–20 based on overall usefulness and longevity:

  • S-Tier: Silence, Combo, Onslaught
    These are the most valuable to acquire and upgrade, and they can remain useful even into the mid-game.
  • A-Tier: Wisdom, Hold Fast
    Solid picks if you need a cheap magic buff (Wisdom) or defensive support (Hold Fast). They’re easy to rebirth or move to secondary lineups.
  • B-Tier: Instigation
    Situational but can be used in a hyper-control setup. Otherwise, you can skip it.
  • C-Tier: Meteor, Stray Arrow
    Useful in niche scenarios (boss damage), but mostly overshadowed by better options.
  • F-Tier: Grace, Support, Fortify, Thump
    These have minimal utility, and you’ll likely regret spending crystals on them once you progress further.

Your main goal is to avoid pouring resources into skills that will quickly become obsolete. Focus on those with lasting impact, and you’ll have a smoother path when transitioning to higher-level skills that truly define endgame strategies.

Summary

Navigating the early levels of the Tower of Knowledge (0–20) can be tricky. You need enough power to compete in Preparation servers without wasting crystals on skills you’ll just rebirth later. Silence, Combo, and Onslaught shine as top choices thanks to their balance of cost-effectiveness and long-term potential. Meanwhile, a few others like Wisdom and Hold Fast can be decent choices as well for a shorter period of time.

Everything else is largely optional or too niche to be worth your purple crystals. By keeping your spending smart, you’ll have plenty left to invest in the powerful late-game ToK skills that truly make a difference. Use this guide to plan your early ToK path, stay efficient, and lay the groundwork for a formidable army in Infinity Kingdom!

description: Here is the completed Tower of Knowledge Tier List Guide (Levels 21-30) for Infinity Kingdom!
html:
Here is the completed Tower of Knowledge Tier List Guide (Levels 21-30) for Infinity Kingdom!

Welcome, fellow Infinity Kingdom players! This guide focuses on Tower of Knowledge (ToK) skills from levels 21 to 30. During the early preparation stage, it’s easy to overspend purple crystals on skills that you’ll later need to replace. Rebirthing skills costs you 20% of the original crystal investment, so it’s crucial to choose wisely and avoid wasting precious resources. I’ll share which skills I recommend upgrading, which to skip, and how to keep your builds efficient while still enjoying a power boost in these early levels.

As you progress through levels 21-30 in the Tower of Knowledge (ToK), you unlock some of the most impactful skills in Infinity Kingdom. These abilities shape PvE boss fights, PvP battles, and hybrid team compositions.

This guide will help new and experienced players decide which skills to invest in, and which to avoid to maximize their purple crystal efficiency.

Level 22 Unlocks

Root

  • Effect: Deals single-target damage and applies a Root effect to immobilize enemies.
  • Analysis: Great for PvE boss fights due to its consistent single-target damage. However, not very useful in PvP, where mobility and cleanse effects diminish its value.
  • Tier: B (Good for PvE, weak in PvP)

Precision

  • Effect: Increases accuracy by 15%.
  • Analysis: Accuracy is rarely an issue, making this skill pointless in most scenarios.
  • Tier: D (Avoid)

Penance

  • Effect: Reflects a small portion of damage back at the attacker.
  • Analysis: The reflected damage is minimal, making this a waste of resources.
  • Tier: D (Avoid)

Level 24 Unlocks

Rage

  • Effect: Increases critical hit rate.
  • Analysis: Very strong if you have a crit-based team, especially in fire teams using Chase. However, it will eventually be replaced by better skills.
  • Tier: A (Great early on, but will be dropped later)

Concentration

  • Effect: Increases magic damage by 30%.
  • Analysis: One of the best skills for mages, as raw damage scaling is incredibly powerful. A core skill for any magic-based Immortal.
  • Tier: S (Must-have for magic teams)

Level 25 Unlocks

Agile

  • Effect: Increases dodge rate.
  • Analysis: Dodge rate is unreliable, and the impact is minimal. Not worth the investment.
  • Tier: D (Avoid)

Retaliate

  • Effect: 30% chance to counterattack when hit by a normal attack.
  • Analysis: Can be useful in niche scenarios, such as a Peter frontline against hybrid teams. However, its uses are too situational to justify investing in.
  • Tier: C (Situational)

Chase

  • Effect: Allows follow-up extra attacks.
  • Analysis: Fantastic early game skill, especially when paired with crit-based teams. It eventually falls off, but remains a strong investment for most of the game.
  • Tier: A (Strong, but not permanent)

Level 26 Unlocks

Magic Shield

  • Effect: Reduces magic damage taken.
  • Analysis: Magic damage isn’t a big enough threat to justify using a skill slot for this.
  • Tier: C (Not useful in most situations)

Chaotic Blade

  • Effect: Increases normal attack damage with a chance for bonus damage.
  • Analysis: Very strong in the early game, especially for attack-speed-based Immortals. Over time, it gets outclassed but remains great for secondary teams.
  • Tier: A (Good early, still useful later)

Level 27 Unlocks

Physical Shield

  • Effect: Reduces physical damage taken.
  • Analysis: Unlike Magic Shield, this skill is actually useful because most normal attacks and ultimates are physical.
  • Tier: A (Good defensive skill)

Anger

  • Effect: Increases physical damage by 30%.
  • Analysis: A top-tier skill for physical damage dealers like Alexander, Hannibal, and Attila.
  • Tier: S (Essential for physical teams)

Absorb

  • Effect: Provides lifesteal (leeching damage for healing).
  • Analysis: On certain builds, like Duel Master Alexander, this skill can provide crazy sustain. However, not useful for most teams.
  • Tier: C (Situational)

Level 28 Unlocks

Heavenly Thunder

  • Effect: Deals magic damage based on attack speed.
  • Analysis: Strong in hybrid teams where attack speed is high. Works well in specific hybrid builds but not a general-use skill.
  • Tier: B (Good in specific setups)

Fighting Master

  • Effect: Grants control immunity.
  • Analysis: One of the best PvP skills in the game. Being immune to crowd control is game-changing in high-level fights.
  • Tier: S (Must-have for PvP)

Level 29 Unlocks

After-Image

  • Effect: Boosts dodge rate.
  • Analysis: Not great on its own, but when paired with Misleading (unlocked later), it can create a dodge-focused team.
  • Tier: B (Mediocre alone, strong with Misleading)

Toxin Nova

  • Effect: Deals poison damage over time.
  • Analysis: A strong early-to-mid game skill, but will eventually be replaced by better abilities.
  • Tier: A (Good, but temporary)

Defensive Blessing

  • Effect: Provides flat defense boosts.
  • Analysis: Amazing for any team, as flat defense reduction is always useful. Works well even in late-game setups.
  • Tier: A (Highly effective)

Level 30 Unlocks

Adrenaline Rush

  • Effect: Increases energy regen speed.
  • Analysis: Absolutely broken on Immortals who rely on ultimates, like Richard, Hippolyta, Charles, and Attila.
  • Tier: S (Game-changing for certain Immortals)

Garrote

  • Effect: Increases bleed damage.
  • Analysis: Good for physical DoT setups. Works similarly to Chaotic Blade.
  • Tier: A (Good, but not core)

Fire Nova

  • Effect: Deals AoE magic damage.
  • Analysis: Solid for magic teams, but eventually replaced by stronger skills like Annihilation. Still great for second and third teams.
  • Tier: A (Strong early, good later)

Iron Will

  • Effect: Provides resistance to magic damage.
  • Analysis: Just like Magic Shield, this is not necessary.
  • Tier: D (Avoid)

Final Tier List Summary

S-Tier (Must-Have Skills)

✔ Concentration (Magic Teams)
✔ Anger (Physical Teams)
✔ Fighting Master (PvP Control Immunity)
✔ Adrenaline Rush (Energy Regen)

A-Tier (Strong & Useful Skills)

✔ Chase
✔ Chaotic Blade
✔ Defensive Blessing
✔ Fire Nova
✔ Garrote

B-Tier (Situational but Good)

✔ Root (PvE Only)
✔ After-Image (Only with Misleading)

C-Tier (Rarely Useful)

✔ Absorb
✔ Magic Shield
✔ Heavenly Thunder

D-Tier (Avoid These Skills)

❌ Precision, Penance, Agile, Iron Will

This guide ensures you invest your purple crystals wisely while maximizing the power of your Immortals! 🚀

title: Tower of Knowledge tier list for level 31-35
description: ToK Tier List and Skill Recommendations (Levels 31-35)
html:
ToK Tier List and Skill Recommendations (Levels 31-35)

As you progress through Infinity Kingdom, choosing the right Tower of Knowledge (ToK) skills is crucial. Some skills will carry you well into the late game, while others serve as temporary but efficient choices for your primary or secondary teams. The goal of this guide is to help you select strong skills that you won’t need to rebirth later, ensuring that you don’t waste precious purple crystals melting skills unnecessarily.

This tier list covers the Level 31-35 skill unlocks, a pivotal stage where some of the game’s most powerful skills become available. These skills will define your strategy for a long time, so making the right choices now is essential for efficiency, longevity, and optimal gameplay progression.

Level 31 Unlocks

Will of Angels – F-Tier

This skill is a complete no-go. Even against wound-based setups, the healing provided is minimal. By level 31, wound-heavy enemies are common, and this skill won’t offer meaningful protection. Avoid it entirely.

Life-Link – B-Tier

A decent skill with some PvP utility. While it won’t last long in your main lineup, it finds continued value in secondary or third teams. Additionally, it’s essential for the Spider Boss setup when paired with Absolute Defense.

Cleave – S-Tier

A top-tier skill for physical damage dealers. Works exceptionally well on Alexander or Hannibal due to their high attack speed and high physical damage output. More attack speed = more activations = more damage, making Cleave a must-have for physical teams.

Level 32 Unlocks

Blessing of War – A-Tier

A strong skill for both PvE and PvP. It won’t last into late game, but you can get huge value in the midgame. Particularly useful in an Earth-Wind Hybrid setup, where it plays a key role in boosting effectiveness.

Demon Body – F-Tier

A completely useless skill. There is no scenario where this skill provides real value. Avoid it.

Level 33 Unlocks

Sacrifice – B/C-Tier

A situational skill that can work on specific support immortals like Dido or Cyrus. It provides an energy boost and a damage increase for allies, but since it’s not guaranteed, it’s an unreliable option. Not a must-have, but can be decent in niche setups.

Duel Master – S-Tier

One of the best skills in the game. It offers wounds immunity, which is essential for immortals that rely on lifesteal or healing. Must-have for:

  • Alexander in Hybrid teams
  • Tutankhamun in Shadow teams against Hybrid or Lightning teams
  • Overall strong damage modifier as well

Berserk – B-Tier

A powerful aura, but only effective in specific builds. If you’re running a Hybrid team, it’s a must-have. It provides good value in your main before transitioning to a secondary hybrid team.

Level 34 Unlocks

Rage Blessing – A-Tier

A very strong regeneration skill, providing sustained healing over time. While it will eventually be replaced (especially when mass silence effects become prevalent), it remains effective well into late seasons.

Resist – B-Tier

A solid magic defense skill, but not a top-tier choice. Blessing of Defense is often the preferred alternative due to its wider defensive coverage. Works well in a secondary team, providing value while progressing.

Note: At level 34, players unlock access to Wisdom Well skill-stone skills, which are locked behind a paywall. These will be covered in a separate guide, as this guide focuses on general skill recommendations accessible to all players.

Level 35 Unlocks

Absolute Defense – A-Tier

A strong defensive skill, particularly effective in backline assist setups. While not as dominant in the current meta due to fast-paced power creep, it still provides good value:

  • Effective once you unlock Tier 5 troops.
  • Essential for the Spider Boss setup.
  • Can be used effectively in PvP, particularly in support-based defensive teams.

Malice – A-Tier

An excellent early-to-midgame aura, reducing critical damage received. Crit-based builds are common in early game and Season 1, making Malice a great defensive option. However, its value declines as dragon specializations unlock more resilience (around Season 2).

Oaken Guard – S-Tier

One of the best physical defense skills in the game. An absolute must-have against any physical damage setup:

  • Essential in almost all compositions except Duel Mage builds.
  • Remains viable well into Conquest servers.
  • Will stay in your main team for a long time.

Final Thoughts

Choosing the right ToK skills between levels 31-35 will significantly impact your progression efficiency and long-term resource management. The best skills are those that carry you well into late game or transition smoothly into secondary teams, ensuring that you do not waste purple crystals rebirthing skills.

Key Takeaways:

  • Top-Tier (S-Tier) Skills:
    • Cleave (Physical Damage Dealers)
    • Duel Master (Hybrid & Shadow Teams)
    • Oaken Guard (Physical Defense)
  • Strong (A-Tier) Skills:
    • Blessing of War (Strong early game, later Hybrid Compositions)
    • Rage Blessing (Regen-based setups)
    • Absolute Defense (Defensive Assist Setups & bosses)
    • Malice (Anti-Crit Defense, Early Game)
  • Situational (B-Tier) Skills:
    • Life-Link (PvP, Spider Boss Setup)
    • Berserk (Hybrid Teams)
    • Sacrifice (Specific Support Immortals)
    • Resist (Magic Defense, Secondary Teams)
  • Avoid (F-Tier) Skills:
    • Will of Angels (Weak Healing)
    • Demon Body (No Competitive Use)

By planning your skill selection wisely, you will optimize growth, avoid wasting resources, and maximize your efficiency in both PvE and PvP. Stay strategic, and your immortals will remain competitive well into the late game.
